Implementation of Quantum Image Processing Techniques Using the Chan-Vese Segmentation Algorithm to Convert Bits to Qubits to Enhance The Storage Capacity of the Pixels to Achieve Optimal Output to Identify the Paddy Leaf Diseases

Dr. A. Premo Kirubakaran4

E-mail: apkirubakaran@lincoln.edu.my; unjanai@gmail.com; midhun.research@gmail.com

DOI: 10.1201/9781003430452-5

Abstract

Malnutrition is a concern in the current situation. This occurs due to issues in food security, which should be concentrated on to eradicate poverty. Though many techniques are evolving deep learning and machine learning that help the agriculture process to get a better yield, quantum computing is a trial run to test its achievability in increasing crop production. It is believed that quantum computing will help to resolve world hunger. The whirling qubits will help solve the problems in the crop production world. Can quantum computing end the difficulties faced in crop yield? if so, how? The other reason for writing this article is the urgency to implement quantum computing in agriculture. Quantum computing is the data processing of the future. In the world of agriculture, artificial intelligence with image processing is quite important. With colossal speedups and growth in the power savings of quantum computers and as the other research field is moving and focusing on the implementation of quantum computing, the idea of shifting quantum technique toward agriculture emerged. The qubit representation of bits in quantum computers as "0" and "1" simultaneously makes it different from classical computers where the bits are represented either as "0" or "1.” The conversion of qubits to bits will be applied through the qubit conversion method, to have more valid bit spacing for real-time evaluation and storing purposes.

Keywords: Quantum Computing, Yield, QiSkit, Convolution

Introduction

The word hunger can be eradicated with more food production. This is possible by identifying the diseases that occur in a plant. Identification at an early stage and spraying the correct pesticide will protect the crop thus helping to increase the yield. Quantum computing is chosen to get a faster result in identifying the diseases in a crop. A programming sequence is incorporated that will help to take all the superpositions (Gandhi and McGinnity, 2013) of all the prior computations. Acquiring superpositions (Gandhi and McGinnity, 2013) will help solve mathematical problems much faster, where the factorization of large numbers is made easy. A question arises of how quantum computing will end hunger-definitely don’t know the right answer but the first step taken with quantum for agriculture will lead us to find a solution.

Perhaps the way fertilizers are used may involve the process of eradicating hunger, the focus lies in finding the disease that occurs in the leaf of a plant, and quantum computing methods with image processing techniques are used for identifying and analyzing the diseases that occur in the leaf of a plant.

Literature Survey

The concept of Human action recognition using graph matching was briefed by Abdulmunem et al. (2019), Quantum theoretical approach to image processing techniques is stated by Abura’ed et al. (2017). To understand machine learning in quantum world was briefed by E. Aimeur, G. Brassad, S. Gamba. Quantum classifier and quantum kernel by C. Blank, D.

Park, J. Rhee. Plant image recognition by A. P. Bhardwaj, M. Kaur where the techniques of converting bits to qubits were briefed.

Methodology

Images may be classified using classifiers, and quantum-based classifiers are becoming more popular in the field of image representation. This study uses a quantum classifier (Abura’ed et al., 2017) to apply a computer vision system for identifying diseased paddy leaves to a quantum computer. As they are separated into two groups, single and clusters, paddy leaf photos of 10 different varieties are acquired for classification, and quantum classification techniques are employed to identify them. Using the Fourier transform (QFT-QED) and Hadamard Gates, the images are processed as pixels, and these pixels are then converted to qubit states. The profile and structural features are extracted with the use of ID convolution and CNOT gates (Controlled Not). The leaf with the highest probability of being the closest match is located using a quantum nearest search classifier.

How to convert the images to pixels

The leaf-processed digital camera image provides the necessary pixels for finding basic elements.

The basic R, G, B, and A (Red, Green, Blue, and Alpha) (Chakraborty et al., 2020) values are used in Python to extract the values from each pixel, which makes up each image. The collection of R, G, B, and A values is known as the RGBA (Abura’ed et al., 2017) color space. Images in all file formats, including gif, bmp, png, and jpg, can be processed using several modules of the Python Imaging Library (PIL). Numerous functions in the library make it simpler to access, extract data from, change the characteristics of, add, and remove photos. Windows should be used with PIL, an integrated library that is pre-installed in Ubuntu.

Classical bits into Qubits

Generally, a bit is either 0 or 1 (Abura’ed et al., 2017) for a conventional bit, whereas a quantum bit, or qubit, is the superposition of 0 and 1. (Superposition: the placement of one thing above or on top of another). A single qubit can simultaneously store two classical values. As a result, both values go through all of the processes necessary to use a qubit. Qubits, therefore, contain (Aímeur, 2006) more information than traditional bits.

Two bits do have the following values: 0, 0, 1, 0, 1, and 1. According to the pattern, 1 qubit takes the values of 2 bits, and 2 qubits can take the values of 4 bits. In addition, 2 qubits (Amin and Khan, 2013) take the values concurrently. Therefore, 2n can be represented by n qubits.

Fourier Transform

The Fourier transform (Du et al., 2007) represents an image as the sum of complex exponentials with different magnitudes, frequencies, and phases. Many image processing applications, such as enhancement, analysis, restoration, and compression, rely heavily on the Fourier transform.

In processing pixelated images, where the high spatial frequency edges of pixels can be easily removed with a 2D Fourier transform, the Fourier transform is used to interpolate functions (Cai et al., 2014) and to smooth signals.

The Fourier Transform (Du et al., 2007) is used in signal processing, signal analysis, image processing, filtering, as well as the calculation of differential equations. In this study, leaf images are converted using the Fourier transform to generate accurate qubits that enable a more accurate evaluation of the image. FT image processing is therefore used.

In this case, the Hadamard (Gandhi and McGinnity, 2013) remodel refers to the Fourier transform is Hadamard (Gandhi and McGinnity, 2013) remodel is what the Fourier transform is in this case, and since it’s carried out using a Hadamard Gate, it’s also known as the Hadamard remodel. This is achieved by concurrently applying a Hadamard gate to each of the n qubits. Both types of the Fourier transform are utilized in Shor’s set of rules (an initial Hadamard rework in addition to QFT)

Hadamard gates

H gates or Hadamard gates are the most frequently used gates to convert the qubit from a clustering state to a uniform superposed state. Using an H gate an image can be rotated from 90 to 180 degrees, this is essential to view the image for clear results. Images that are captured and converted are viewed for leaves with defects. So to visualize the leaf image H gate is implemented whenever Fourier transforms are used.

2. Convolution

That is a simple mathematical operation this is fundamental to many commonplace picture-processing operators. It typically multiplies two arrays of numbers with exclusive sizes however the equal dimensionality produces a third array of numbers of the same dimensionality to evaluate the defective element in the leaf image that has been given as input for processing.

In this research work, 2D convolutions have been implemented that help to find out the blurring, sharpening, and edge detection using general image processing filters. The principle behind this is to use a kernel and iterate it through an input image to get an output image. Every bit that is generated is processed to get an output that is later passed through CNOT gates to encode the bit.

CNOT gate

The controlled-no longer gate or the CNOT gate acts on a pair of qubits, with one acting as “control” and the opposite as “target.” A not operation is done on the target whenever the manage is within the nation. This gate creates entanglement if the manage qubit is in a superposition.

This gate is generated inside the QiSkit (Du et al., 2005), where the implementation takes area by initializing qubits. The primary kingdom is flipped to the second one stays 0>. Subsequently, a CNOT gate is applied in which the first qubit will become the manipulate and the second one will become the target qubit respectively. After this, both the qubits are measured and the outcomes could be sent back from the tool.

This sample program run with QiSkit (Du et al., 2005) gives the values for data compression. Comparing with SVM and other models Chan-Vese gives an output of 90% with 3000 sample data collected from various fileds in and around Tamilnadu.

How Much Storage Is Reduced?

Reducing the storage space for easy processing is the main task of this research work, it is due to the concept of entanglement, qubits can hold up to two bits of data and transmit data between qubits up to 1400 meters apart. Bits hold either 0 or 1, only 1 bit at a time, whereas qubits on the other hand can hold 2 bits at the same time.2 zeroes or 2 ones or any proportion of both 1 or 0 at the same time.

An array of qubits can use the position that is superior (Gandhi and McGinnity, 2013) to represent all 2^64 possible values at once. This array can use these position that is superior (Gandhi and McGinnity, 2013) to represent all 2^64 possible values at once, allowing a quantum computer to solve problems that are practically impossible for standard computers.

This method helps to have all the qubits in a compressed state thus helping to build more space to withhold the data generated while identifying the defect in a paddy leaf plant. This methodology enhances the storage capacity and helps to find the defect in a quicker process. So, the idea of having qubits to bits paves the way for faster detection of the defects that emerges in a leaf. The concept of having 1 and 0 as qubits allows us to have many calculations simultaneously, thus making quantum computing powerful. Hence this is also seen as the future of Artificial Intelligence and Data Science.

Conclusion

With few challenges, exascale digital computers may further advance the knowledge of quantum chromodynamics. Digital computers can never achieve accurate simulations, but quantum computers will do so eventually. A collaborative effect is required by quantumists and field theorists to achieve this. This research work paves way for a new era in the field of agriculture to find the disease in the fastest way to eradicate hunger and food shortage.

Prediction of Bitcoin-Heist Ransomware Attack Using Machine Learning

S. Ishwarya,5

Abstract

Cryptocurrency is frequently used in a variety of virtual transactions to secure transactions. The few years have seen an increase in online scams, and with the advent of cryptocurrencies and their masquerading, it has never been easier for scammers. A cryptocurrency is a type of digital currency that can be exchanged for virtual goods and services over the Internet. Despite cryptocurrencies containing complex codes being kept secret which are meant to protect or preserve their security, capable hackers can nevertheless breach them. Ransomware attacks have emerged as a significant method of malware intrusion in recent years, usually, ransomware attacks take place through a website like linking the link the file gets corrupted. But here is the major scam during Bitcoin transactions. Therefore, we require improved ransomware prediction methods utilizing a suitable machine learning algorithm and a publicly accessible dataset. Using a variety of features to predict malicious transactions, abnormal Bitcoin transactions are used to evaluate these strategies.

Keywords: Cryptocurrency, Ransomware, Bitcoin, Machine learning, Transactions

Introduction

Globally, Crypto curries have revolutionized digital transactions. A little more than a decade after Satoshi Nakamoto created the first Bitcoin block; numerous digital currencies have been put in place. Satoshi Nakamoto introduced Bitcoin as a cryptocurrency in 2008. The maximum Bitcoin is a well-known cryptocurrency. By the use of an open-supply code, Bitcoin changed applied in 2009 with a System of digital banking. Bitcoin is the most widely used decentralized payment system, whereas the public ledger is entirely distributed. A Blockchain is a procedure for updating and growing a distributed public ledger that keeps track of Bitcoin transactions. It is created by some unknown, anonymous individuals.

Bitcoin is a digital asset that utilizes a network of peers to transfer value without banks or a central authority interfering. There are no physical bitcoins in circulation because Bitcoin is a digital currency. A set of implemented blocks is called a Blockchain. Bitcoin transactions are completely digital and virtually anonymous. There were 7,378 cryptocurrencies worldwide as of October 2020, with an overall market capitalization greater than $359.7 billion. Approximately 58% of this total was held by Bitcoin. A real-time blockchain monitoring website called Blockchain. info, says that more than 650,000 blocks have been created and that approximately $21 billion. Now, on average, a transaction is added to the Bitcoin blockchain every day.

Because of this, several online criminals have come to utilize unlawful actions consisting of Ransomware bills in a secure environment. A malicious program known as ransomware targets payment gateways and demands a ransom to be paid.

To detect Ransomware bitcoin addresses, a variety of machine-learning algorithms have been proposed. However, the test results must be verified on more recent Bitcoin addresses because they are not sufficiently general to classify Bitcoin addresses belonging to various malware families.

The pseudo members known as miners, are in charge of preserving and extending a distributed public ledger that records the transactions and is termed as a blockchain. Ransomware affects the payment with vicious code or the cryptocurrencies should be paid. Ransomware can encrypt content or lock access to resources. Ransomware will be conveyed through email connections or web-based weaknesses. Ransomware has recently been distributed through widespread exploits. A message is displayed by the malware requesting a specific number of Sending bitcoins to a Bitcoin address once resources are locked or encrypted. This amount could depend on the sum and size of the encoded assets. The victim receives a decipherment instrument upon payment. However, in some instances, like WannaCry, the ransomware had an untraceable bug that prevented the identification of the ransom payment made by the World Health Organization.

Related Works

Machine learning algorithms and NLP have been generally utilized in writing for different fields and purposes; they need improvement to be a component of the Bitcoin Ransomware area for grouping issues. Algorithms like Random Forest, K-Nearest Neighbour, BeroulliNavieBayes, Artificial Neural Network, long short-term memory, BI-LSTM & OoW techniques yield an accuracy of 94.92% with 3000 ransomware records belonging to 5 prominent families considering 23 particular pre-attack evasive API calls (Ricardo et al., 2021). In today’s computing world, ransomware has become a serious threat that must be stopped immediately. Digital substations and smart grid operations can also be disrupted by ransomware attacks. This paper examines an AI-based ransomware detection strategy and presents a ransomware attack modeling technique aimed at disrupting the running of a digital substation with a convolutional neural network model that produces an accuracy of 96.22% (Alvee et al., 2021).The implementation and methods of each type of ransomware vary, starting with how they spread, exploit vulnerabilities, and conceal their actions from performance, encryption techniques, and antivirus software. Ransomware-as-a-service, such as the Conti ransomware, is sophisticated since February 27, 2022 with static and dynamic analysis (Alzahrani et al., 2022). Due to its simplicity, digital currency or cryptocurrency is frequently used in a variety of virtual transactions. Virtual money that can be used to make payments on the internet is called cryptocurrency. Litecoin, Ethereum, Monero, Ripple, and Bitcoin are the most common cryptocurrencies. Ransomware detection model is built by using a back propagation artificial neural network of 5000 samples with an accuracy of 97% (Cahyani et al., 2021). The most common type of contemporary malware, crypto-ransomware, has had an impact on several industries and demanded a sizable ransom with static and dynamic analysis.Many AI-based studies of ransomware frequently lack behavioral analysis and correlation mapping with NLP and Machine learning classifiers for AIRaD (AI-based Ransomware Detection) (Poudyal and Dasgupta, 2021). A type of malware known as crypto-ransomware encrypts user data by utilizing the cryptography capabilities of the system. It becomes challenging to access user files when they are encrypted by a crypto-ransomware attack without the decryption key. Numerous variants of ransomware are being developed as a result of the accessibility of toolkits for creating ransomware, such as Ransomware as a Service (RaaS). This is because ransomware must be detected before encryption with adaptive pre-encryption models to deal with crypto-ransomware (Urooj et al., 2021). As an alternative means of storing value, Bitcoin is gaining popularity. It surpasses all other cryptocurrencies on the market in terms of market capitalization.However, because of its great worth, cybercriminals find it to be a desirable target.An industry standard for reporting information on cyber security breaches used to exploit Bitcoin exchange platforms was developed after a thorough assessment of 36 Bitcoin exchange security incidents. Two BTC laundering cases were examined in order to identify adversarial tactics following the breach (Oosthoek and Doerr, 2020). Cryptocurrencies that allow for pseudo-anonymous transactions have increased the number of various forms of electronic crime, particularly the use of cryptocurrency payments in hacking attacks that demand ransom by encrypting sensitive user data. Users use Bitcoin as a source of ransomware with topological data analysis to recognize fresh families of ransomware with no record of dealings. In the future, the topological and geometric approach to mapping entities to IP addresses in different locations will be proposed (Akcora et al., 2019). Large businesses and healthcare providers frequently face ransomware attacks. Ransomware aims to extract money from the victim by threatening to delete their data. Typically, ransomware works in three steps: identifying vulnerability in taking advantage of the network traffic of the victim. It primarily focuses on an API-based approach to ransomware detection using machine learning (ML) techniques and sandbox analysis. In future the multi-layer security solutions to protect ransomware families (Almousa et al., 2021). Due to its significant economic worth, numerous thefts have occurred of Bitcoin. Victims suffer enormous financial losses as a result of hackers stealing to transfer Bitcoin from hacked users, using their Bitcoin wallet keys. Methodology

Attacks using ransomware are becoming a significant source of virus penetration in recent years. One of the most disruptive cyber dangers is ransomware, which also affects productivity, accessibility, and reputation in addition to costing a lot of money. Ransomware is frequently created to avoid detection, despite its ultimate aims (encryption/locking), by running a sequence of pre-attack API requests, or “paranoia” activities, for choosing an appropriate execution environment. In this paper, we propose a ground-breaking attempt to use such paranoia behaviors to identify distinguishing ransomware behaviors. To accomplish this, we use more than 3000 samples from recent/notable ransomware families to identify their distinctively honed paranoia-inducing behaviors. In this study, we offer a dynamic analytic method for identifying ransomware samples based on their paranoid behaviors before an attack. To gather information about the behavioral traits/features of more than 3,000 ransomware samples from five well-known families, we execute them in a sandboxing environment while making 23 pre-attack evasion API calls that are connected to detecting the execution environment.

A Review of Classification, Detection, and Prognosis of Coronary Artery Disease

C. K. Revathi6

E-mail: revathi.ck2020@vitstudent.ac.in

DOI: 10.1201/9781003430452-7

Abstract

Coronary artery disease is a type of heart disease also called Ischemic heart disease. Currently, coronary heart disease is becoming a very common life-threatening disease in the world. It influences the young and old alike. The changes in people’s lifestyles are the major warning signs of CAD. Some major signs of CHD are smoking, unhealthy eating habits, obesity, hypertension, diabetes, and lack of exercise. These factors cause blocks in the arteries, which are nothing but plaques made up of fatty acids and other substances. It restricts the blood flow to the heart. Depending on the degree of damage to a coronary artery, one or more blocks form in the artery, resulting in myocardial infarction. If coronary artery disease is not controlled early, it leads to congestive heart failure. Early classification, detection, and prevention of coronary artery disease is very important to prevent this situation. Classification methods are used to discriminate between healthy individuals and CAD patients. A discovery method is used to discover the type of CAD that has occurred. Prevention methods are used to prescribe medications and treatments to prevent further complications from CAD. A variety of diagnostic methods are used to determine the severity of CAD. So, in this article, we looked at the types of CAD, the risk factors for CAD, and the various algorithms used to classify, diagnose, detect, and predict CAD.

Keywords: Coronary artery disease, classification, Detection, Prediction, Diagnosis, Risk factors

Introduction

The heart is the vital organ of the body that circulates blood through arteries and veins called the circulatory system. Body parts need oxygen-rich blood to function. The aorta receives oxygenated blood from the lungs and supplies blood through the coronary arteries. In Shahjehan and Bhutta (2021), the author describes that there are various types of arteries, such as the right coronary artery, the left artery, the circumflex artery, and the left anterior descending coronary artery. Khan et al. (2020), the authors reported that atherosclerosis is a major cause of coronary heart disease. This is nothing but more plaque formation in the arteries. Plaque is a substance such as cholesterol, fatty acids, and other substances that form in the arteries, narrowing the arteries and reducing or blocking blood flow, which prevents the heart from getting enough blood, leading to coronary heart disease. Because of the decreased blood supply, other bodily parts are also impacted. For example, a stroke can occur because the brain does not get enough blood. In Shahjehan and Bhutta (2021), the authors stated that peripheral arterial disease (PAD) occurs because there is not enough blood supply to the arms and legs. This coronary artery disease occurs due to risk factors. In Zhang et al. (2019), the authors argue that the strongest risk factor for CHD is plasma OX-LDL, which is detected in the early stages. The authors discussed various hazards of CAD in Malakar et al. (2019). Smoking increases atherosclerotic lesions and moves coronary heart disease to the next stage called coronary artery occlusion. Another cholesterol-related risk factor for CHD is type 2 diabetes. Cholesterol levels are maintained with medication.

Cholesterol is formed as a result of fat accumulation. Fats are classified into two types. One of them is the good fat that your body uses for metabolic activity. Also, bad fats affect normal blood circulation. It is deposited in the coronary arteries, called plaques, and blocks blood flow to the heart.

Epidemiology CAD

  • From 1990 to 2020, the number of deaths in India attributable to cardiovascular disease grew from 2.26 million to 4.77 million. Mortality from coronary heart disease increased by 1.6% to 7.4% of the rural population and by 1% to 13.2% of the urban population.
  • Coronary heart disease was a very dangerous disease in 2019, causing 360,000 deaths in 2019. Young and old people are also affected by CAD from age 20 to 65.

Types of CAD

In Khan et al. (2020), the authors have described the different types of CAD. Small artery walls develop single-vessel coronary artery disease, which restricts the flow of blood containing oxygen to the heart. Lack of blood flow causes chest pain and shortness of breath. Diagnosis is through medication and treatment. Two-way coronary artery disease reduces blood flow in a cross-sectional area of both arteries. DVCAD patients are usually treated medically or surgically. Revascularization techniques are used to treat poor left ventricular function. Three-vessel coronary artery disease occurred in all three large epicardial coronary arteries. Patients with TVCAD are treated with an angioplasty procedure.

The remaining sections of the article are arranged as follows. Under Section 2, the literature review of existing papers was reviewed and mainly focused on the classification of CAD, detection of CAD, diagnosis, and prevention of CAD. In Section 3 the overview of the paper was discussed and concluded with the future works.

Related Works

Classification of CAD

In Raghavendra et al. (2018), the author talked about the issue of non-invasive diagnostic test methods not being able to determine the precise effects of CAD. Therefore, the author proposed a computer-aided diagnostic system to detect coronary artery disease by taking the ECG images and decomposing them into the sub-bands using the Double Density Dual Tree Discrete Wavelet Transform (DD-DTDWT), and the Features are extracted from the sub-bands using entropies and dimensions are reduced by Marginal FisherAnalysis (MFA). The accuracy of this technique, which uses the CADRI to classify coronary artery disease, is 96%.

In Caliskan and Yuksel (2017), the author said medical experts in well-equipped hospitals are doing the procedure of invasive diagnosis of CAD. Due to its high cost, this diagnostic method has been used by a limited number of patients. The proposed method is a combination of two autoencoders and a soft-max layer along with a DNN classifier for CAD classification and shows the highest accuracy compared to SVM, KNN, and DT.

In Khan et al. (2020), the authors took the raw ECG signal. Empirical mode decomposition and eigenmode functions were used to extract statistical, shape, energy, and entropy properties after preprocessing and segmentation. This pre-processed signal was passed to the Cubic-SVM classifier. He classified general items and CAD items and classified CAD into SVCAD, DVCAD, and TVCAD. The proposed method provides 95% accuracy.

In Sharma and Acharya (2019), the authors addressed the problem of manual analysis of ECG signals as inefficient and error-prone, and CAD diagnostic testing is more difficult for the elderly and patients with physical disabilities. Therefore, the authors proposed an automated diagnosis method for the classification of CAD. The authors used an optimal focusing time-frequency (OTFC) and bidirectional wavelet filter bank (BWFB) for CAD identification. Extract features from OTFC using log energy and fuzzy entropy. CAD classification is achieved by 10-fold cross-validation and GSVM. This method gives 99.53% accuracy.

Detection of CAD

In Acharya et al. (2017), the author discussed the instability of the ECG signal, the diagnosis of abnormal heart rhythms took a long time and resulted in errors. Therefore, the authors used an auto-diagnostic method. The proposed method is a CNN it includes 4 convolution layers, 3 fully connected layers, and 4 maximally pooled layers. 2s and 5s ECG signals are used to diagnose CAD. This method gives an accuracy of 94.95%

In Acharya et al. (2018), the authors point out that the ECG signal is unstable, and the expert visually corrects the signal. Accordingly, the author proposed a computer system for signal purification that can easily detect CAD. The authors used entropy to reveal hidden characteristics of the ECG signal and differentiate between healthy individuals and CAD-affected persons. If the detection of the Q3 variability of the ECG signal indicates an abnormal heart rate, In contrast to healthy people, it is less useful in people with the disease. This method provides 90% accuracy.

In AlHosani et al. (2017), the PAT technique is employed to create a QRS detection system for CAD detection. The authors proposed a method to detect the R peak in the ECG signal and determine the smallest R-R interval. The characteristics are taken from the ECG signal and classified using the following algorithms called KNN, DT, and SVM. This method provides greater than 90% accuracy.

In Banerjee et al. (2020) was that there were no clinically known biomarkers for the diagnosis of CAD. The authors combined two non-specific biomarkers: atypical ECG morphology and irregular heart rate variability, using a combined CNN-LSTM architecture to classify CAD. CNN was used to measure the expansion of heart rate variability to extract morphological features from ECG and LSTM. This method gives 93% accuracy.

In Butun et al. (2020), the authors proposed automatic CAD detection using capsule networks, a technique known as deep neural networks. ECG signals at 2s and 5s automatically detect CAD using a deep learning model called 1D-CAPSNET. This method gives an accuracy of 99.44%.

Prediction of CAD

In Chen and Hengjinda (2021), Early prediction of CHD is a challenging task. Therefore, the authors proposed knowledge-based identification and construction of the Pooled Area Curve (PUC) for a more accurate and faster estimation of CAD using machine learning. The SVM algorithm is a recent image-based adaptive classification method for CAD prediction with an accuracy of 93%

. In Ayon et al. (2022), the authors used Naive Bayes, Random Forest, and K-Nearest Neighbor for Coronary Heart Disease Prediction, along with seven artificial intelligence techniques, such as decision trees, support vector machines, deep neural networks, and logistic regression. When compared to other organizations, this deep neural network obtained accuracy with the best score of 98.15 percent.

In Khan (2020), predicting heart disease is a difficult task, so experts predicted heart disease using IoT sensors, but the accuracy was poor. The author connects the smartwatch sensor and monitoring device to the patient’s MDCNN to detect heart disease, receives blood pressure and electrocardiogram measurements through the sensor, classifies the patient, and compares them with the DNN. A modified deep convolutional neural network (MDCNN) is suggested. and logistic regression. Provides 98.2 % accuracy.

In Ayatollahi et al. (2019), CAD prediction was performed by many algorithms, but they did not provide better accuracy, so the authors proposed two data mining algorithms for CAD prediction. The authors used ANN and SVM algorithms for prediction in these SVMs, which gave the highest accuracy compared to ANN. These data mining algorithms are used to increase the PPV value for CAD prediction. Evaluate CAD proactively using machine learning. The SVM algorithm is a recent adaptive image-based classification method for predicting CAD with the highest accuracy.

Diagnosis of CAD

In Velusamy and Ramasamy (2021), the authors suggest using a heterogeneous ensemble approach. The ensemble voting technique used the K-Nearest Neighbor, Random Forest, and Support Vector Machine three fundamental classifiers to forecast CAD. These classifiers are based on the majority vote (MVEn), the weighted average vote (AVEn), and the average voting rate (WAVEn). Using the Boruta wrapper feature selection technique, features were chosen. There are 98 in the WAVEn algorithm, which is used to identify CAD early on. accuracy of 97%.

In Abdar et al. (2019), the consequences of CDSS (Clinical Decision Support System) on individual health are rapidly increasing, making it difficult for doctors to diagnose. To overcome this, the author used a method called (NE-nu-SVC). This method combines an ensemble learning method with a machine learning model for CAD diagnosis. Performance was improved using a genetic search algorithm and class balancer for feature extraction, a resampling method was used to balance the data with a multi-level filtering method, and four kernel functions were used to achieve up to 98.60% accuracy.

In Zomorodi-moghadam et al. (2021), rule detection is a complex data mining problem. However, production rules were used for accurate and efficient automatic CAD detection. The authors proposed a Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) algorithm to identify CAD diagnostic rules for real, integer, and binary data types. A combination of real and binary PSO is used to diagnose CAD. Features are selected in two ways: the 11-feature selection method and the 13-subset selection method. Compared to 13 subset selection methods, 11 subset selection methods showed the highest accuracy.

In Joloudari et al. (2020) diagnosed coronary artery disease using a medical imaging technique called coronary angiography, but it was expensive and accompanied by various side effects. Therefore, the authors proposed a comprehensive machine-learning method for selecting prognostic features for accurate CAD diagnosis. The authors used four classification models for CAD diagnosis:

SVM, CHAID, C5.0 decision tree, and a 10-fold cross-validated random tree. The authors concluded that random trees provide the highest accuracy compared to other models.

Conclusions and Future Studies

In this review, we studied the various algorithms used for the classification, detection, prevention, and diagnosis methods of CAD. The classification method is the foremost method to diagnose patients. In the existing papers, SVM, GSVM, DT, and KNN and various algorithms are used. Compared to this algorithm DNN algorithms like CNN and LSTM give 99.85% accuracy. Some of the disadvantages identified in the existing work are less number of images are used for feature selection and extraction. In the detection of CAD, borderline patients are not identified. The weights of the classifier are not considered for the feature extraction process. The Deep Neural network and its algorithms effectively classify the CAD for the future diagnosis process.

Optimization of Packet Length using Exclusive SCCO Algorithm In WSN And IoT Based Networks

R. Adhi lakshmi7

Mail id: rajan@psnacet.edu.in

E-mail: radhilakshmi80@gmail.com*, rajan@psnacet.edu.in, anwar@crescent.education

DOI: 10.1201/9781003430452-8

Abstract

The IoT (Internet of Things) nodes consuming energy efficiency (EE) depend on optimizing packet sizes. The fundamental idea behind WSN is to reduce the amount of energy used for wireless packet delivery. Battery-less networks with packet size optimization in WSN and IoT-based networks had not yet been addressed. The development of optimization algorithms inspired by the natural phenomenon is widely presented in many papers. The rules utilized in the bio-inspired algorithm are simple, they provide improved performance. Bio-inspired algorithms have grown as a newly developing field in computer technology and services in various kinds of applications. The development of bio-inspired algorithms needs a suitable problem representation, determining the solution accuracy using fitness function and setting expressions to develop a new solution set. Three different types of networks namely, 1-hop, 2-hop, and multi-hop networks are used to implement the suggested technique. For all these three types of networks, a mathematical model is created that accounts for the communication channel, energy efficiency, and energy consumption. Shifting Cultivation and Cropping based optimization (SCCO) algorithm depends on the fields that are cultivated for a relatively short time and allowed to recover. Then, the new crops are planted after the cultivation. This process is said to be SCCO. This process is utilizing MATLAB, the outcomes obtained from the newly introduced work are verified and the performance is compared with the conventional optimization algorithm. From the evaluation and simulation outcomes, it is said that the newly modified technique provides better accuracy and faster convergence.

Keywords: Bio-inspired, optimization algorithm, Fitness function, Problem-solving

Introduction

In today’s world scenario, the developed society entails “maximum benefit with minimum cost.” Typically, these objectives can be obtained with the utilization of optimization techniques. This kind of object is required in different fields and those objectives are developed as optimization issues and the optimum solutions using various optimization procedures. The process of modifying a process’ inputs or a device’s features to establish the least or maximum output is identified as optimization based on the requirement. The input for the problem contains variables; the process to be optimized is differently named as the objective function, cost, or fitness function. Their respective output of the process is the fitness or cost outcome. Hence, it should be carefully considered in presenting the optimization algorithm that the initial values must be selected for ensuring convergence towards the global optimum and not to converge at the local optimum. These demerits can be overcome by the heuristic optimization techniques which provide optimum solutions within a logical amount of time and by consuming less computation time and less memory space.

Related Work

Bio-Inspired Algorithms (BIA) have developed as a newly developing field in computer technology and serve in various kinds of applications such as computer networks, biomedical engineering, security, control systems, robotics, data mining, power systems, etc. To create the new BIA namely Spined Loach Searching Optimization (SLSO) algorithm, consideration was given to how spiny loach fish look for food and whether the environment is suitable for their survival (Sasikala and Pavalarajan, 2022). Additionally, the repetitive transmissions are reduced effectively within the clusters (Sasikala and Pavalarajan, 2022). The efficient Zone head (ZH) is elected using the PSO algorithm (Sasi et al., 2019). The fitness value is calculated using three factors, the amount of remaining battery power, the number of nearby sensor nodes, and the Euclidean distance of the deployment area for the nodes to the center. Many BIAs for resolving optimization issues have been presented. They are Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) (Kennedy and Eberhart, 1995) algorithm, Genetic algorithm (GA) (De Jong, 1975), Biogeography-Based Optimizer (BBO) [10] method, Simulated Annealing (SA) (Kirkpatrick and Gelatt, 1983), Gravitational Search Algorithm (GSA) [14], Gravitational Local Search Algorithm (GLSA) (Webster and Bernhard, 2003), Ant Colony Optimization (ACO) (Dorigo and Blum, 2005), Big-Bang Big-Crunch (BBBC) (Erol and Eksin, 2006).

Proposed Methodology

SCCO algorithm in WSN

SCCO is a meta-heuristic process based on the shifting-cropping activity of cultivators in the agricultural land. Each crop symbolizes a sensor node in this learning. First, select a Global Cultivator (GC) as a potential solution based on performance. When food becomes scarce, GC divides the population into subgroups. A Local Cultivator (LC) is in charge of each sub-group. The group members discuss their findings after one investigation cycle, and the cultivator goes to the region with the most plentiful agricultural land (i.e., optimal result). As a result, the global cultivator shifts to the perfect location in the overall exploration findings, while local cultivators move to the best position within their local groups. As a result, SCCO finds the best location rapidly while avoiding convergence to local optima.

Probability of Shifting Cultivation in SCCO

Nodes Initialization

The initialization of the population is the first step in the exploration process. Node deployment uses Eq. (4), SM represents a node in the search space ranging from 1 to N.

(1)
SCij = SCminj  + R1 × (SCmaxj −SCminj )

SCij is ithspider monkey in jthdimension, R1 is a random number: 0< R1<1 , SCminj and SCmaxj are search space’s lowest and higher limits.

Local cultivator phase

The local cultivator (leader) phase is defined as,

(2)
$$\begin{array}{l} \left. SC_{i}^{\text{new~}}\leftarrow SC_{i} + R_{1} \times \left( {Lc - SC_{i}} \right) + R_{2} \times \left( {SC_{r} - SC_{i}} \right), \right. \\ {i = (1,2,\ldots,\text{N})} \\ \end{array}$$

where N is the number of shifting cultivations, SCinew is the updated location of the ith shifting cultivation, SCi is its current location, R1 & R2 denote a random number between (0,1) & (1,1)

respectively, Lc is the location of a local cultivator, and SCr is the location of a randomly selected shifting cultivation from the same group. If r 1 >PR, (5) is evaluated; where PR is the perturbation rate.

Global cultivator phase

This phase follows the local cultivator phase. SC’s position is updated here based on Gc experience, social experience, and perseverance. In this phase, the positional update formula is provided below:

(3)
$$\begin{array}{l} \left. SC_{j}^{\text{new~}}\leftarrow SC_{j} + R_{1} \times \left( {Gc - SC_{j}} \right) + R_{2} \times \left( {SC_{r} - SC_{j}} \right), \right. \\ {i = (1,2,\ldots,\text{N})} \\ \end{array}$$

Gc holds the position of global cultivator. In this stage, the SC’s position is updated based on the probability Pi computed from the fitness value. As a result, the superior candidate has a better probability of receiving an upgrade.

(4)
$$P_{i} = 0.9 \times \frac{fit_{i}}{\text{max}_{\text{f}}\text{it}} + 0.1$$

The fitness of ith SC is fit, and the maximal fitness value in the cropping cluster is max_ fit. The new position of the SC is created and the fitness rate is calculated only ifRl< Pi. The new fitness value is compared to the previous one, and if the new value is better, the new position is taken.

Local Cultivator Decision Phase

If the local cultivator does not get organized to a predetermined limit in local cultivator, members of the group periodically adjust their places using either random initialization or PR-based data on global cultivator experience given by,

(5)
SCjnew ←SCij+R1×(Lc−SCij)+R2×(SCrj−Lc)

CH selection using SCCO

Algorithm CH selection using SCCO

  1. Initialize the population, local & global cultivator limit, perturbation limit
  2. Calculate fitness (individual nodes fitness using (9))
  3. Select local & global cultivators through greedy algorithm

    2. Using fitness outcome, choose greedy rule

End Loop

(9)

Where Econs(Ni) is the energy consumed by the ith node. The node having more remaining energy is the better candidate to be selected as the CH. Thus, pick up the node nearest to the target as the CH.

Where (Ni) is the distance between ith node and destination. The CH node should have minimum distance to the destination. Sending packets of data from the sender to the receiver in a less time improves system performance.

Optimizing and Controlling of Packet Length

The goal of SC optimization is to reduce the cost function and increase the fitness function of energy efficiency. Following calculation, the packet length’s efficiency is related to the best fitness outcome ( SC best ) and the score of the randomly selected is computed and denoted as

(13)
SCbest = max {SCijnew}&SCscore = SCinew + SCjnew

The new optimal solution set is then identified in the next round.

And finally, the efficient remaining energy of CH can be determined using the following equation as,

(15)

The neighbor CH with higher remaining energy and good link quality is selected as a relay node toward the destination for effective communication. The data transmission procedure begins after finding the optimum path.

Performance Analysis

The first step is to analyze the energy efficiency (EE), packet error rate, and energy consumption of the networks in relation to various payloads and the distance between the source and the destination. As a first measure, the payload size and distance among the source and destination nodes of the packet are checked for three different types of networks. Figure 1a shows the rise in packet error as a function of the separation between the source and destination nodes. The payload in this simulation process is stable at 100 and 1000 bits, which represent the maximum and minimum payload bits.

The minimum distance of 120 cm at which data can be transmitted with an inaccuracy of roughly 0.15 p.u. The route for data packets with an optimum size can be determined using this information. Figure 1b depicts the rise in PER as a result of the larger payload. It tested on all three networks in the 0 to 300-bit packet size range for two separate source and destination distances of 150 cm and 200 cm. As the payload expands beyond the capability of the transmission link, the PER rate will also rise.

Conclusion

In this paper, a Shifting Cultivation and Cropping based optimization (SCCO) has been considered for presenting a bio-inspired optimization process. The SCCO procedure is presented by taking the features of the plant such as plant size, fruit size, fruit color, and the number of grains as the variable. For obtained the solution set for the given optimization issues, search space by considering the plants located in the field as population. Then from this population, the plant which is superior in the consideration of all features is selected as the optimum solution. It is used to control packet sizes in networks powered by WSNs and IoTs. By contrasting the simulated results with the outcomes obtained using traditional algorithms such as S2SO, PSO, and ACO in terms of PER, EE, and Energy usage, the suggested algorithm is proven to be effective.

Novel Triphasic Architecture to Ascertain Malicious Exam-Takers

Aditya Deepak Joshi, Garvit Luhadia, Rajarshi Bhattacharyay, Sendhil Kumar, K. S.,8

SCOPE, Vellore Institute of Technology, Vellore, India

DOI: 10.1201/9781003430452-9

Abstract

In this paper, we propose a novel attack vector against webcams aptly named “video feed replacement.” We begin by introducing the presence and the possible impacts of it being used, in academic, professional, and most importantly online exam settings. Post establishing its existence, the researchers propose a triphasic architecture to counter the vulnerability and detect other forms of malpractices (namely off-screen devices, periods of focus, and stress). The triphasic design will detect video loops faster and more reliably than the human eye while minimizing the instances of false positives. The specific goals of this paper are to present an architecture encompassing a pattern-matching solution to a video-feed replacement, a Gaze Tracking system to monitor the gaze of the subject offscreen, and a blink rate monitor to gauge the attributes of stress and focus. Furthermore, the researchers aim for this paper to emphasize the possible untoward security impacts of this medium of attacks right from being professionally unethical at best to impersonation and gaining unauthorized access to information at worst. Finally, the researchers end the paper by establishing the robustness of the architecture by subjecting it to varying framerates and resolutions of incoming video feeds and subjects facing the webcam.

Keywords: video Loop Detection, KMP algorithm, perceptual hashing, gaze detection, blink rate detection

Introduction

Video Conferencing or Video Calling as is the common parlance has become the most lucid and widespread means of near-in-person communication in today’s day and age. This ubiquity has brought with it an unprecedented and exigent rise in cybercrime (Monteith et al., 2021). It was only a matter of time before the education sector became a target of the same (Abdelrahim, 2021). The fundamental nature of remote working is remote e-exams from the bud remove a layer of integrity checks that usually exist during in- person examinations. These include but are not limited to (Aldridge and Wooley, 1990) pat-downs of students, checking for the absence of chits and other objectionable materials and preventing collaborative malpractice of students, and preventing damage to institutional infrastructure. To facilitate these new remote education needs, platforms like Teams, Zoom, and Codetantra have seen phenomenal rises in usage rates. This not only facilitated the resumption of examinations but also ensured the continuity of classes for students the world over. However, this boon brought with it the bane of malpractices. There have been reports of people substituting with other people, replacing live video feeds in exams such as the GRE and the GMAT (NDTV, 2021; Varma et al., 2021; Pranav Mukul, 2021). Furthermore, one would be wrong in assuming that the pre-existing exams such as those that existed before this wave of new software would remain unaffected in this scourge of exam malpractices. The in- home variant of these tests does have preliminary checks of the exam taker’s environment however, clever sleight of hand has been known to undo these efforts. Video Feed Replacement refers to the replacement of a live webcam feed with a pre- recorded video, in essence deceiving the software into thinking the video source is a video input device. To be perfectly transparent, the use cases of this software were perfectly harmless and extremely useful. They are meant to augment the experience of hosting live streams and videos by providing hotfixes and shortcuts to quickly switch to and from a video source to screen share to a recorded video. Now comes the nefarious bit, under the cover of a recorded video malicious actors could perform devious acts unbeknownst to the person on the receiving end. While this paper primarily discusses the harmful impacts that this could potentially have in an exam scenario, another not-so-benign outlet could be in the workplace or in a classroom wherein the listener absences themselves or slacks off thereby drastically reducing overall productivity. The scale of Zoom meetings in the year 2022 was over 300 million daily visitors (Zippia, 2022). A flaw compromising the integrity of this platform could hamper the ability to conduct day-to-day business for thousands of institutions.

What makes securing against this attack complicated is that the “replaced” video feeds also display UUIDs like those of authentic webcams. Additionally, except for tiny watermarks, these feeds are nearly indistinguishable from the original feeds both in terms of their performance and their quality. A motivated attacker could potentially opt for a paid subscription rendering them indistinguishable to the human eye with quicker, more streamlined transitions between videos.

In the topic of Gaze Tracking, by monitoring the subject’s eye movements and finding patterns that may suggest malice, one can use it to detect and deter cheating in computer-based examinations. For example, if an examinee regularly glances at a second device or looks away from the screen for extended periods, this could indicate assistance from a third party. Furthermore, gaze tracking can detect patterns such as fast eye movements or changes in pupil dilation that may suggest tension or worry, as well as cheating conduct. Gaze tracking can help to assure the integrity and fairness of computer-based exams by detecting and discouraging cheating. To ensure the real- time responsiveness of the proposed system, the authors focused on low-level features that can provide deterministic results. Not only that, but gaze pattern recognition is also a technology that analyses and interprets an individual’s gaze patterns using eye-tracking software and algorithms. It is used to investigate how people interact with their surroundings. Traditionally Shi et al. (2021) and Yeamkuan and Chamnongthai (2020), gaze pattern recognition technology tracks the movement of the eyes using an additional camera or sensors, which analyze the data to find patterns. The device can measure where a person looks, how long they look there, and even their blink rate. Analyzing these patterns can offer insights into human behavior and decision-making. The status quo surrounding the measurement of gaze is two-fold, it involves the gaze tracking devices meant to be attached to the face of the subject or measuring the gaze of a subject within the screen using calibration points. A person’s blinking rate has long been used as a tool to analyze a person’s thought processes. Initially, it was used as a lie detection method without the use of instruments (Porter and Brinke, 2008; Leal and Vrij, 2008). Furthermore coupled with Artificial Intelligence of late blink rate has been an effective medium in the forensic sciences and interrogatory situations (Gullapalli et al., 2021; Koganti et al., 2022). The researchers posit that this can be used as a powerful first ‘red flag’ in online video-based communication channels. It has been established on numerous occasions that the blink rate is influenced heavily by the subject’s thought processes and mental state. For instance, the authors of Ranti et al. (2020) definitively state that the blink rate of a person slows down in periods of heavy focus as is usually the case in exams. Combining these insights, we reach the resultant architecture in Fig. 2. The webcam serves as the data input while the loop construct in the architecture breaks apart the video feed into a buffer that the three modules tap into. The three modules respectively result in binary flags f1, f2, and f3 which can then be converted into flashing indicators for the benefit of the proctor. The architecture will then be tested against videos of exam-givers with varying video parameters of framerates and resolutions while testing for the execution time in sending out the flags.

Related Work

When we came across the work of Klijn et al. (2022), we found that the findings by the authors reflected our encounters, and it was, therefore, a natural starting point for our research. It concluded the following; First, in terms of higher accuracy and quicker completion times, the students who received the issue in the latter round did better. Second, there are no appreciable variations between the various exam versions in terms of accuracy and time taken for questions that were not random in order, or by the university’s code of ethics, which was flashed at random to half of the students midway during the exam. The researchers of Klijn et al. (2022) left us with the dilemma that, for the exam under consideration to be fair, all students should be given the same questions. For online tests, however, it seems hazardous to assign identical questions to every student, especially if there are no additional safeguards against cheating. Understanding the factors that lead to cheating in performance situations in the early stages of schooling can be crucial for preventing dishonest conduct in the future, particularly if cheating persists over time as a habit or a character feature (Klijn et al., 2022). To drastically reduce the number of rogue psychological characteristics associated with maturity that may have an impact on the study’s findings, research was predominantly done on primary school students. They show that children who have higher IQs and socioeconomic positions are more likely to cheat. They identify an intriguing relationship between altruism and incentives, as well as the fact that the availability of rewards for improved performance does not promote cheating behavior: altruistic students cheat significantly less in the presence of incentives. This shows that good-hearted kids could be reluctant to get pecuniary advantage from immoral behavior. The extensive body of research on other-regarding preferences has shown that entitlements and the source of income play a significant role in predicting other-regarding behavior. The study finds no conclusive evidence of the influence of parenting approaches on cheating, and there is no connection between cheating and risk or temporal references. The authors found it fascinating that a creative performance setting produces an interesting outcome on cheating and performance, whereby exposure to many sorts of replies and learning obtained from cheating may help one to do better in the future. For educational policymakers, investigating measures to stop dishonest behavior in children at a young age is a top priority. The work done by Klijn et al. (2022) provides an exploration of academic cheating at a young age, in a performance context where incentives can be adjusted. According to the authors of [8], students who were not compelled to employ a proctor performed 11% better on average than those who did. Additionally, in the in-person class where increased socializing might encourage cooperation, the gap in results of proctored and unproctored tests was significantly larger. The authors discover that students with lower ACT scores tend to partake in malicious tactics to a greater extent. The findings provide credence to the idea that exam anxiety may have an impact on both proctored and unproctored exam performance. As a sad consequence of the widespread use of standardized testing within and between nations, there has been a recent drive for more accountability in the delivery of education. As rightly stated in Martinelli et al. (2018) via legislative repercussions for the schools or through penalties for student promotion, reliance on standardized testing has inevitably increased the stakes in the assessments for both instructors and kids. Finally putting this together, the experiment in Milone et al. (2017) demonstrates that online proctoring has a substantial impact on learning especially when compared to unproctored tests. It concludes that using an online proctoring service hurts the exam-giving process and inexorably increases cheating. In this paper, we propose a methodology to augment and empower observers and exam proctors to effectively clip the rampant problem of bad actors in online examinations while remaining sufficiently real-timed to provide the requisite fairness on the spot.

Methodology

Video Feed Integrity

The concept of a perceptual hash is well researched, initially discussed in The Hacker Factor Blog (2023). Most recently it has found applications in computer vision as it allows for an easier comparison of images and devises a form of relative arithmetic between the images. For instance, an image of a white and a black cardigan is relatively similar, however, a third image of a grey cardigan is considered closer in terms of hashes to the white one than the black one is. Keeping this in mind, the researchers inculcate this concept into a live video feed, a groundbreaking concept considering the usage of hashing in videos is restricted to protecting video streams rather than being used to detect patterns in them. To emphasize the scale of this the researchers would encourage the researchers to imagine a pattern-matching problem that involves a repeating string such as in Fig. 3. Now to identify this the traditional means would either involve the observer remembering the alphabets A through F to then meaningfully identify that there was a repeating pattern. However, it has been demonstrated in the curve of forgetting that in a matter of minutes, richer details of the subject begin slipping from memory rendering the attack successful.

Now to solve this the researchers introduce a novel concept of linking the Knuth-Morris-Pratt (KMP) Algorithm a dynamically programmed algorithm to exactly perform the above while maintaining a highly minimal record of image PHashes and also providing the expected real- timedness of such a platform. This is achieved by the very nature of the algorithm being 0(n). The implementation of this algorithm is as follows; it avoids comparison with an incoming Hash of a new frame Hm that has previously been compared with the repeating pattern or the buffer of Hashes. The dynamic programming aspect allows us to store the intermediate results instead of recomputing them in essence performing the remembrance for the observer. In totality the algorithm allows us to prevent the backtracking on the stream of previous video frame hashes.

Gaze Tracking

To begin the Gaze Tracking we use the Image Buffer to establish the subject’s eyes’ coordinates. The real-time eye coordinates of a person are in essence, sequential data. In several minutes, any patterns in the movement of the eyes in the coordinate space act as an indicator of a violation of academic integrity and are an indicator of a distracted or malicious flitting of gaze from the task at hand. To discover patterns in these high- volume, high-velocity data points, we need to devise a highly efficient motif discovery methodology. To analyze this time series data, one could either visualize the data or calculate a global summary of it or describe it through statistics. As we have a considerably longer duration of time series, we considered developing an ARIMA model to detect anomalies or attempting a forecasting model in which we compare our forecasted values to the actual data. We quickly found that these were too complex to cater to the required real-time experience. To add to the disadvantages, they frequently produce false positives and provide no interpretable information. A probable reason is, these methods attempt to exploit all available dimensions, rendering them prone to failure. Therefore, in addition to being efficient, we require the method to be intelligent in generating the Multi-Dimensional(MD) Matrix Profile(MP) to aid us in picking the relevant subset of dimensions to be used in finding MD motifs.``

(1)
T(i) ∈ Rn : T = [T(1),T(2),T(3),…,T(d)]T

(2)
T(i, m) ∈ R(d × m) : T(i, m) = [T(i, m)(1),T(i, m)(2),T(i, m)(3),…,T(i, m)(d)]T

(3)
$${dist}^{(k)}\left( {T_{i,m},T_{j,m}} \right) = \min\limits_{X}{dist}\left( {T_{i,m}(X),T_{j,m}(X)} \right)$$

(4)
D ∈ Rn − m + 1 = dist(k)(Ti, m,Tj, m)∀j ∈ [1, 2, …, n − m + 1]

(5)
$$\begin{array}{l} {{dist}^{(k)}\left( {T_{a,m},T_{b,m}} \right) \leq {dist}^{(k)}\left( {T_{i,m},T_{j,m}} \right)} \\ {\forall i,j \in \lbrack 1,2,3,\ldots,n - m + 1\rbrack\forall a \neq b \land i \neq j} \\ \end{array}$$

(6)
P ∈ Rn − m + 1 = D ∈ Rn − m + 1∀j ∈ [1, 2, 3, …, n − m + 1]

We present a strategy based on simple mathematical calculations that allow us to recognize approximately repeating subsequences located inside a longer time series using techniques employed in DNA sequencing. To claim that a pattern or subsequence is “roughly repeated,” you must possess the ability to compare them. We were inspired by how MP was used in Zhu (2016). The primary benefit of computing the MP is that it not only helps you to locate motifs fast but also finds the nearest neighbor for every subsequence in your time series. To begin with, a multidimensional time series T as stated by the researchers is a set of time series that co-evolve and have a set dimensionality and subsequence length. Since it is not feasible to discover motifs in all the dimensions of the time series, a subsequence is extracted only using a subset of all dimensions. This is essentially a set of univariant subsequences from T of length m starting from position i. Next, to identify the dimensions to be used and reduce the dimensionality of the sequential data, a distance function is used, which calculates the “distance between two multidimensional subsequences” using the best k dimensions out of a total of d. This data is then stored in a vectorial representation D. Using this distance metric, the most similar subdimensional subsequence pairs, are found and labeled as “motifs.” These motifs are stored in pairs (as defined in Equation 5) and are stored as a matrix. This is the MP utilized when attempting to find patterns in sequential data. Mathematically, a k-dimensional MP is a meta-time series that stores normalized Euclidean distances between each subsequence and its nearest neighbor. Finally, it is tasked with recording the smallest non-trivial distances in each instance in the real implementation of our use case, this substantially reduces the space complexity to 0(n) (Zhu, 2016), another essential characteristic of such an architecture considering the scale. This method enables us to approach this problem as essentially a time series analysis in which we detect the data points that do not conform to the established pattern, which when repeated over a specified number of video frames, are flagged as potentially malicious.

Blink Rate

This section of the application involves the detection of the blinking of the subject in a timeframe. The researchers devised an improvement to the current method of blink detection as follows. Firstly, the detection of a blink as demonstrated in Soukupova and Jan Cech (2016) is largely subject to computer vision and the detection of a person’s facial landmarks, the sclera of the subject, and its disappearance. This applied to a video feed is slow and disallows the ability to establish a rate. This is because the detection is largely down to probabilities and is not subject to a binary (eyes open - eyes closed response). The system proposed here is to measure the blinks by establishing the nature of the eyes using the static images from the buffer. Compared to current works not only would this allow for a higher degree of confidence in the detection but also allow for a faster response time. Establishing the level of granularity in Fig 4 would be highly intractable using the conventional method considering the normal rate of 12-20 blinks per minute. Our system proposes to analyze this single-degree measure across time to highlight extended lengths of time with a higher or lower blink rate. This takes into account the innate blinking rate and highlights the periods of stress or focus in the context of the online environment. Take for instance the period between minutes 4 and 5 where the blink rate skyrockets to 28 or 29 blinks per minute. This indeed highlights a period of frantic blinking or distracted blinking that the proctor must be made aware of. Furthermore, we see a large and continued drop after minute 8, this highlights a period of focus and indicates a period wherein the subject must not be perturbed.

Results

To analyze the architecture setup the researchers subjected it to looped footage of exam-givers of varying lengths, resolutions, and framerates. This was done to simulate various webcam setups as well as to determine the performance of the algorithm. The metric to analyze the performance is the time taken to determine the presence of a loop, this is done for the simple purpose that the system needs to ascertain malicious acts with confidence while being sufficiently real-time as the detection of a deed long after it is committed is near pointless. Following the implementation and testing of the experimental setup, the researchers tabulated and analyzed the data through the lens of execution time. The researchers executed the novel loop detection structure against loops of length from 5 seconds up to 30 seconds while also varying the framerate parameter. The results were extremely encouraging. Firstly, the 24fps graph demonstrates that the total time taken to detect a loop which consists of the time taken to split the video into frames, write these frames, hash these frames, and perform the same rarely exceeded the length of the loop in our testing. Furthermore, we observed the time to hash and pattern match followed a roughly linear pattern with respect to the increasing length of the video.

Continuing further in the case of the 60fps video the researchers observed that the total time boomed at only the 20sec mark. This is understandably so as the amount of data influx is huge, that notwithstanding the time taken with respect to the hashing still maintained a roughly linear path only breaking minorly(though not as much as total time) at the 20 sec mark. This anomaly could be attributed as mentioned to the framing time and the limitations of the library responsible for the frame splitting, while the researchers’ proposal remained robust in terms of time complexity. Finally, when subject to a range of video resolutions ranging from 240p video (102,240 pixels) to 2160p(8,294,400 pixels) the results are as expected as both height and width increase along the X-axis leading to an exponentially growing graph. The notable aspect, however, is how the growth rate of the algorithm (blue line) is slower than the total time yielding the result that the dynamic aspect of the frame comparisons processes higher resolutions better than it does lower resolutions. The time taken for the Hashing + Pattern Matching decreases from 4.936ps per pixel for 240p video to 2.925ps per pixel for 2160p or 4k video.

Conclusion and Future Scope

To conclude, the proposed methods were implemented to prevent malpractices in an online environment, while augmenting the power in the hands of the proctor. As evidenced by the respective results the researchers were able to successfully detect and thwart the attack promptly while also being memory efficient. The researchers recognize that there are a few vulnerabilities that are still available to be exploited by prospective dishonest students such as the usage of mobile electronic devices. A possible solution would be to perform an eye-tracking analysis as well as verify of bright lights present in the vicinity of the exam taker. However, this is highly dependent on the quality of the feed and tends false positives. Additionally, other vulnerabilities involving multiple people in the same room are tackled by invigilator vigilance or the presence of auxiliary cameras in the form of mobile phones. We encourage improvements on the motif discovery aspects of our implementation as and when improvements are made to the algorithm involving ‘Distance Measuring to Compare Long Time Series’ as well as imbibing the concept of Time Series Primitives to aid in the real-world classification aspect of the subject.
