SDKL Hybrid ML Model to Predict Heart Disease Detection

M. Balamurugan,9

DOI: 10.1201/9781003430452-10

Abstract

The heart is the body’s most important organ for pumping blood throughout it. Heart disease is one of the leading causes of death today. Blood sugar levels that are too high damage most of the organs and are one of the main causes of heart disease. As more diseases emerge as potential mortalities for humans, clinical decision support systems (DSS) have shown their utility in assisting cardiologists and other healthcare professionals with clinical decision-making. The World Heart Federation (WHF) estimates that 391 million people worldwide already have heart disease, and that number will increase to 597 million by 2038. Clinical data analysis is a common barrier to detecting heart problems. We propose using hybrid machine learning techniques in this context to predict cardiac disease. Traditional machine learning methods that are taken into account include KNN, Support Vector Machine, Logistic Regression, and Decision Tree.

Introduction

Heart illnesses are a serious health danger that the human race is currently facing. The typical cause of heart disease is atherosclerotic blockage, which eventually results in diminished blood flow to the heart. This is the primary cause of heart attacks in humans. The American Heart Association (AHA) reports that heart disease affects more than one-third of the population. There are about 1,800,000 deaths each year due to cardiovascular disease, or 31% of all deaths, as reported by the WHO. Smoking, elevated cholesterol, and blood pressure levels increased risk could be caused by lifestyle choices and additional medical conditions like diabetes, obesity, and being overweight. A substantial portion of the decision- making process relies on machine learning (ML) algorithms because of the massive amounts of data they process. The velocity, volume, and diversity of the data are required before any data analysis techniques can be used. Predictive models that use ML for early diagnosis are useful in medical research. We recommend mixed machine learning approaches to predict heart disease because it has grown to be a serious health issue.

Objective

Many people’s lives could be saved if heart disease could be recognized early. Regular clinical data analysis is a major obstacle to correctly diagnosing heart conditions such as coronary artery disease, heart attacks, etc. ML model development to predict potential heart problems in the future deciding on risk variables that could cause cardiac illnesses in light of clinical facts to identify feature selection techniques and understand how they function (Akiba et al., 2019).

System Analysis

For the best study outcome, this section clarifies the intended objective, the calculations used, and the trial design.

Existing System

Heart plays a vital role in the human body. Because, when the heart stops its function, then it impacts all other parts of the body to stop their function properly. Thus, the prediction of heart disease has become crucial in the medical field. When compared to contemporary models in the same field, the outcomes are deemed to be superior. To discover trends in the data of people with heart disease, the XGboost algorithm is utilized.

Proposed System

It is now necessary to establish a framework to accurately predict heart problems due to the increased number of deaths brought on by heart disorders. The purpose of this research was to determine which ML algorithm is best at spotting heart problems. The performance of the ML algorithms KNN, SVM, Decision Tree, and Logistic Regression are measured within this framework. Algorithms would be selected for inclusion in the hybrid model for heart disease prediction based on their relative effectiveness (Cai et al., 2020). The following diagram depicts the overall design architecture of the project. The overall concept of the project is seen in Fig. 1.

Data collection and Pre-processing

The UCI repository is used to collect the data, and NumPy and pandas are imported to perform statistical analysis. The Python library for manipulating numbers is called Numerical Python (NumPy). Data structures for arrays and matrices are available in NumPy. Numerous mathematical processes, such as trigonometry, statistics, and algebraic operations, are among its capabilities. Here, NumPy is used for statistical calculations. Data science, machine learning, and data analysis functions are frequently carried out using the Python package Pandas. It is built on top of NumPy, another multi-dimensional array- supporting Python package. The Pandas module is even used in this instance of SciPy for statistical analysis, including determining the median, distribution, and average of columns, as well as working with Matplotlib to perform plotting operations. Basically, datasets are unusable for machine learning models because they have noise, missing data, and possibly an unworkable structure (Attia et al., 2019). Pre-processing is a crucial step in preparing data for machine learning models, as it improves the model’s accuracy and efficiency. The sklearn package is used to complete it. The sklearn package’s Minmax scaler transforms features by scaling each one to a specific range. In any case, a portion of the information may be erratic, for instance, may contain false information, insufficient information, or wrong information, thus we perform data preparation. Here, we are looking for any missing or void values.

Data Visualization

With the help of packages from Seaborn and Matplotlib, the data is shown visually. For its multi-platform toolbox for data visualization, Matplotlib is well known. The benefit of visual representation is that it gives us access to images, converting a vast number of datasets into visually appealing and understandable representations. A large variety of graph types, such as line, pie, bar, histogram, scatter, and more, are available in Matplotlib. A Python library called Seaborn makes it possible to create statistical graphs. It is built on matplotlib and is immediately mixed with Pandas data structures. Data assimilation is aided by Seaborn. Technically, it does mapping and data aggregation to make explanatory graphs. It offers graphing capabilities that deal with arrays and data tables that comprise entire datasets. Plotted graphs help us grasp the dataset.

Training and Testing Dataset Using Algorithms

There are a number of ways to determine whether or not your model is accurate. It is used to train models in SVM, Logistic Regression, Decision Tree, and KNN. Logistic regression is a statistical technique for predicting a categorical dependent variable from a set of independent variables. A random integer between 0 and 1 is generated instead of a binary 0 or 1 answer. Maybe it is true, may be it is not, maybe it is 0 or 1 or some other figure in between. Decision trees are built via an algorithmic procedure by unifying different ways of categorizing data sets depending on their context. the most well- known and fruitful supervised machine learning methods. The problems of classification and regression maybe tackled with the use of decision trees, a supervised unbounded learning approach. The KNN approach requires nothing in the way of setup time and provides substantial benefits for massive datasets. It is well-known that KNN outperforms sophisticated classification and regression techniques while being relatively simple to implement. An essential and powerful classification method, the KNN Classifier allows for the creation of predictive machine-learning models. In this case, the element’s classification is decided by how its neighbors are arranged. KNN categorizes fresh datasets based on the similarity level of previously stored items. To differentiate themselves from competing classification techniques, Support Vector Machines (SVM) choose the boundary that best measures the dissimilarity between neighboring classes. The SVM-derived decision border is the classifier with the biggest margin. As its name suggests, a linear SVM classifier draws a straight line between two categories (Alkeshoush et al., 2017). This means that each data point on one side of the margin represents one variety, while each data point on the other side represents a different variety. This suggests that there is potentially infinite material to analyze in terms of lineage. Each algorithm’s precision is rated.

Hybrid Model

We use a variety of methods to build a hybrid model that is highly accurate. The combined model operates based on the probability of the selected algorithms. To create the hybrid model SDKL, the methods Decision tree, SVM, Logistic Regression, and KNN are merged (Mohan et al., 2019). The train data is combined with the probabilities from each algorithm. The same is true for test data, which is stacked with known probabilities. The dataset has now been trained and evaluated using the hybrid model SDKL, and its accuracy has been determined.

Hybrid Model

Using this framework, we combined many algorithms for cardiac condition prediction using hybrid machine learning methods, yielding a hybrid model. When compared to other algorithms, the hybrid model SDKL provides the highest accuracy. Consequently, one may accurately forecast the likelihood of developing heart disease by utilizing the hybrid model. The accuracy values for different machine learning algorithms, when it was executed using Python, are as below.

Conclusion

Heart disease is a serious ailment that affects people all over the world. A person’s health is negatively impacted by both changing their way of life and not exercising. Differentiating the treatment of unprocessed heart-related medical data can aid in the early detection of heart function abnormalities and the possible life-saving effects. To organize the raw data and create a new, cutting-edge discernment on heart disorders, machine learning techniques were applied in this study. Heart disease prediction in the clinical setting is challenging yet crucial. In any case, if the sickness is identified earlier and preventive measures are put in place, the fatality rate can be greatly reduced. The clinical sector provides a huge selection of diagnostic techniques. However, it is believed that machine learning offers the highest level of precision. The effectiveness of the machine learning algorithms SVM, Logistic Regression, Decision Tree, and KNN is taken into account in the proposed framework (Kuppers et al., 2020). These algorithms are utilized to construct the hybrid model, which is the most accurate and is used for the exact diagnosis of cardiac disease. This work made use of data stored at the University of California, Irvine (UCI).

Optimization of Energy Aware Clustering For Wireless Sensor Network

N. Sasikala,10

DOI: 10.1201/9781003430452-11

Abstract

Wireless Sensor Networks (WSNs) are frequently utilized in a wide range of engineering applications for sensing and gathering data about an environment from a remote location. The routing protocols, which face significant energy challenges, facilitate the data flow among the nodes. To ensure energy balancing, the energy-aware routing is presented through the optimal cluster head (CH) selection process. We describe a routing protocol based on the Improved Muddy Fish Optimization Algorithm (IMFOA) in this study. The cluster head that corresponds to the intended objective function is then determined to have a minimum value and is known as the ideal cluster head. It depends on the cluster’s nodes’ proximity to one another, their energy levels, the cluster’s traffic density, and the delay in transferring data packets. Optimal routes are identified with the support of a Bio-geography based optimization (BBO) algorithm. Routes used for transmitting data should be shorter and less energy-consuming path. By placing this network in a simulation environment, the proposed IMFOA-based routing protocol is evaluated and related to their relevant protocols. The network lifetime is increased, and the message cost is reduced.

Keywords: WSN. Clustering, IMFOA, Routing, BBO algorithm

Introduction

In the fields of industry and the military, WSNs have great uses for monitoring human health and the environment (Mahajana et al., 2014). A WSN is a gathering of more amounts of low-cost, -power sensor nodes. The energy constraint should be considered to ensure successful communication in WSNs because it frequently appears to be a costly activity (Kumar and Kumar, 2016). It takes the combined efforts of many nodes to detect and collect those essential pieces of environmental information. Sensor nodes would use a lot of energy while collecting data during this time (Bagci and Yazici, 2013) while sensing, receiving, and transferring data. The battery and hardware resources for the sensor nodes are scarce, and networks suffer because of the nodes’ vast and haphazard deployment, their dynamic nature, and their unreliability (Chavan and Khiani, 2016).

Approaches that use the clustering methodology are used to achieve energy conservation (Haseeb et al., 2017). One sensor node serves as the Cluster Head (CH) for each cluster, and the other sensor nodes serve as member nodes. The CH gathers and compiles data from sensors in its cluster before sending it to the BS. For extending the lifespan of sensor networks, current research on the sensor routing problem (Prasanth and Pavalarajan, 2019) is primarily focused on protocols with energy-aware and leniency to sensor loss or energy exhaustion (Prasanth and Pavalarajan, 2017). However, the need to take the quality of service (QoS) into account is crucial for the development of wireless sensor networks, and the energy limitation highlights the challenges (Sasikala and Pavalarajan, 2022). Considering these factors, new concept design is proposed. Below, they are highlighted.

  • CH selection and the optimized portion of routing are done in two steps.
  • The enhanced muddy soil fish optimization technique is used to pick CH (IMFOA).
  • The suggested methods choose the best routes using the fitness function and the best CH nodes using a variety of criteria.
  • The multi-hop routing is done using Bio- geography based optimization (BBO) algorithm.
  • This type of optimization leads to better CH selection and the comparisons are made with the relevant algorithms.

Literature Survey

In topology control (Heinzelman et al., 2002) of WSN, clustering is a key concept that activates specific network nodes as cluster head (CH) nodes. The backbone network is made up of cluster head nodes, which can be switched to sleep mode to lower energy consumption on other member nodes. The network’s energy consumption is balanced by rotating through the cluster head nodes regularly. The network life cycle is also extended at the same time. A round is a collective term for every step taken to choose cluster head nodes and reassemble a network.

An updated variant of LEACH, LEACH-C (Latiff et al., 2007), uses the simulated annealing technique to choose the best CH nodes. The optimization method called particle swarm optimization (PSO) (Sasi et al., 2019) has been more well-liked in recent years. It could be utilized to find cluster head nodes and generate better outcomes. Recently proposed approaches that use PSO algorithms to pick the cluster head are PSO-SD (Singh and Lobiyal, 2012) and MOPSO (Hamid Ali et al., 2012). PSO is employed in previous research to localize cluster heads based on member node distance and energy remaining (Pavalarajan and Krishna Moorthy, 2014).

These PSO-based methods, however, frequently need extra calculations and complex settings. Nodes are organized into several clusters of fuzzy subsets before the network is launched (Priya et al., 2022; Lakshmi and Pavalarajan, 2022; Pavalarajan and Prasanth, 2019). All these sub-clusters will work simultaneously, reducing the size and processing time of each subset. Using a genetic algorithm (GA), Kong et al. (2018) proposed energy-aware routing that creates many stations for data transmission and reception. This technique costs more to build and uses more energy. This technique alters the routes in accordance with the location of the mobile sink to produce almost optimal paths. It aids in lowering the cost of the routes’ necessary rehabilitation. Additionally, it just obliges a small number of nodes to build routes. Establishing a few regulations is required.

Methodology

A WSN is molded with a group of E links and V nodes. V as sensor nodes in the group and E as links in the group, make up a model of a sensor network. The total nodes in WSN are indicated by the letter n, and the network is believed to be a linked graph. The network node’s position is indicated by the letter i. The node at position I is denoted by the symbol N(i). The CH node is indicated as and the sink node is indicated as. Every time a need for data transmission occurs, the network’s clustering process is initiated. Using a passive clustering strategy, the network’s nodes are grouped. In the first phase of the clustering process, all network nodes are in their INITIAL mode. The procedure for choosing the CH is described in Fig. 1.

The CH selection procedure is carried out utilizing an optimization algorithm once the residual energy has been delivered to all nodes. Each node’s fitness value is calculated depending on its distance from the sink node, degree, and energy. The IMFOA technique is then proposed, and the node with the best fitness is chosen as the CH node. Greater node degree guarantees load-balanced processing while extraordinary residual energy retains the network’s lifespan longer.

The network’s energy consumption is influenced by the separation between the transmitting and receiving CH nodes. Whenever a data packet of size is transferred to the CH node, energy dissipation is indicated by the symbol, which is expressed as in Equation (1).

(1)
edis (N(CH)l) = eelect  × ℘

where indicates the energy lost in nodes as a result of the presence of power amplifiers and electronic components. The energy of a sensor node is modernized each time data is sent by the node or received by the node. Equation (2a) shows the modernized equation for member nodes, while Equation (2b) shows the energy modernize equation for CH node .

(2a)
e(t + 1)(N(i)) = e(i)(N(i)) − eeis(N(i))

(2b)
e(t + 1)(N(CH)l) = e(t)(N(CH)l) − edis(N(CH)l)

where represents the time instantly, while stands for the energy node residual state . Up until it is exhausted, the node’s remaining energy is updated. The energy of nodes is considered while choosing the best cluster head for clusters.

The algorithm aims to choose the node that is closest to the sink, has the highest node degree, and has the most residual energy. Thus, using these parameters as in Equation (3), the fitness function for the maximizing issue is created.

(3)
$$\begin{array}{l} {FF_{CH} = ND(N(i)) + e^{\text{init~}}(N(i))} \\ {+ \lbrack 1 - (P(N(i)) - P(N(S)))\rbrack} \\ {+ \lbrack 1 - (P(N(i)) - P(N(i + 1)))\rbrack} \\ {+ \lbrack 1 - (P(N(i)) - P(N(i + 2)))\rbrack} \\ {+ \ldots + \lbrack 1 - (P(N(i)) - P(N(i + n)))\rbrack} \\ \end{array}$$

Maximizing the fitness function is the goal. The iteration of optimization terminates and the related node is chosen as the CH when the fitness function value reaches its maximum. The IMFOA provides a better answer to challenging engineering issues.

The volume of food that a fish consumes is based on the enhancement attained in its objective function in the current iteration. The weight update formula is given in Equation (4).

(4)
$$\omega_{i}(l + 1) = \omega_{i}(l) + \frac{\Delta f_{i}}{\max\Delta f}$$

weight of fish, at generation t at present, and stands for the difference in the objective function between fish i’s previous and subsequent positions. For the fishes at the same place, this difference is zero.

When there is no difference in objective function (i.e. ), instinctive collective movement happens where the individual movement of fish occurs. Thus, the fish that show improvement in their fitness can induce the movement of the swarm. In this condition, the obtained direction designed from the influence of the movements engaged by the fish and the fresh position of the fish is computed using Equations (5) and (6).

(5)
$${\overset{\rightarrow}{I}}^{t} = \frac{{\sum_{i = 1}^{N}\Delta}{\overset{\rightarrow}{p}}_{i}\Delta f_{i}}{{\sum_{i = 1}^{N}\Delta}f_{i}}$$

(6)
$${\overset{\rightarrow}{p}}_{i}^{t + 1} = {\overset{\rightarrow}{p}}_{i}^{t} + {\overset{\rightarrow}{I}}^{t}$$

The increasing weight of swarm indicates that the search process moving toward the success of the objective function. For searching in other regions for food, the “radius” of the swarm must decline. Thus, if the swarm weight is not increasing or decreasing, to enable the investigation of new areas, the radius should be increased. For the narrowing of the region occupied by the swarm, the centroid concept is taken. This is calculated by taking a biased average position of all fish according to the fish weights. This is given in Equation (7).

(7)
$${\overset{\rightarrow}{p}}_{\text{avg~}}t = \frac{{\sum_{i - 1}^{N}{\overset{\rightarrow}{p}}_{i}}\omega_{i}^{t}}{{\sum_{i - 1}^{N}{\overset{\rightarrow}{p}}_{i}}\omega_{i}^{t}\,}$$

After the clustering process, the routes inside the network need to be found. The routes for data transmission are formed by connecting the cluster heads and forming links. The data gathered by the CH nodes are transmitted through these links. Several paths can be formed for transmitting data from a CH node to the sink node. Hence the optimal path must be selected among them. For selecting the optimal routes for data transmission, the optimization algorithm can be used. The selected path should be the shortest as well as less energy-consuming path. Hence the optimal paths are determined by considering the factors like energy consumption and distance. The fitness function for optimal route computation is given in Equation (8).

(8)
$$\begin{array}{l} {FF_{route}} \\ {= {\sum\limits_{i = 1}^{m}\left( {e\left( {N{(\text{CH})}_{i}} \right) + \left( {P\left( {N{(\text{CH})}_{i}} \right) - P\left( {N{(\text{CH})}_{i + 1}} \right)} \right)} \right)}} \\ \end{array}$$

The optimum fitness function is computed using the BBO algorithm. BBO algorithm is developed from the inspiration of migration of biological species between habitats. The species migrate from one habitat to another based on several factors that suit their living. These factors are seasonal changes, environmental conditions, food availability, etc. Habitat Suitability Index (HSI) and Suitability Index Variables (SIV) are the metrics used in this algorithm which controls the migration process. The migration process happened in two types; immigration and emigration. For the optimization problem, the SIVs are taken as the population and HIS is equivalent to the fitness function. The immigration rate ( and emigration rate 0 plays a significant role in the algorithm which can be computed using Equations (9) and (10) respectively for species .

(9)
$$\lambda_{i} = I\left( {1 - \frac{K(i)}{N}} \right)$$

(10)
$$\mu_{i} = E\left( \frac{K(i)}{N} \right)$$

where E and I are maximum emigration and immigration rate values respectively. The habitat set is denoted as in Equation (11).

(11)
$$H = \begin{bmatrix} \left\lbrack {e\left( {N{(\text{CH})}_{11}} \right),P\left( {N{(\text{CH})}_{11}} \right)} \right\rbrack & \left\lbrack {e\left( {N{(\text{CH})}_{21}} \right),P\left( {N{(\text{CH})}_{21}} \right)} \right\rbrack & \ldots & \left\lbrack {e\left( {N{(\text{CH})}_{m1}} \right),P\left( {N{(\text{CH})}_{m1}} \right)} \right\rbrack \\ \left\lbrack {e\left( {N{(\text{CH})}_{12}} \right),P\left( {N{(\text{CH})}_{12}} \right)} \right\rbrack & \left\lbrack {e\left( {N{(\text{CH})}_{22}} \right),P\left( {N{(\text{CH})}_{22}} \right)} \right\rbrack & \ldots & \left\lbrack {e\left( {N{(\text{CH})}_{m2}} \right),P\left( {N{(\text{CH})}_{m2}} \right)} \right\rbrack \\ \ldots & \ldots & \ldots & \ldots \\ \left\lbrack {e\left( {N{(\text{CH})}_{1l}} \right),P\left( {N{(\text{CH})}_{1l}} \right)} \right\rbrack & \left\lbrack {e\left( {N{(\text{CH})}_{2l}} \right),P\left( {N{(\text{CH})}_{2l}} \right)} \right\rbrack & \ldots & \left\lbrack {e\left( {N{(\text{CH})}_{ml}} \right),P\left( {N{(\text{CH})}_{ml}} \right)} \right\rbrack \\ \end{bmatrix}$$

The HSI value for each habitat set is computed using Equation (13). HSI is computed for the elements of each row. After computing HSI, the elite habitats are taken and then the non-elite habitats are considered for migration in next iteration. The habitat set from row iand row j are selected randomly and they are applied in migration process. Then the fitness in next iteration is computed. This procedure can be continued till it attains satisfaction of this condition.

Results and Discussion

The performance of the proposed optimized data routing with energy-aware clustering is analyzed in MATLAB simulation software. 100 nodes are deployed in a WSN that is randomly distributed. By analyzing the metrics of energy usage, message cost, and network lifetime, the planned task is assessed.

Figure 2 shows a comparison of network lifetimes. For many approaches, including LEACH, Greedy algorithm-based routing, BBO routing, and IMFOA clustering, the number of living nodes in rounds is shown in a graph. The lifetime of network Plot demonstrates that the network’s lifespan is shorter with the LEACH protocol, whereas the clustering process in IMFOA possesses an increased lifetime.

Figure 3 shows the message cost for various techniques. The number of transmissions that took place in the network is represented by message cost. The graph shows that the IMFOA clustering reduces the number of transmissions when compared to the LEACH clustering approach.

Conclusion

The optimal CH selection and optimal path detection for energy conservation in WSN are presented in this work. The newly submitted IMFOA-based optimal CH selection considers network residual energy, degree, distance from the sink node, and other network nodes. This IMFOA overcomes the disadvantage presented in the conventional MFOA (Veluchamy et al. (2021) and FOA. Then the optimal paths for transferring data from the CH node to the sink node can be identified using BBO algorithm. The IMFOA approach is assessed using simulation in a WSN scenario with 100 nodes deployed. The evaluation outcomes prove that the proposed work combining IMFOA clustering and BBO routing helps to reduce the consumption of energy and extends the network period. In addition, the clustering process reduces unwanted transmissions and the detection shortest path reduces the number of hops with the deduction of transmission cost.

Next-Gen Technologies in Computational Intelligence [NGTC-2023] PID 62 Prediction of Corneal Ulcer Using Deep Convolutional Neural Network and Support Vector Machine Classification Model

S. Janet Grace Susila11

E-mail: Janetgracesuila2020.research@spiher.ac.in

DOI: 10.1201/9781003430452-12

Abstract

Corneal ulcer disease detection and treatment can avoid vision loss. A red, watery, and bloodshot eye; intense pain in the eye; and pus or other discharge are all symptoms. Data mining improves predictive diagnosis and finds the most common cause of bacteria. Data mining techniques (DMTs) can predict medical datasets early to save lives. Real-world applications used many medical datasets from many sources. Machine learning can predict disease and spot corneal ulcers. An eye ailment recognition system is proposed to identify the ailments of the cornea of an eye. Pre-processing, feature extraction, and classification are all part of the proposed system. Following simulation results showed that the proposed model shows high accuracy rate98.43% precision 96.78%, recall 96.60%, and f-measure 92%.

Keywords: Convolution Neural Network, Support Vector Machine, Global Average Pooling, Softmax Function

Introduction

Corneal ulcers are a very common and difficult-to- diagnose condition that can cause vision loss. There are accurate methods for analysis of corneal ulcers which can help guide treatment decisions. Cornea is the clear covering over your eye, protecting it from dust and germs but also helping you see. It fights off infection by circulating antibodies and white blood cells cleared by the immune system, as well as producing a layer of mucus over it to protect against minor scratches or abrasion. If this layer gets damaged or inflamed, however, it can lead to ulcers known as corneal ulcers. There are several different causes of corneal ulcers including trauma, eye irritation (such as chemicals), infections, and vascular problems within the cornea itself (such as diabetes). Depending on the cause, these conditions can lead to dull vision loss if not treated properly.

Corneal ulcers are typically detected by an ophthalmologist using a slit-lamp examination and the proper fluorescein dye. Ophthalmologists can only do this if the image in question has been properly stained, making it difficult to make an accurate prediction regarding the prognosis of a corneal ulcer. The possibility of predicting the outcome of a corneal ulcer on the other hand, it is not possible to determine or detect the ulcer size with any degree of accuracy. The correct diagnosis of an ulcer on the cornea and the precise segmentation of the ulcer region are both necessary steps in the process of empirically determining the severity of a corneal ulcer. Because of this, it would be beneficial for medical diagnostics if the corneal ulcer could be reliably detected and automatically segmented (Iorliam et al., 2021). Knowing how to differentiate different types of eye problems is key to treating them effectively. Researchers are working hard to develop an AI system that can recognize and differentiate the eye region, in addition to categorizing various types of eye problems. There are a few different approaches (Campagnini et al., 2022; Karuna & Shilpy, 2022; Kim & Armstrong, 2022; Mujeeb Rahman et al., 2022)that have been published, which can be used to determine the location of corneal ulcers and then divide them up into individual ulcers. This image processing technique involves the use of a digital camera to capture an image of the patient’s face in order to determine the presence of corneal ulcers. After cropping, recognizing faces, and identifying eyes, this particular image-processing method employs convolution neural network (CNN) modeling to distinguish between corneal ulcers and non-corneal ulcers based on these characteristics (Padhy et al., 2022). We propose a novel automated eye ailment recognition system employing machine learning techniques. The proposed algorithm detects the presence and location of corneal ulcers automatically, by analyzing images collected from patients from multiple angles.

Related works

Corneal ulcers are an inflammatory reaction that takes place in the cornea and is a common form of eye illness. Corneal ulcers are characterized by thickening, scarring, and tenderness (Rampat et al., 2021). The infectious agents that include viruses, fungus, bacteria, and acanthamoeba are among the primary contributors to developing CU. Extreme pain, drooping eyelids, and sensitivity to light are common symptoms associated with this condition Learning and memory are both dependent to a significant degree on the coordinated activity of the neurons in the brain (Roshini & Kiran, 2022). In addition, it has been demonstrated that the efficient processing of information in neuronal networks requires the dependable propagation of synchronous neural activity (Huang et al., 2022).

An examination of the regional synchronization of spontaneous fMRI data is one of the most common applications of the regional homogeneity (ReHo) metric. In prior studies that assessed the levels of brain activity in persons who have vision impairments, it was found to be beneficial (Wani et al., 2021). The purpose of this research was to determine whether individuals suffering from CU had symptoms of abnormally synchronized brain activity and whether any differences were observed with respect to the physiological correlates of these behaviors.

Proposed Method

We propose a novel automated eye ailment recognition system employing machine learning techniques like Deep Convolution Neural Network (DCNN)and Support Vector Machine (SVM).

Pre-processing

Images were retrieved from the internet, and they ranged in quality, resolution, and file format. These images were reduced to 256 x 256 in order to enhance quality and simplify feature extraction. The initial eye photos’ size needs to be reduced from 64 x 64 to 256 x 256 in order to start. There are a lot of websites with their pictures that show the full spectrum of sickness but we don’t have time for all of those changes so we’ll use the least usable one as an example. After photos have been resized the cropping tool is next utilized to remove any faces that contain eyes which are followed by applying a median filter smoothing effect. The median filter is a method that is utilized to lessen the jarring noise that is present in an image while at the same time maintaining the integrity of the image’s essential elements and border regions. When this filter is applied to an image, the value of the median intensity of pixels that are next to the pixel being processed will substitute for the original value of this pixel. A convolution neural network can then be trained using data from these treated images after they have been treated (CNN). This gives us automatic differentiation between corneal ulcer illness and other types of ulcers that do not impact the cornea automatically.

CNN-SVM Classification

CNN-SVM is a combination of CNN and SVM. The structure of the model used by CNN has been changed from the traditional CNN model structure to a connected network with a global average. This adjustment has the impact of decreasing the quantity of CNN model parameters as well as the amount of time it takes to calculate results. Second, rather than using the Softmax function during the testing phase, the nonlinear Support Vector Machine (SVM) is used. The accuracy of finding out which category an image belongs to has greatly increased with this augmented CNN-SVM technique in its analysis process as shown in Fig. 1.

The CNN-SVM method that has been enhanced uses a model, and Figure 1 illustrates a simplified form of that model. A feature extraction layer, an output layer for the estimation of classifications, and an input layer make up most of the updated CNN-SVM method. These layers are responsible for the majority of the method functionality. The standard CNN has 23 fully linked layers; these two layers are piled one on top of another in this structure. Figure 2 illustrates their overall design in its entirety.

A conventional CNN that possesses a completely connected network can be seen as an extension of a single-layer feed-forward network (also known as convolution or fully connected), which is typically used as the model. A flatten function can be used to convert a multidimensional array with dimensions of 6 x 6 x 32 into a 1 x 1 x 32 array, which allows for more efficient processing. Because of this, the array can now be used as an input for the model. In most cases, a completely connected layer will have an underlying hidden layer that is two or three tiers deep.

The output layer, also known as the output class, is made up of 256 nodes. Each of the two hidden layers has 256 trainable parameters because they both have 512 nodes. Given that these three layers are all connected by an activation function, there are therefore 512 node-activations that can be used for training since this particular neural network depth has only five layers that can be stored within a fully linked layer is 724,234.


$$\begin{array}{l} {(6 \times 6 \times 32 + 1) \times 512 + (512 + 1) \times 256 + (256} \\ {\text{~+~1)~}10 = 724,234} \\ \end{array}$$

The process of joining components can be complex and require a significant amount of computational power. The typical CNN struggles to conduct calculations accurately when working with high-res images, due to errors in the completely linked layer. The solution that has been suggested for this issue involves getting rid of the completely linked sector and replacing it with a technology solution that is based on the idea of pooling the average from all over the world. The global average pooling feature map size should be 1 x 10, which is the same as the output of a fully linked layer. Since the CNN calculation requires a fully linked layer, all layers will have identical input and output maps following the training phase. The produced two-dimensional representation will have dimensions of 1 x 1 x 10. The output feature map has dimensions of 1 x 1 x 10, whereas the global average pooling layer has dimensions of 6 x 6 x 32. To obtain a value of 1, the value of 6 x 6 x 32 must be decreased to 1 x 1 x 10.

A square with dimensions of 6 x 6 x 10 replaces the image with dimensions of 6632. To better meet the requirements of this application, a 1 x 1 x 3210 transitional convolution layer has been created. The Same padding mode is utilized by the convolution kernel with a stride of 1 and a size of 1. Additionally, the kernel has a size of 1. The transitional convolution layer is in charge of changing the input feature map by either increasing or decreasing the number of output channels while maintaining the same overall image size. Figure 2 shows that there are 32 convolution kernels and 32 input channels. Since the element map is a sum of 32 info channels, we need to decrease the size of the component map from 140 to 10 by including 3 unique convolution bit bunches that contain 16 convolution pieces each. Within the 16 convolution kernel group, there are a total of (32 x 11) 320 distinct convolution kernels. A kernel’s output value must be greater than 0 to ensure that it does not contain connected components, which gives it a value of 10.

A novel spatial domain representation has made it possible to use convolution filters. Using 32 66 input feature maps as the basis, we were able to carry out a convolution calculation using 32 x 1 1 filters. Even if the size of the input feature map is maintained throughout the 11 convolution procedure, we are still able to collect the entire set of 32 x 6 maps. This is a result of the input map being confounded with itself. After that, the data from the 32 maps with 66 features are combined to create a single map with 66 features and 66 features in total. Convolution kernels are used to construct the ten feature maps that are produced as the procedure’s final output. By combining data from a wide range of sources, the Global Average is more accurate. The global average is calculated by averaging the ten distinct pooling kernels, each of which is represented by a map with 66 attributes. For real-world situations with a large number of possible outcomes, this technology system can be used to estimate probabilities with greater precision. Each input array channel will be combined by the Global Average Pooling Layer. This is accomplished by generating a single value that represents the overall average of each input feature map by taking the mean of all the channels. If it is to be used as a global average pooling layer, the same number of channels will be applied to each input image. Its size, stride, and padding mode are all set to 6 x 6 (or 66). Without a doubt, the best approach is the CNN variant that makes use of global average pooling. This is because the standard CNN model makes use of a layer that is entirely connected. The CNN model will be more accurate because global average pooling significantly reduces the total number of training parameters. Just 330 variables are required to complete the period of this situation that involves joining the midpoints from everywhere in the world.

In order to improve the performance of deep learning, it has been proposed that a CNN- SVM model can accomplish the same task with a reduced number of connections between the layers. By improving the model and introducing new techniques, Upstarts has made some impressive advancements in AI technology while keeping aspects of traditional AI techniques alive.

Raw Data Input Layer

The first stage in the process is normalizing and standardizing the data. The purpose of this step is to make sure that there are no outliers that would cause problems later on when training the network. All values are first squared, then divided by the mean value so that each dot on the grid represents an average value.

Feature Extraction Layer

A computer program that can learn from examples is called a deep learning network. A tried-and-true feature extraction layer that has been maintained throughout the process serves as the foundation for the CNN model. The network is constructed using a variety of convolution, activation, and pooling layers. Convolution layers, initiation layers, and pooling layers might be stacked to make a profound component extraction layer, yet the particulars will rely upon the indicative instrument being utilized.

Using the Softmax function is typical practice in order to standardize the calculation and, as a result, find a solution to this issue. Results and Discussions

In order to carry out our computations, we use a technique known as 5-fold cross-validation on both the original dataset and the one that we have updated. This method is applied to both datasets simultaneously. However, unlike the previous approaches, our method does not require the same experimental setting, dataset, or learning task in order to function well. The vast majority of the published instances of corneal ulcer segmentation make use of photos that have been stained with fluorescein. Making comparisons to other cases is difficult and time-consuming as a direct result of this, which is a direct consequence of this. Although diagnosing corneal ulcer disease based purely on observable symptoms is notoriously challenging, our approach yields favorable outcomes. The findings of the experiments indicate that the solution performs better than other modern methods, which is demonstrated by the fact that the solution is superior.

The cornea Fluorescein is used to stain 712 of the collection images, and these may be found in the Sustech-Sysu archive. You can view the raw images that were included in the dataset Images capturing the ocular surfaces were collected from patients of various corneal ulcer degrees at the Zhongshan Ophthalmic Center at Sun Yat-sen University.

Tensor flow, a framework for deep learning, was applied to carry out this particular experiment. Our neural networks were trained with the assistance of a processor with a clock speed of 2.20 GHz provided by the Intel Core i7- 8750H and a graphics card provided by NVIDIA with a clock speed of 4 GB. With CUDA10.0 and CUDNN7.6’s assistance, we were able to successfully finish the model’s training on schedule. In the course of the process of training the model, the dataset was segmented in a way that was completely random. In order to train the model, each of these datasets was utilized in a standalone fashion. Images with a resolution of 256 by 256 by 3 were shown to the input network while the experiment was being conducted. Optimizer Adam was selected to be utilized, and a starting learning rate of 0.0001 was decided upon for him.

In this, a 5-fold cross-validation test is run on a total of 40 epochs of data. CNN-SVM provides better detection and segmentation of corneal ulcers. These networks were used to detect and segment corneal ulcers. In this section, we give the findings of our experiments, which include training and validating the entire dataset. The total dataset includes both images that have not been edited and those that have been edited, hence this section presents both sets of results.

Conclusions

In this paper, an image of the person’s face can be used to accurately diagnose corneal ulcer disease using the system. The diagnosis is made based on the image of the person’s face. CNNs are utilized in the execution of this method. Our method can automatically classify the eye area based on the facial image by utilizing feature-based cascade classifiers. The conventional method is competent to recognize corneal ulcer disease in images taken with a digital camera designed for other purposes. In order to determine whether or not corneal illness is present, several structures of the eye, in conjunction with the CNN approach, are evaluated. If the disease is present, the ulcer region will be segmented automatically when we implement this technique. Methods of data augmentation are also used in order to improve the total size of the dataset as well as the visual diversity of the training data. This is done in order to prepare the dataset for machine learning applications. How the original image was processed compared to how the enhanced image was handled is visible to be a significant improvement.

Efficient PHOA Based Routing Network Protocol for IoT-Sem System

P. Priyadharshini,12

DOI: 10.1201/9781003430452-13

Abstract

Internet of Things (IoT) is a system of machines, computing devices, electronic equipment, and different sensors. It forms a network where the transmission of device-related data can be accomplished. The devices in IoT are connected through wireless links. The smart energy management (SEM) system can be implemented using IoT for managing energy consumption in industrial applications, home applications, and commercial buildings. Demand response energy management in industries and home applications is a vital thing required for the reduction of energy costs. In IoT based SEM system, the lifetime of the sensors is a greater concern. The lifetime of the network can be maximized by introducing energy-efficient data transmission in the network. Therefore, a routing protocol based on Pony Herd Optimization Algorithm (PHOA) for IoT based SEM system is proposed in this work. The proposed approach is created to meet a scaled WSN’s efficiency requirements. The suggested protocol takes advantage of clustering to select cluster heads to transfer data from source to endpoint, creating a scalable network and enhancing PHOA performance-based routing protocol. This number of data transmission and energy consumption can be reduced. The proposed PHOA with IoT based SEM performance is evaluated by analyzing transmission delay, network lifetime, and energy consumption. The simulation results are validated by comparing them with the existing methods TEAR and ETASA.

Keywords: Internet of Things, Smart home, Energhy management, Demand response, Energy consumption, Wireless sensor network

Introduction

The smart energy management SEM system provides the information about energy consumption of the devices involved in the environment to the end-user. The end-user can control the devices to change their action for maintaining the supply/demand balance. SEM performs demand side management, peak load reduction and reduced energy cost. Demand response (DR) based smart energy management (SEM) performs effective control to reduce energy consumption and peak loads to maintain a balance among supply and demand of electrical energy [1]. The requirement of implementing demand response management is to obtain better utilization of energy from the power supply for reducing energy costs. In IoT based SEM system, the lifetime of the sensors is a greater concern. PHOA with IoT based SEM method is proposed to enhance the lifetime of a network using optimization-based clustering and energy- efficient routing scheme in WSN-based IoT.

Literature Survey

Smart buildings are the latest developing technologies to minimize energy consumption using energy management techniques. Hence the smart grids (SG) are designed where the electrical devices, energy sources, smart meters, data processing elements, and controllers are interconnected [4]. All the components presented in the SG should communicate with each other for sending the necessary information for implementing the energy management process. Lin, Jie, et al. explains SG as Smart grids (SG) are designed where the electrical devices, energy sources, smart meters, data processing elements, and controllers are interconnected. Implementing energy management system says Wang, Xiuwang, Xinna Mao, and Hossein Khodaei. Ali, H., et al., proposes work with smart cities deployment is presented which employed Automatic Meter Reading (AMR) system using Zigbee mesh WSN [5]. This method presents DR Management and reduces peak loads.

Methodology

In this work, SEM system with IoT-based WSN is designed with effective routing schemes. A typical SEM system with WSN contains the electrical appliances in the field, the associated sensors to read the measures and the controllers for taking necessary action [3]. The details of the appliances measured by the sensors are transmitted to the cloud server and among the appliances inside the network. The structure of the proposed SEM with WSN and the data transmission by sensors are deliberated in consecutive sections. Then the traffic and data routing protocol is presented for the WSN to overcome the issues mentioned in Section 1.

Design of IoT based WSN for SEM

In this work, energy management in a residential building is considered. A smart home is implemented with IoT based WSN and connected to the SG. The sensors transmit data through wireless communication channel [8].

System Model

The proposed IoT based WSN is designed to implement energy management in the home, which aims to reduce the energy consumption of home appliances in peak hours. The energy consumption of different appliances in the home is different. Hence the energy consumption of one device must be known by all appliances of the network. If one appliance is essentially needed at a particular time slot, irrespective of energy consumption, the other high energy-consuming device with less need must be turned OFF. Thus the energy consumption of the home appliances is maintained not to exceed the peak load. Usually in home the electrical appliances are of two types; frequently operating devices (FOD) and occasionally operating devices (OOD). For example, the living room electrical appliances like fans, TV, AC, and computers are considered as FOD and the other devices like, kitchen appliances, washing machines, heaters, and electric pumps are considered as OOD. These devices are connected to the sensor nodes through wireless links. All the nodes of the network are interconnected. Thus a wireless sensor network is formed. A typical IoT based SEM with home appliances presenting in various rooms along with the nodes is depicted in Fig. 1.

SEM is implemented in this network for demand management. While implementing, network issues should also be considered. Hence in this work, energy-efficient routing for IoT based WSN is presented which is based on traffic and data-aware routing.

Operation and Data Transmission

The device state transition based on the available energy of the supply source is the most critical data to be communicated in the network. When the demand for smart home appliances is very large, the following actions can be taken.

  1. Turning OFF unwanted appliances.
  2. Reducing the load of some appliances and thereby ensuring their total energy consumption does not exceed the peak value.
  3. Turning OFF the appliance that consuming more excessive energy

Based on the received message the starting time of the appliance is controlled using a control algorithm. In control algorithm, the command for starting the appliance immediately can be transmitted or the appliance is started after a time delay if sufficient energy is not available. Thus the SEM process is implemented with the control algorithm.

Proposed Routing Protocol

Inspiration of Pony-based Optimization

Pony herds’ hierarchical organization serves as the primary source of inspiration for the Pony Optimization Algorithm. Ponies have adapted to coexist in herds. The formation of a stable hierarchical structure, or “pecking order,” is crucial to lowering aggression and boosting social cohesiveness, as it is with many animals that live in big groups. This is typically a linear system, although not necessarily [9]. Pony A may be dominant over Pony B, who may be dominant over Pony C, yet Pony C may be dominant over Pony A in non-linear hierarchies. Ponies behave hierarchically when they are in a herd; the more important animals eat and drink first. When low-status animals eat last, they might not get enough to eat, and if there isn’t much grain available, higher-status ponies might prevent lower-status ponies from eating at all.

Results and Discussions

The performance of the proposed traffic-aware and delay-aware routing technique for IoT based WSN is observed through simulation results. A simulation setup with different home appliances connected with sensor nodes is deployed. The performance is evaluated using MATLAB simulation software. An IoT system with 20 devices and 20 sensor nodes is arranged where the nodes are unevenly distributed. The nodes are connected to the home appliances and SMU of the IoT system is also connected to a sensor node. For communicating data in the system, wireless links are used in the range of 100 x 100 m. The simulation settings used for evaluating the proposed work with a packet size of about 512 bits. To validate the proposed work, the comparative analysis is performed with TEAR and ETASA methods. The network lifetime is observed for the proposed work and depicted in Fig. 5. From the figure, it is noted that the nodes die after 3000 rounds and 4500 rounds in TEAR technique and ETASA technique respectively.

In PHOA optimizer method, traffic rate and data critical level are considered and delay is set accordingly. Hence, less energy is consumed in the proposed work. The employment of the proposed technique increases the network lifetime where the nodes are alive even after 5000 rounds with 3J taken for initial energy of nodes. The energy consumption for number of state transitions is depicted in Fig. 5. The graph shows that energy consumption is less in the proposed work compared with TEAR and ETASA protocols. Energy consumption in this work is achieved in PHOA by setting a delay for data transmission. As the delay is assigned based on the type of data and traffic of the node, higher energy consumption is achieved here.

In TEAR and ETASA methods, the delay is not assigned according to the data critical level. In the PHOA-SEM based proposed work, when the data criticality level is high, less delay is set.

Figure 6 shows energy consumption for different traffic rate. When traffic rate is high, more energy is consumed in data transmission. In TEAR and ETASA methods, the energy consumption is decreased when traffic rate increases. In the proposed work, along with the traffic rate, critical level of data is considered. Based on these two factors, delay is set for data transmission. For high traffic rate, more delay is set. Thus the energy consumed for the proposed PHOA based data transmission is reduced.

Conclusion

In this work, PHOA with IoT based SEM scheme is presented for lifetime maximization in IoT based WSN used for SEM system. The proposed routing algorithm enables to send the critical data in the network without any delay. In the proposed PHOA method, delay is set for transmitting data, based on its critical level and traffic rate at the node. The routing algorithm helps in reducing the number of transmissions in the network. Moreover, the delay for critical data transmission is set to be low. Hence the critical data are sent without missing. This ensures data transmission accuracy in the network. The proposed work is evaluated by simulating the network and observing the metrics like energy consumption, delay, and network lifetime. The results of PHOA with IoT based SEM scheme show that for nodes with less traffic, less energy is consumed. It is also observed that when the data critical level is low, less energy is consumed. The proposed SEM work gives better performance when compared with TEAR and ETASA methods. In the future, security concerns and methods for enhancing security in the proposed work can be presented.

Enhancement of Security and Performance of Multimedia Data Transmission Over Fog

Ayushi13

E-mail: Ayushi.hce@gmail.com; manishaagarwal18@yahoo.com

DOI: 10.1201/9781003430452-14

Abstract

Present research is focusing on the security and performance enhancement of graphical content in fog environment. Here image data has been split after performing a watermarking operation and data has been processed by visual encryption mechanism. The watermarking is making content copyrighted where as splitting is breaking data into multiple parts to allow transmission from fog and core cloud. On the other hand visual encryption has been integrated to improve security. Need for visual cryptography is growing day by day in order to perform privacy protection in multimedia applications. Present paper is focused on the enhancement of privacy protection of multimedia content using watermarking along with visual cryptography approach. The cover image is processed with a watermarked image, and then halftoning is done on the watermarked image in order to limit pixel expansion. This work is being suggested. Image with halftones is partitioned using extended VCS into two shares. When sharing, a QR code may be included, and the compression of QR-based shares can be accomplished using a lossless compressing process. After then, this information is sent to the recipient from the sender. After receiving data on the receiver end the quality of the image has been checked after decryption. The PSNR and SSIM of image is considered in case of conventional and proposed work to assure the quality of image at the time of visual cryptography. Proposed work is supposed to provide better PSNR and SSIM as compared to conventional scheme.

Keywords: Image processing, Fog Computing, Watermarking, Data splitting, Visual cryptography, PSNR, SSIM

Introduction

Recently, a new category of digital watermarking systems has been created that use ideas from visual cryptography (VC) to protect watermarked material. Furthermore, it is possible to apply VC- based watermarking to strengthen the identification of an extracted watermark from attacked photos. When using VC for watermarking, for instance, the binary logo is encrypted into two noise-like binary shares before being embedded into the host picture. Both shares are distributed to the public, but one is kept secret as a watermark share (Wang, 2011). The other portion stands in for a public watermark portion and is being integrated into the host picture by a typical watermarking approach that works in either the spatial or frequency domain of the host image.

Visual Cryptography

Visual Cryptography is a specialized encryption technology that divides a hidden picture into numerous layers in order to conceal information inside the image. Each layer stores a certain amount of information. When the receiver aligns layers, the hidden information becomes visible to human eyes and does not need any complicated computations to decipher (Hsu et al., 2007). A kind of encryption known as visual cryptography disassembles confidential pictures into several separate pieces. To reconstruct the original picture, these shares are either digitally or physically overlapping one another, which eliminates the need for complicated mathematical procedures or extra gear. Throughout its history, visual cryptography has spawned a plethora of distinct iterations, each of which proposes unique solution issues or is designed to meet a specific set of Existing review publications on the subject only addresses some of the several forms of visual cryptography, and they do not compare the different systems (Feng et al., 2008).

To encrypt visual data (images, text, etc. ) in a manner that can be decrypted by human beings, a cryptographic approach known as “visual cryptography” has been developed (without computers). In 1994, Moni Naor & Adi Shamir created the first method of visual cryptography. The picture was divided into n parts, and only those who had all n parts could piece them back together to reveal the original. To implement this in practice, you may print each share on a separate transparency and stack them on top of one another (Hsu et al., 2012). In their method, even if n-1 people share a photograph, no one will learn anything about the original. Fog Computing

A dispersed computing architecture known as fog computing puts data, processing, storage, and applications in the “fog,” also known as the space that lies between the data source and the cloud. Fog computing and edge computing both provide some of the advantages and capabilities of cloud computing to sites that are physically closer to the areas where data is being created and utilized. Because of the similarities that exist between the two concepts, the phrases “fog computing” and “edge computing” are often interchanged with one another. The following is a list of some of the advantages that FC provides:

  • When fog computing is used, the amount of data that is uploaded to the cloud is cut down, which results in cost savings linked to bandwidth charges.
  • The first processing of the data takes place in close proximity to the data itself, which both lowers the amount of latency experienced and increases the responsiveness of the system. The response time that is expected to be achieved is on the order of milliseconds, which makes it possible to handle data in a period that is very near to real-time.
  • Even if most of the time, computational resources are deployed at the local area network (LAN) level, one might argue that the network is still a crucial component of the architecture of fog computing even though this is the case. Edge computing works like this because it distributes computational resources at the level of individual devices.

Problem Statement

According to aconventional findings, there are still issues with pixel expansion, bad recovered picture quality, computational complexity, and memory requirements, and additional research is still needed to optimize the trade-off between these needs. Researchers are looking into how visual cryptography and watermarking can be used to protect data. The problem with the research done in the past is that traditional methods ignored image quality, data security, and performance. Lastly, a comparison of image quality, performance, and data security shows that the proposed model gives better-quality images and sends data quickly because it compresses image files. Also, the proposed work is more secure than the usual way of doing things.

Proposed Work

In the proposed research work, data security is being considered in relation to visual cryptography and watermarking. Previous study work had a problem in that it used traditional methods, but these methods overlooked picture quality, data security, and performance. As a result, the suggested study takes into consideration a hybrid method to safeguard multimedia data. In this discussion, watermarks and visual cryptography will be looked at. Finally, a comparative examination of picture quality, performance, and data security ensures that the suggested model provides superior-quality images and that the performance of data transmission is improved by compressing image files. In addition, the suggested work was shown to have a higher level of security when compared to the traditional technique.

Researchers have proposed a VCS that is based on QR codes as a solution to the pixel expansion and nonsensical concerns that are present in VCS. First, they built a block-by-block extended version control system or EVCS, that was a user- friendly VCS for storing valuable files based on the principle of conserving the pixel dimensions of hidden photos, which allows us to avoid possible attackers’ suspicions. An integrated model for image security by integrating Visual cryptography and watermark.

Through the use of the OR operation, HVS is able to openly disclose the hidden image by merely superimposing the received shares. Then, in order to send shares, we make use of QR codes’ high data capacity. Since the error-correcting code words are not altered during encoding, a regular QR code reader will be able to read and decode the encoded QR codes. Without compromising the benefits of QR codes and VCS, QECVS makes it possible to send confidential photos safely and reliably. But there is a need to integrate watermarking mechanism and compression mechanism. Integration of watermarking would improve security while compression is improving performance. Thus a watermarking mechanism is producing a watermarked image by taking cover image as input. On other hand, compression mechanism has been integrated into encryption phase. In both the traditional and the suggested approach, the PSNR and SSIM of the picture are taken into account in order to guarantee the image’s high quality throughout the visual cryptography process. In comparison to the traditional method, it is anticipated that the proposed work result in improved PSNR and SSIM.

Abstract

Underwater Wireless Sensor Network (UWSN) technology is widely used and has proven valuable in various underwater monitoring and inspection applications. Over the years, different UWSN protocols have been designed, and ad hoc modifications of existing protocols have been made to facilitate efficient and qualitative research analysis. However, battery-powered underwater sensor nodes have limited ability and must be transmitted at low power to save energy. The UWSN’s energy-efficient cooperative routing scheme is called Cluster-Based Neighbor Node Mobility and Incrementally Cooperative Dynamic Routing. The proposed method, Genetic Algorithm (GA), takes advantage of the broadcast nature of wireless nodes to perform advanced cooperative routing. The first stage builds the transmission distance, finds optimal distance neighbors, and establishes underwater network links. In the second stage, the link established in the first stage dynamically changes according to the difference in the Energy Level (EL) of adjacent nodes in the link to achieve the energy balance of the whole network and significantly extend the network life. Reliable routing and efficient network topology from multiple nodes to sink nodes. A cooperative routing protocol Time-Based Trustworthy Links (TBTL) for dynamic topologies. The third stage examines all paths and specifies the most reliable path to send the packet. Simulation results show that the genetic Algorithm outperforms the standard energy balance routing algorithm regarding network lifetime, transmission loss, and data throughput.

Keywords: Underwater Wireless Sensor Network (UWSN), energy-efficient, Time Based Trustworthy Link (TBTL), transmission, neighbors, secure communication, Cooperative Routing, Wireless nodes.

Chest X—Ray Based Classification of Lungs Pathology Using VGG-16 Features and Double Ensemble Classifier

Sadakathulla P. K.a and Dr. R Parameswarib

School of Computing Sciences, Vels Institute of Science, Technology and Advanced Studies (VISTAS)-Chennai, India

E-mail ID: sadakpk@gmail.com, dr.r.parameswari16@gmail.com

DOI: 10.1201/9781003430452-16

Abstract

Lung diseases include various globally common ailments that cause incorrect lung function. COPD, asthma, pneumonia, TB, and fibrosis are some of the most well-known lung diseases. These diseases are usually diagnosed by medical practitioners using chest X-ray images, which are time-consuming and cumbersome. So, Computer-aided diagnosis (CAD) systems can be of great use in developing countries, where there is a shortage of qualified practitioners. In this paper, the proposed procedure to classify lung diseases into different classes based on CNN- based VGG-16 features using the ensemble learning technique. For evaluating our system, this work has made use of the ChestX-ray8 dataset, which includes chest X-rays with over 15 different pathologies.

Keywords: Lung diseases, Chest X-ray, CAD, CNN, VGG-16, Ensemble learning

Introduction

The term “lung disease” refers to a variety of illnesses or conditions that can have an impact on pulmonary function and respiratory function. Infections with bacteria, viruses, or fungi can lead to a variety of lung diseases. Environmental factors too can lead to lung diseases such as lung cancer, mesothelioma, and asthma (National Institute of Environmental Health Sciences, n.d.).

With recent advances in computer vision, automated computer-aided diagnosis (CAD) systems have gained popularity. Several methods have been introduced to extract useful data from X-rays that will help clinicians understand the X-ray quantitatively. At present, the growth of machine and deep learning paradigms is heavily employed by the healthcare industry (Davenport & Kalakota, 2019).

In this work, mainly concentrated on chest X-rays for the classification of different lung pathologies that can be crucial in the identification and diagnosis of different lung diseases. The contents of this paper are organized as follows: Section 2 includes a brief look at the state-of- the-art techniques, and Section 3 shows the overall proposed framework for lung disease classification. Section 4, will display details about the performance of the proposed method, and at last, will deduce in Section 5.

Related Works

According to the literature, the first form of CAD architecture for lung disease detection was introduced in the late 1980s. But these efforts were not very powerful due to limitations in hardware and software support. Later, advances in hardware, such as GPUs, and software, such as deep learning modules, had a significant impact on the performance of lung disease diagnosis systems.

A system for lung disease prediction was put forward in Bharati et al., (2020), where the authors pointed out the poor performance of basic CNN in predictions due to extreme class imbalance. Their proposal included a novel hybrid deep learning framework by combining different approaches like VGG, STN, and data augmentation. They achieved a validation accuracy of 73%.

Another work claiming better feature extraction from X-ray images with deeper CNNs was presented in Choudhary et al., (2022). They used a fine- tuned CNN-based network called DenseNet-121 to extract X-ray features, followed by an artificial neural network (ANN) for classification.

The effects of outliers and multi-labels in the benchmark dataset were considered in Jing & Li (2022). They have come up with an auto- outlier fusion mechanism to get rid of outliers in the dataset. Their system achieved the highest accuracy of 72.62%.

While some researchers tried to classify different lung disease pathologies, others concentrated on particular lung diseases like pneumonia, thorax, cardiomegaly, etc. using the same dataset. Jun et al., (2018) proposed a pneumothorax diagnosis system. They developed an ensemble model of three similar CNN frameworks accepting different input image scales for this purpose. Cardiomegaly identification was the chosen disease in Zhou et al., (2019), where the authors employed transfer learning mechanisms to solve the problem. They extracted features using three different pre-trained CNN models (ResNet-50, Xception, and InceptionV3) and trained the classifier with single and combinations of the features obtained. Moreover, the same problem is discussed in Sarpotdar (2022). Here the authors have applied a customized, pre-trained U-Net framework as the resolution.

Another lung condition or infection that ranks highly among the causes of death in children and the elderly is pneumonia. Pneumonia predictions from x-ray images are demonstrated in Shah et al., (2020)and Yimer et al., (2021)created a CNN-based VGG-16 to address the issue, whereas Thakur et al., (2017)used mask R-CNN for the same purpose.

Methodology

This section provides the specifications of the key parts of our methodology, likely pre-processing, feature extraction, and classification. Once gather our needed data, and will first pre-process the images to make them more fruitful, then the x-ray image features will be extracted using VGG-16, and finally, the feature maps produced will be fed into ensemble learning frameworks created using a variety of traditional machine learning algorithms.

Data Description

The ChestX-ray8 dataset (Wang et al., 2017) released by the National Institutes of Health (NIH) consists 14 different lung diseases and one health condition termed “No Findings” in the database used in this work.

Pre-processing

The performance of a classification framework is significantly impacted by the pre-processing of data. Here included the following pre-processing methods to make sure all the images were ready for our target procedure.

Data removal

The ChestX-ray8 database consisted of multi- label images, that is, some images that belonged to more than one class, and these images were removed from the database. Hence, finally reduced the database, which contained about 112,120 images, to 93,969 images, which became our final database.

Filtering and contrast enhancement

The system has employed a median filter since studies have shown that it is one of the superior filters for removing salt and pepper noises along with speckle and Poisson noises from X-ray images (Yimer et al., 2021; Thakur et al., 2017; Das et al., 2016 ).

Resizing and RGB conversion

This work going to extract features of interest from the x-ray images using VGG-16 which uses a 3-channeled input image, so it has duplicated 1-channel data of our respective grayscale image into 3 channels.

6. Feature Extraction

The work chose a CNN-based VGG-16 model that has been pre-trained on ImageNet Simonyan & Zisserman (2014) In this work tried to exploit the power of transfer learning (TL), through which could incorporate previously acquired knowledge into new data, thereby making learning mechanisms easier than learning a freshly developed model from scratch.

Classification

When the data samples of different classes are imbalanced, CNN-based classification is known to degrade its performance [15]. Most real data, particularly medical data, is unbalanced, as the number of healthy people is always greater than the number of patients with actual illness. So instead of using the VGG-16 classifier for the classification, here applied an ensemble machine learning algorithm to achieve goal.

Experiments and Results

This section discusses the effectiveness of the proposed methodology. To ensure the capability of any system, a thorough study of its performance on a benchmark database with standard metrics plays a key function. For carrying out our experiments, simply divided each class in the complete dataset into train and test groups in 80:20 ratios. Additionally, For the implementation of the proposed framework, also utilized Python using the Keras library and TensorFlow.

The study measured the working performance of our proposed methodology using metrics that include accuracy, specificity, and sensitivity. And presented the efficiency of the suggested ensemble technique (binary and multi-class) along with a straight multi-class ensemble model without binary division and the VGG-16 classifier in Table 1. The VGG-16 classification suffers from being biased towards the majority-class overfitting problem. While straight ensemble tries to overcome this, the division of the whole problem into two sub- classifications could solve this problem to a great extent.

Table 1. Performance of the proposed system
Method Accuracy (%) Specificity (%) Sensitivity (%)
VGG-16 classification 74.6 % 77.4% 71.9%
Proposed Ensemble classification 78.9% 81.3% 74.2%
Proposed subdivided Ensemble classification 81.3% 86.1% 78.2%

Conclusion

Chest X-rays are an integral part of the analysis and diagnosis of various chest diseases. Visual inspections are typically assigned to an expert in the field. These are time-consuming and prone to personal errors that can be hazardous. This work tried to integrate some of the existing approaches to build a better CAD system for lung disease predictions. It began by analyzing the benchmark ChestX-ray8 database for gaps in order to produce higher-quality results. Instead of replacing experts in diagnosis, our system is designed to assist them in making better decisions and reducing personal errors

The matching score further filters out the queries with respect to the subdivisions.
