Mobile-Based Cloud Detection Model for Skin Cancer Using Machine Learning

K. Devi, B. Muthusenthil,25

E-mail: devii.jeya@gmail.com

DOI: 10.1201/9781003430452-33

Abstract

A recent development in the field of deep learning has taken the spotlight for creating rich applications. Computer-based applications in medicine are the upcoming projects, which are wide-spreading the advancement of the IT industry. This paper takes the readers and researchers on an expedition across the cloud-based approach to detecting skin cancers in people. We are aware that skin cancer is a fatal condition, and that improving the likelihood of effective survival depends on early identification. Deep learning approaches have shown up their strengths in terms of performance like sensitivity, accuracy, and precision. So, in this paper, we are using convolutional neural networks (CNNs) in experimenting with image recognition and image classification to detect skin cancer. We are also deploying the application in a cloud platform so that anyone can use this with the help of the internet.

Keywords: Convolutional Neural Network, Image Classification, Skin Cancer, Cloud Computing, Deep Learning, Image Recognition, Transfer Learning

Introduction

Skin cancer is merely subjected to ultraviolet (UV) radiation causing contagious disease among people (Vijayalakshmi, 2019; Vedanti Chintawar & Jignyasa Sanghavi) . Early diagnosis is the initial possible measure reducing the risks of extending the disease to the next level (Vijayalakshmi, 2019; Yuexiang li & Linlin Shen, 2018) .

Insights reports concede that there has been a 53% expansion in the melanoma cases analyzed every year (Esteva et al., 2017; (World Health Organization, n.d.). Multiple individuals kick the bucket because of skin disease each hour in the U.S. The death rate is under 14% on the off chance that it is analyzed in later stages (Erkol et al., 2005; Zorman et al., 1997). Likewise, the endurance rate is over 97% in case it is analyzed in the beginning phases (Siegel et al., 2018). This tells us early detection helps us to easily overcome this disease.

Yet, the dermatologist’s expertise has a significant impact on precise determination. It has been noted that the top dermatologists struggle to effectively diagnose skin malignant growths with an accuracy rate of under 80% (Marks, 2000). Besides, talented dermatologists are extremely less. To conquer this issue of exactness and deficiency of clinical dermatologists, AI calculations can be utilized for identifying the presence of skin malignant growth. The cutting-edge model for skin malignant growth location is proposed by many creators (Esteva et al., 2017; Kittler et al., 2002; Yu et al., 2016). Using this quality service can be provided. Due to the advancement in cloud computing, deploying our model in the cloud this service can be used by almost everyone. The Internet serves as a great helping hand in utilizing cloud-based systems. The image of the patient skin condition can be sent to the cloud system, which can predict the return of the result to the patient immediately. Furthermore, the cost and time taken for implementing this service are very less. An additional advantage is that patients do not have to wait for a skilled dermatologist for accurate results. A mobile-based model detection system is been proposed (Xiangfeng Dai et al., n.d.). However, it has its drawbacks such as: High-performance mobile is required for such a model to run, time taken for the model to predict is very high and the machine learning model cannot be updated

In our paper, we overcome these drawbacks by proposing a model in which we deploy the model in a cloud-based computer so that prediction is done in the server rather than in the client device. Therefore, the client’s role is to just take a photo and upload it to the server. The processing and prediction are performed in the server and the result is sent back to the client. If we get a model with higher performance, it can be easily deployed in the server system.

Recent Works

Earlier researchers first perform lesion segmentation, then extract the features from them and use that for skin cancer classification. To identify skin cancer, Manu and Yu made use of artificial neural networks, namely fully-convolutional residual networks (Yu et al., 2016). For lesion classification, Codella recently merged recent developments in machine learning technology with deep learning [14].

In order to train the model using supervised learning techniques, a lot of data and processing power are required. Duraipandian presented the use of the cloud for IoT for increasing the computation speed (Duraipandian, 2020). Therefore, these models can be deployed in cloud-based computers. For example, Alghatani and Rezgui (Khalid Alghatani & Abdelmounaam Rezgui, 2019) presented a platform for remote monitoring of patients. In addition, a system to monitor hypertension patients was presented by Melillo and Scala (Ruiz-Zafra et al., 2013). They used a cloud-based platform to develop mHealth apps that could be used for monitoring, collecting information, and viewing diagnostic videos remotely.

Application Design and Architecture

Overall System Design

We propose a cloud-based skin cancer detection system. It can be broadly classified into three parts — client input layer, cloud platform layer, and output visualization layer. The client takes a photo with help of input sensors like the camera. After capturing the photo is encrypted using a certain encryption algorithm and then it is uploaded to the server. When the cloud system receives the photo, it first decrypts the data using a specific decryption algorithm and it starts processing it. After predicting the result, it is encrypted and sent back to the client. The client receives the data from the server, decrypts the data, and displays the result. The server is used to deliver the detection of skin cancer model, which is trained separately. In order to guarantee total security, the information is encrypted during transmission.

In this architecture, the dataset is stored in the cloud environment and the deep learning model is completely trained in the cloud platform. Also, the prediction i.e. classifying whether the image contains skin cancer or not is computed in the cloud platform. The client’s role is to just upload an image and everything else is performed in the cloud. This also contains an authentication module so that only the authorized user can use this application. This architecture is exhibited in Fig. 1.

Client Input Layer

The client’s main role is to capture an image and send and receive data to and from the server. The client mainly consists of three modules: authentication, image capturing, and uploading the data to the cloud. In the authentication module, the end-user has to first register with his detail, and Cloud storage for the data is encrypted. Then the user has to log in with the same credentials. These credentials are again sent to the server. If the credentials are correct the send a positive reply then the user is allowed to use our application else not allowed.

After successful authentication, the image is captured with help of the input sensors and uploaded to the server via a gateway device. This device sends an HTTP request to the server with the captured image with the help of the internet.

Cloud Platform Layer

The server mainly consists of five modules: An authentication module, a Database module, a Machine learning training module, reception and transmission of data, and a machine learning model for prediction.

The server authentication module is to check and verify the user. When a user registers the details are saved in the database. Then when the user login those credentials are cross-checked with the database. If the user has already registered positive response is sent else a negative response is sent to the client. The dataset “HAM10000. Dataset” is downloaded from the source website and it is stored in the cloud storage. This database can be accessed by the API provided by the cloud service provider. The resource accessing overhead time is also managed by the cloud provided. The database module also contains user authentication data.

The complete deep learning model training is done on this cloud platform. The deep learning training module gets the data database and trains the machine learning model according to the given configuration. The time taken to train the model is normally very high. The model is trained before we deploy the application for public use. So this training time is not related to our application usage. It generates a model using deep learning with direct skin cancer prediction capabilities. This model is stored in a cloud database for further use.

Reception and transmission of the data module are used for communication with the end user. It decrypts the received data and encrypts the data sent to the client. The image which is sent by the user is sent as input is classified using the trained model. This classification is also completely done on the cloud platform. The time taken for this computation is very less because of the huge computation power available in the cloud platform, so there is not much delay for the result to be sent back. After this result is computed, the result is sent back to the client.

Output Visualisation Layer

This module receives the output data from the cloud platform and displays that result to the user. It contains the skin output label corresponding to the input image.

Experimentation and Implementation

The cloud environment for this application was created using Amazon web services. We use the skin cancer dataset from “The HAM10000. Dataset: A Large Collection of Multi-Source Dermatoscopic Images of Common Pigmented Skin Lesions” (Tschandl et al., 2018), which contain 10015 labeled images of seven types of skin problem which are 1) Melanocytic nevi 2) Melanoma 3) Benign keratosis 4) Basal cell carcinoma 5) Actinic keratoses 6) Vascular lesions 7) Dermatofibroma.

This entire dataset is downloaded and saved in the Amazon S3 bucket. From here the data is taken for the training of the deep learning model using the API provided by the Amazon S3 services.

The machine learning algorithms can be developed and trained using python (Python, n.d.)] libraries like TensorFlow (Tensorflow, n.d.), PyTorch, Fastai, etc. We employ a technique known as transfer learning (Pan & Yang, 2010; Karl Weiss et al., 2016) . In this method, we can use the features gathered from all the pre-trained models that were trained on a particularly large dataset for our model. DenseNet (Huang et al., 2016; Duraipandian, 2020)CNN is being used. We are using the feature-extracting layer of the DenseNet model and adding our custom classifier which helps us map the features to the corresponding label in our skin cancer detection. The precision of our model is 0.889166 and recall is 0.889166, and F-Measure is 0.88916.

Conclusion

The prominent drawback in implementing CNNs or the one which is impermissible in adopting and executing the CNN architecture is fitting the high computational power, which is very well handled with a cloud monitoring system. As the image is sent to the cloud systems the computation is done in the cloud. Also, our deep layered model captures the features and classifies the result with high accuracy that the leading dermatologist. Also, this solution is available to a wider range now. Summing up, good quality medical service is now available to everyone at the correct time, irrespective of place and time. So, this disease can be identified and cured easily.

Abstract

The brain acts as the body’s master control system. It regulates the mind, memory, voice, and body. Images play a crucial part in the diagnosis of brain disorders in humans and may be used to diagnose a wide variety of neurological conditions. Imaging examinations may be used to detect a brain Tumor. The brain is imaged with the use of X-rays, powerful magnets, or radioactive chemicals. Examining the brain using a magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) or computed tomography (CT) scan is the gold standard for diagnosing brain disorders. Neural network predicts what happens to the tumor in the future. Data Sets are converted to neural networks which exactly predict what happens in the future.

Introduction

The cerebrum is the primary brain structure and is found posterior to the skull. The human brain contains 86 billion nerve cells and also the same number of non-neuronal cells.

An artificial neural network, or simply a network of cells. In the aspects of deep learning, neurone network is considered as its subset. Best Fit Topic Model Coherence Improvement for Subectivity Analysis of Gestational Diabetes Mellitus

J. Jeyalakshmi28

Department of Computer Science and Engineering, Rajalakshmi Engineering College-Chennai-India

DOI: 10.1201/9781003430452-36

Abstract

The subjectivity analysis can shed light on the crux of content over an open discussion forum. Gestational Diabetes Mellitus(GDM) has become more common among young pregnant women in India. To analyze the public mentality, causality analysis, and spreading awareness, it will be helpful to analyze the content of tweets. Methods and Material: The system uses Best Fit Topic Modeling and Coherence improvement by hyperparameter tuning on the corpora crawled from Twitter over GDM. Results: The Best Fit Topic Model is drafted from LDA, CTM, and Gibbs Sampling. The measures like Inter topic Distance relations are drafted using Multi Dimension Scaling, Coherence scores are quantified and is optimized to 70.8% from 39% using LDA-Mallet by hyperparameter tuning. The system gives inferences regarding Physical activity-based control measures for GDM, Low Glycemic Index diet, Consumption of prescribed medicine, and quantity ex. folate content, Risk of potato causing GDM. Conclusion: The proposed work shows subjectivity analysis on Twitter content for GDM and presents better inferences on the subject of discussion.

Keywords: Data Mining, Gestational Diabetes, Diabetes Mellitus, Machine Learning, Prediction, Geo-Spatial Analysis, Etc

Introduction

GDM (Gestational Diabetes Mellitus) is becoming a more common short-term illness among middle-aged women. Women diagnosed with GDM have remained at risk for diabetes for 4-5 years, even though it is a short-term condition. GDM has been found to affect at least 10% of all pregnant women. Sentiment analysis is used in the proposed system to try to extract such tacit information from tweets and give an analysis of the symptoms, precautions, and preventive treatments discussed in the tweets. In light of this knowledge, the proposed study analyses population health using open social network content, such as Twitter, and uses Opinion, Sentiment mining, Topic Modelling, Coherence improvisation, and Inter-topic distance parameters to identify people’s mentalities and disease-specific content of discussion. Building Best Fit Topic Models to properly infer the substance of the discussion is the focus of the research. With MALLET, it improves the coherence of topic models. The paper is organized to Chapter 1 based on Introduction, chapter 2 based on Literature and existing work, chapter 3 based on Experimentation, and Chapter 4 on Conclusion and Future Work.

Related work

The existing systems are summarized in this chapter in regard to the analysis of textual content over social media.

Hao Cui et al. (2021), proposed a study on social media in China based on COVID-19. They used content on Sina Weibo microblogging website for their analysis. They discovered a decay in attention which did not help find the impact of the efforts by the government towards spreading awareness on COVID-19 pandemic. Sebastian Hermes et al. (2020), had suggested a model to study the impact of social media on patients (Cui & Kertez, 2021; Hermes et al., 2020; Dyer & Kolic, 2020). The social media in comparison with the traditional industries, work with data and people who generate the data and content. The influence of the actors in generating value for the healthcare service provider. The value of the organization, the transformation in the value, the capture of the value and the transformation of the process, and the delivery of value were discussed in the paper (Ferretti et al., 2019; Salas-Zarate et al., 2017; Singh et al., 2017). Joel Dye et al. (2010), had proposed a study on sentiment of risk perception over Twitter on COVID-19. The study of the open social network was based on a hypothesis, that the mortality rate during COVID-19 was related to the attention of the netizens(Takabe, 2016; Barnwal et al., 2016; Woo & Chen, 2016). The emotion and semantic analysis were done. Co-occurence of the words was investigated. The “death” was an interesting node with lot of co-occurring terms. Many such inferences were drafted. The study has led to usage of Topic Models and hyperparameter tuning to improvise the inference of content in the unstructured text.

Experimentation

The proposed system architecture is presented in this section along with the results and discussions in Fig. 1. The work is implemented in Python and R Studio using packages like TwitterR, Sentiment, etc., The analysis is presented in broadly two categories as suggested below.

  1. Best Fit Topic Modeling
  2. Coherence Improvement by Hyper-parameter tuning

Best Fit Topic Modeling

The results of topic modeling are retrieved by creating a best fit out of Latent Dirichlet allocation, Correlated Topic Model, and Gibbs Sampling as an ensemble. The Subjectivity analysis reveals facts about the following issues regarding GDM in Fig. 2.

  • Physical activity based control measures for GDM.
  • Risk of potato causing GDM

Hyper Parameter Tuning for Improving Coherence Score with Topic Scalability

The hyperparameters used in this work are alpha which represents document-topic density and Beta represents topic-word density. After hyperparameter tuning and coherence, saliency, and relevance parameters are measured for the text. Performance Comparison is shown inTable 1. Once the coherence score increases the meaningfulness of the content under study also increases as inTable 2.

Conclusion

The paper discusses how unstructured and semi-structured textual information can be used to make useful inferences using text mining, Topic Modeling, and Hyper Parameter tuning. The understanding can be used in new patients or people seeking awareness on the issues.

A Decentralized Application-DAPP for Remote Voting System Based on Blockchain Technology

K. Iswarya,29

E-mail: aishwaryakannan45@gmail.com, bpecleela2005@gmail.com, cdevimayavanpd@gmail.com

DOI: 10.1201/9781003430452-37

Abstract

In any country, democratic voting is mandatory because of widespread mistrust of the traditional voting system. It has been observed that people have been violated in their fundamental rights. Lack of transparency has led to challenges to other digital voting systems. The majority of voting methods are not sufficiently transparent, which makes it highly challenging for the government to win over voters’ trust. The previous and present digital voting systems have failed because they are susceptible to manipulation. The major objective is to address any errors or unfair voting practices that may arise in both the traditional and computerized voting systems. To ensure a fair election and lessen unfairness, blockchain technology can be included in the voting process. The computerized voting methods are not flawless enough to be used on a broad scale, and the physical voting systems have numerous problems as well. This evaluates the requirement for a remedy to safeguard citizens’ democratic rights. This editorial proposes a framework built on cutting-edge blockchain technology to create a reliable working relationship between voters and election officials. Without using any actual polling places, the suggested method offers a framework that may be used to conduct voting activity digitally through blockchain. Our suggested architecture employs adaptable consensus techniques to allow for a scalable blockchain. During a chain transaction, smart contracts offer a safe connection between the user and the network. Discussions have also focused on the voting system’s security, which is built on a blockchain. Transactions on the blockchain can now be encrypted using cryptographic hashes. We assess the potential of appropriated record developments in particular through the depiction of a pertinent examination, specifically the pattern of a political race, and the use of blockchain-based software, which takes good care of security issues and reduces the cost of administering a cross-country political campaign.

Keywords: Blockchain, Smart contracts, Cryptographic hash, Consensus algorithms

Introduction

The voting system must be as precise, effective, and efficient as possible because voting is one of the most crucial democratic instruments. With regard to defining the locations, hiring employees, and mitigating security threats at polling places, blockchain can significantly reduce the time and resources required. Blockchain-based digital elections provide cost savings while lowering the possibility of unfair votes. It can improve transaction traceability, voting system reliability, and transparency.

A voting machine that is connected to a centralized database has been utilized in traditional digital voting systems. A person with physical access to this device can tamper with it. In contrast to an immutable blockchain, which wouldn’t be affected by a single network saboteur, the voting system’s entire network might as a result experience one potential point of failure. Information is decentralized and kept on a blockchain, where the veracity of the records is continuously checked. As a result, the peer-to-peer network would continue to provide all services even if a node were the victim of a malicious attack; just that node would be affected. Blockchain technology has developed to the point where it can be trusted and utilized as a private voting ledger. More security and trust may now be found with blockchain than with earlier systems. It doesn’t need a real voting machine or module, which is always susceptible to hacking through tampering tools. The most appealing aspect of this method is its transparency, which gives voters confidence that their votes are being cast in the most appropriate ways. Considerable systems are being studied for deployment, including banking, healthcare, food safety, and cryptocurrency trading. Blockchain technology can be used to conduct an honest election that protects voter confidentiality and confidence.

The opportunity to meddle with votes or add fake votes while they are being counted exists in the traditional voting procedure. The authorities have the authority to proclaim false results when they are influenced by a third party. The voter is not given any assurance that his vote would be counted or not. Overall, the traditional voting procedure does not guarantee unbiased voting or transparency. Only digitalizing the system or using digital voting devices to cast ballots won’t fix the problem. Hackers may manipulate these computerized voting devices, which would interfere with the voting process. Therefore, a decentralized system is needed that can maintain data security even if one node becomes corrupt. This paper’s primary goal is to encourage the use of a blockchain-based system of voting in order to safeguard against manipulation of the voting process and win over voters. The premise that a node connected to the network will never be erased is one of the fundamental characteristics of blockchain technology. Blockchain technology, which provides decentralized data storage, makes it possible.

It is impossible to simultaneously delete the data from every node since it is duplicated across every node in the network and is stored on numerous nodes across the chain. Additionally, since each node computes the data separately before combining it, the computation required to tally the results is minimized. The use of blockchain in the voting system is proposed as a way to prevent vote tampering and the casting of ghost votes. Each ID may be used to cast one vote. Blockchain prevents any unauthorized attempts to modify any part of the chain. It ends the voting system’s reliance on middlemen, which helps conserve resources and reduces human error.

Related Work

In order to prevent vote fraud or tampering, Yang Yang et al., (2021)proposes a self-tallying electoral system based on blockchain called “PriScore” that supports score voting. Each voter can give the candidates distinct assessment ratings (within a given range) using PriScore. The aggregate of each ballot’s assessment scores, which are anonymous to protect the privacy of voters, should equal a predefined constant.The simultaneous verification of both constraints demands, range proof and sum proof, is a critical problem in score casting. To demonstrate the scores satisfying two important conditions, we provide a novel method we term dual zero-knowledge proof (dual-ZKP), which nontrivially mixes distributed ElGamal crypto with 1-out-of-K” proof. Any party using PriScore can compute and check the election results because of the self-tallying process, which ensures fairness and avoids conflicts. According to the security analysis, PriScore satisfactorily satisfies the following requirements: eligibility, thoroughness, coherence, widespread verifiability, and multiple-voting detection.

A cryptographic method for an election with verified, end-to-end verifiable, and secret ballots was suggested by Panja & Roy, (2021). It suggests a safe and reliable system for voter registration and identification. It stops attempts to stuff ballots. In order to prevent any adversary from creating and secretly posting a legal ballot posted on the community noticeboard, they updated the DRE-ip system. This work suggests a technique that uses secure multi-party computing, non-interactive zero-knowledge (NIZK) proof, and Direct-Recording Electronic (DRE) devices to broadcast the final count without revealing the totals from particular DRE devices. The analysis demonstrates that the effective zero-knowledge proof (NIZK) made by Lin & Zhang (2019) for APSIPA ASC 2019 is invalid because it does not satisfy the bystander distinguishability requirement. As a result, it adds a superior NIZK proof, which boosts the system’s efficiency.

In order to establish and intimate the numerous fulminations brought on by an intrusion at multiple levels; Using Blockchain technology, Rathee et al, (2021)created a secure and open IoT platform for electronic voting. Message tampering, DoS and DDoS attacks, and authentication latency are only a handful of the security factors that are investigated in order to certify the proposed system. They used the Social Weighted Rank technique and the Algorithm of Secured E-Voting Using Trusted IoT Devices to assess IoT trust.

A platform developed by Farooq et al, (2022) is based on cutting-edge blockchain technology and offers maximum system transparency and dependability in order to foster a relationship of trust between voters and election officials. With the use of this software, voting activities might be carried out online using blockchain without the need for physical polling places. Thanks to the use of adaptable consensus techniques, this provides a scalable blockchain. The voting process is more secure because of the Chain Security Algorithm used in the system. During a chain transaction, smart contracts provide an encrypted connection between the client and the network. The suggested system’s performance evaluation demonstrates the system’s capacity for deployment in a huge population.

Ethereum’s Blockchain-based electronic voting method was introduced by Al-Madani et al, (2020). This application can overcome the limitations and potential vulnerabilities of the centralized voting mechanism by utilizing Blockchain technology. This study illustrated the data security features of a blockchain. It developed a voting system that employs a smart contract in a decentralized way. After that, a local blockchain received a shared ledger for this application. As a platform, the application uses Ethereum Blockchain technology, and a decentralized database is used to store information about candidates, votes, and ballotter identities.

Roopak & Sumathi, (2020)proposed a structure for a cryptographically secure electronic voting mechanism using a separate virtual ID offered by UIDAI. The Aadhar database allows for the collection of voter demographic data, including fingerprint data. To safeguard the confidentiality of the vote in the block, the fingerprint is turned into a digital signature during encryption. With the use of a private key and the use of hash work, this framework includes a method for carrying out operations on encoded data.

A mobile voting system was suggested by Abayomi-Zannu et al, (2020)to lessen election fraud in Nigeria. This study developed a mobile system of voting that securely stores votes using blockchain technology and verifies voters using two factors. The suggested system was then assessed using the ISO 9241-11 usability paradigm, and the findings indicated that it obtained a good usability rating, indicating that it may be used in a voting process.

A mechanism called Provotum was suggested by Killer et al, (2020). By deploying a private blockchain as a publicly viewable message board and allowing the explicit allocation of trust across various permission blockchain nodes, Provotum introduces a brand-new and entirely decentralized blockchain-based Regional E-Voting system. Client-side encryption is used in Provotum’s fully distributed operation, enabling features like ballot secrecy, distributed key generation, smart contracts, asymmetric cryptography, and cooperative decryption. In order to enable open and end-to-end verification, the BC creates an audit trail.

In order to safeguard voter and vote confidentiality as well as poll integrity, Qureshi et al, (2019) presented SeVEP, a secure and fully transparent voting system. It also authenticates voter identification using a multifactor authentication technique, permits multiple votes throughout the allotted voting period, prohibits double voting, and offers verifiability and uncoercibility in the event of malfunctioning voting machines. SeVEP is a secure, verifiable, and useful e-polling system, as demonstrated by its efficiency, security, and comparative evaluation in terms of security attributes and cryptographic costs.

In order to improve voting security and transparency, Pandey et al, (2019)created the VoteChain voting system using the blockchain. Vote data is kept on a distributed public ledger using a blockchain. For establishing consensus among servers, this system uses Proof of Work and a HashCash variation called VoteMaker.

Sivaram et al, (2022)suggested the COVID-19 Pandemic - Remote Voting System (C19P-RVS). The system’s entire operations will be dependable based on the application software, which further minimizes duplication during the Aadhaar data verification. With his automatic authorization and verified system compliance, the voter is granted access to remote voting activities, and the entire process provides legitimacy.

Lin & Zhang (2019)have developed a method that uses Blockchain as a bulletin board and “Efficient One-out-of-T” zero-knowledge proof to facilitate multiple-candidate voting (ZKP). The concerns with adaptable and reversible are also fixed. It can be utilized in intimate, private situations that require anonymity, such as board elections in corporations. The results of the performance assessment demonstrate that the recommended ZKP uses less time.

Proposed Methodology

The envisaged architecture provides a framework that might be utilized to carry out voting procedures virtually using blockchain technology without using any actual polling locations. In this approach, a person’s computerized National ID is confirmed from the database so they can vote from anywhere, regardless of whether they are in another country. Each user has equitable access to the entire voting process through the system. Additionally, it provides post-voting traceability. Voters register in the system using their access data. To enroll a voter into the system, the system uses her ID information and checks it against an online database. Complete voter data is stored in the system. Voting Coins (VC) awarded to each voter who successfully registers in the system will be added to your wallet. Thus every voter receives a single VC in in order to avoid double voting.

After completing the verification, the voter is added to the database of the system. The blockchain is configured using a single-chain system. The method also leverages the country’s national database in order to protect the people’s voting right to cast an honest ballot. Each vote triggers a transaction that includes the voter’s National ID. The transaction is subsequently mined by the minors, who then deposit it in the blockchain. All across the voting process, Vote Coin from the voter’s account is also exploited.

The registered voter is only permitted to use one vote coin at a time. After signing in with their credentials, the ballotter is routed to the vote-casting portal, where they can see every contender in the race in their district. When a voter requests to cast a ballot, the system uses the blockchain to cross-reference the ballotter’s digitized National ID credentials with all of the previously completed transactions to verify the ballotter’s right to poll.

If a session hash is discovered to match the voter’s electronic National ID, the voter will be unlogged from the system and the claim will be rejected. If no vote has been cast, the miner gets the request to append the node.

A transaction hash is used to track the transaction, which is performed out by the miner. The voting chain is then connected to the node after that. The votes are completely protected by a cryptographic hash. The chain will grow by one block for each registered voter. The voting method also makes sure that each user could only cast one vote by utilizing the voting currency. Regardless of whether the casting coin’s balance is left unchanged due to a technical issue, the process ensures that no voter has cast a duplicate ballot. The miner will immediately reject any rogue nodes or requests made by voters if it can tell if the transaction hash was generated using the voter’s computerized National ID or not. After effectively executing the transaction, the vote was added to the overall number of votes cast in the election. The voter offered a unique session hash that he could use to authenticate his vote online. The voter’s wallet will be depleted of all vote currency if a vote is correctly cast.

With the utilization of blockchain technology, various systems have incorporated the voting mechanism. The information about their typical response time and security requirement compliance in graphs Figs. 2 and 3.

Cryptographic Hash

The privacy of the user’s identity is one of the many advantages of cryptographic hashing, which sustains the statistics secret from any system intruders, and cryptographic hashing is implemented with SHA-256 and Advanced Encryption Standard (AES). Because only the person who is authorized to use the transaction can decrypt it and access the data using his private key, the transaction is secure while it travels over the network to be pushed to a node. By entering the address of his transaction, it is possible to track the voter’s vote; the voter is informed via SMS and email as soon as the vote is cast. By using the hash value of the transaction that is provided on the registered phone number, voters can monitor their vote on the blockchain. The information gathered during the voting procedure is included in the vote data. The content is still obscured, safe, and secure. Only the voter has access to the tracing information, and only the ballotter can witness and validate their voting history. The transaction is locked using the citizen’s public key once it has been committed in a block. The tracking node is perceived using the ballotter’s public key. Using his individual secret key, the voter can see the transaction that was made by his wallet. Once a vote has been cast, a voter can only observe their vote; they are never able to modify or cancel it. Cryptography is used to encrypt any user information transferred during a transaction.

Smart Contract

Simple blockchain entrenched strategy called “smart contracts” that execute when certain criteria are met. A contract is often implemented automatically so that both participants can be sure of the outcome right away, without the need for a mediator or a lag. Smart contracts provide a secure link between the user and the network during the execution of a transaction in the chain. These rules are universal to the blockchain and cannot, even under any conditions, be ignored. All nodes must follow the smart contracts in order for the vote to be successfully saved in the system.

Result and Discussion

The proposed decentralized application for a distant location voting system based on blockchain technology is built using smart contracts, advanced encryption standards (AES) and SHA-256. This system satisfies the security criteria for maximum ballot secrecy, completeness, soundness, Fairness, personal and global verifiability, detection of double votes, and the absence of disputes and self-tallying. Because it employs the more efficient method of developing a dynamic consensus algorithm to lessen the large computational power utilized by the blockchain, this system’s usability functions effectively. When the system operates transparently, people are much more likely to count on it and trust it.

Conclusion

The purpose of the suggestion of an ethereum - based electoral system solution was to foster confidence between both the government and the public to persuade them that their voting integrity is safeguarded. The blockchain voting system also makes the process accessible and trustworthy.The existing voting process is incredibly expensive in every country, but the alternative approach would use blockchain polling technique to make voting less expensive, quicker, and more trustworthyPeople’s relationships with their representative democracy are thus improved as a result of the system’s dependability and transparency. The suggested strategy offers a well-founded, open, and trustworthy framework for the government and the populace. The outlined structure provides a favorable result according to the performance assessment of blockchain-based in VMS. The study indicated the system’s effectiveness maintains efficiency even when handling a significant volume of blockchain transactions.

Diagnosis of Mild Cognitive Impairment Using Multimodal Imaging With Machine Learning Techniques

Ms. K. R. Nandhashree,30

E-mail: nandhashree29@gmail.com, pjshree12@gmail.com

DOI: 10.1201/9781003430452-38

Abstract

Computer-aided identification of Alzheimer’s disease (AD) can assist physicians to a wide extent in the timely diagnosis of the presence of dementia in aged people. Also, the unavailability of indisputable diagnostic methodology makes early recognition of AD a significant health concern. A few non-invasive biomarkers have been proposed, including Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) based volumetric analysis, Positron Emission Tomography (PET) based metabolic activity analysis, as alternatives in contrast to neuropsychological assessment, which helps in diagnosis. These methodologies have indicated encouraging results, but a complete data fusion analysis has not led to examining whether these various modalities convey corresponding data and assuming this case, the framework of whether they can be joined to give a progressively precise analysis is taken for the research. In this exertion, an analysis of consolidating MRI and PET data utilizing an ensemble classifier-based joined pixel fusion approach is employed in this work. The feature extraction is performed using a novel hybrid method combining GLDM, MSER, and EHS. Better performance is obtained using this novel technique with ensemble classifiers. Accuracy of about 86% is achieved using this CAD approach.

Keywords: Alzheimer’s disease, Feature optimization, Feature Extraction, MRI. PET.

Introduction

AD, is a kind of neurodegenerative dementia and the most recognized reason for dementia, comprising 60 to 90% of all symptoms considered (American Psychiatric Association-APA 2013). AD accounts for one in the list of valid reasons for death in many nations. Early diagnosis helps in preventing the advancement of AD (Ding & Yei, 2019; Peng et al., 2019). Mild Cognitive Impairment (MCI) is the starting stage of dementia (Agarwal & Bedi, 2019; Anter et al., 2019; Baltrusaitis et al., 2018; Baskar & Annadurai, 2019). On the off chance that the ailment is analyzed at this stage, medication can be arranged, and through regular follow up we can predict the advancement of dementia. MRI scans are utilized to investigate the structural deformations of the internal organs within the body. To defeat the challenges in analyzing the clinical image, the segmentation procedure of computerized imaging is utilized which gives an increment in demonstrative efficiency. The Positron Emission Tomography (PET) scan is a brain imaging technique that gives information about how the brain tissues are functioning.

Exploratory Study

For AD prognosis, many methods have employed development in feature extraction (Acharya et al., 2019; Alickovic et al., 2019; Lulu et al., 2019) and selection ideas using one or two modalities. In Alickovic et al, (2019) the histogram is used to transfer images to feature vectors. AD classification in Ahmed et al, (2019); Duc, (2020);Han, (2019); Islam & Zhang, (2018); Jain et al, (2019); Jimenez-Mesa, (2020); Ju et al, (2019); Kanghan et al, (2019); Kruthika et al, (2019); Liang et al, (2019); Lowe et al, (2019); Lu et al, (2018); Lulu et al, (2019); Bhatia, (2019); Ju et al, (2019)is done using deep learning techniques employed on the brain network and using gene data. The network is built by considering the connectivity of the regions of the brain obtained using resting-state fMRI. In Ahmed et al, (2018) a survey is given by the researchers where a conclusion stating that the deep learning and multimodal approach combing functional and structural modality can enhance the accuracy of disease identification. Disease diagnostics with neuroimaging information have utilized many machine-learning calculations (Bastia, 2018; Moore et al., 2019; Pan et al., 2019; Peng et al., 2019; Razavi et al, 2019). The reason is that multimodal information has more amount of information than considering single modality data [2]. The concept of fusion in images helps in providing an accurate description of the framework and reduces the memory requirement by fusion of images instead of storing all the imaging modalities (Richhariya, 2020; Sanchez-Reyna, 2019; Shaikh & Ali, 2019).

From the literature survey, the inference made is that only a single modality is used in most of the works (Anter et al, 2019; Moore et al, 2019; Pan et al, 2019) . Thus, considering the multimodal approach of combining a structural modality (i.e.) MRI and functional modality (i.e.,) PET is a rationale for this research work. Multimodal image fusion (Liang et al, 2019; Lowe et al, 2019; Lu et al, 2018)and classification (Baskar & Annadurai, 2019)have drawn a considerable amount of research space in the past decade.

Methods

In this section, the proposed framework and the procedures used are described in brief. The proposed multimodal framework is portrayed in Fig. 1.

Image Acquisition

The MRI and the PET scan images are obtained from the standard ADNI, and from that ADNI1_ Annual 2 yr_3T and ADNI1_Baseline_3T are used in particular. 520 MRI and 728 PET data have been used in the work.

Preprocessing

For all the ADNI data obtained, we consider the MRI modality achieved at 1.5T and the PET modality. All the artifacts of both modalities are pre-processed to remove the skull, which may lead to an accurate classification. This removes the non-brain regions of the brain and is done using a brain surface extraction algorithm. The midsagittal line alignment is done to align the sagittal part of the brain. The original image differs from its coordinate system because the patient’s head remains tilted. The inhomogeneity is corrected initially to reduce the errors in the co-registration of the images.

Segmentation

The algorithm partitions an image into discrete regions consisting of each pixel having the same attributes. To be meaningful and valuable for image analysis and understanding. The fuzzy c - means is a technique for grouping that permits one bit of information to have a place with at least two clusters.

Image Fusion

The multimodal fusion method is used with the nonsubsampled contourlet transform (NSCT). Initially, on preregistered raw images, NSCT was run to obtain their low and high-frequency subbands. The NSCT is a multiscale, shift-invariant, multi-direction expansion that helps in giving a fast execution. The NSCT has demonstrated to be extremely proficient in image denoising and image enhancement.

Feature Extraction

This module is done with the hybrid novel algorithm by combining the below 3 algorithms. All the feature extraction algorithms used are texture-based analyses.

Gray-Level Difference Method (GLDM)

Two pixels were given an absolute difference in grey level and separated by a specific displacement d. The motion vector can be computed from Eq. (1) and the probability density function can be computed from Eq. (2).

(1)
$$\begin{array}{l} {\delta = (\Delta x,\Delta y)} \\ \left. \text{Let,~}S\delta(x,y) = \middle| S(x,y) - S(x + \Delta x,y + \Delta y) \right| \\ \end{array}$$

(2)
D(i ∣ δ) = Prob[(Sδ(x, y) = i]

The initial values are attained from the input image. By concatenating the angular second moment, contrast, entropy, and mean that are calculated from PDF, a feature vector is calculated.

Maximally Stable Extremal Regions (MSER)

MSER is a stable connected component with a sequence of gray-level pixels of the image. If we exhibit a sequence of thresholded images inside frame t relating to threshold t, We would initially see a black image at that point and the white spots associated with the local intensity minima would appear. All pixels below the threshold would be white, and all pixels above or equal to the threshold would be black. Gradually the white level becomes greater. Over a period, these white spots will merge until the whole image is white. Edge Histogram Descriptor (EHD)

An EHD is a type of feature vector that depicts the spatial distribution of five types of edges. A neighborhood is a set of five edges that are relative to one another and may be considered a sub-image or an image block. The sub-image is found by partitioning the available image space into 4 x 4 non-overlapping blocks. In this way, the image partition makes 16 equivalent estimated blocks that are independent of the size of the initial image.

Feature Selection

Feature selection, also termed as a selection in variables or attribute selection, is the technique for choosing a subset of features (variables, indicators) that are used in model construction. Discrete Particle Swarm Optimization (DPSO) is a kind of optimization technique that falls under the category of an Iterative optimization technique that optimizes a candidate solution by attempting to improve it based on a proportion of input value.

Results and Discussion

The proposed framework is extended to classify normal control patients and MCI patients. Different classification algorithms are used and clearly, from Figure 2 the ensemble classifier outperforms the other classifiers like SVM, KNN, and Naïve Bayes. The Ensemble classifier produces an accuracy of 86%. Other performance metrics that are calculated are precision, recall, F-measure, and specificity. The specificity for all the other classifiers is 100%.

Future Work

Several ideas are outlined that can be used to extend the scope of this research work to diagnose and classify patients with multiclass diseases like CN, MCI, and AD. The region of interest and the background of medical images, which often depict clinically relevant regions and clinically irrelevant backgrounds, may be separately coded at different quality levels.

Conclusion

A clear investigation of the type of classification on AD is done using the classification techniques and the multimodal strategy which will aid the neuro medical clinicians and doctors to identify and to provide a follow-up for the patients with an accuracy of 86% using the MRI and PET images. The given method is based on the multimodal fusion strategy and the texture-based features are obtained with the hybrid of GLDM, MSER, EHD from which the optimal set of features is further extracted.

Surface Defect Detection for Wet Blue Leather Using Deep Learning Approach

Vinith Kumar31

Department of Computer Science Engineering, Hindustan Institute of Technology and Science, Chennai, India

DOI: 10.1201/9781003430452-39

Abstract

Due to the diverse nature of defects and the lack of publicly available data for algorithm benchmarking, automated visual inspection for leather defect detection is a challenging endeavor in the leather industry. The existing Leather Defect Detection methods are mostly done with manual inspection or during the later stage of the finished leather product. Traditional machine learning methods use hand-crafted features from the textural or transform domain, which takes a lot of computational time and it is hard to generalize. The proposed Leather Defect Detection method using Convolution Neural Network for blue wet leather identifies the defect in the earlier stage with 93.4% accuracy and lessens the processing cost and yields profit to the manufacturers. The IoT module in the proposed model sends the results of leather defect detection to the administrators and makes them monitor the process from a remote place by automating the defect detection process by reducing time and increasing the profit.

Keywords: Convolutional Neural Network, Data augmentation, Pre-trained models, Image processing, Computer vision, Blue wet leather

Introduction

The leather industry is always looking for ways to cut costs while simultaneously increasing productivity and product quality. The detection of flaws in leather hides and skins is one crucial step toward achieving this objective. The time-consuming and error-prone process of manual inspection can clog the leather processing pipeline. Defect detection efficiency and accuracy can be enhanced by automated visual inspection systems, which can also reduce rejection costs. The convolutional neural networks (CNNs), focus on the detection of flaws in blue wet leather in this study. This procedure aids in the identification of flaws that may not be apparent in dry leather. The public dataset of blue wet leather images is used for transfer learning and data augmentation techniques to train and test the model.

Stages in Leather processing:

  1. Pre-Treatment: The raw hides are prepared for processing at this stage.
  2. Tanning: The hides are treated with a tanning agent during the tanning process. Among the various kinds of tanning agents are mineral salts.
  3. Neutralization: The hides are treated with acid after they have been tanned to bring the pH level back to neutral and remove any excess tanning agent.
  4. Dyeing: the leather can be dyed to the desired color.
  5. Finishing: After that, the leather is finished to get the texture and appearance you want. Sanding, embossing, buffing.

Challenges in the Leather Defect Detection:

There are a number of reasons why leather defect detection can be difficult, including:

  1. 1.3 Leather quality variation: The quality of the leather can be significantly influenced by the raw materials’ origin, tanning method, and finishing techniques.
  2. 1.4 The variety of leather’s patterns and textures: Defects in leather can be difficult to spot due to its sometimes-intricate patterns and textures.
  3. 1.5 Individuality: Cowhide imperfection identification frequently includes visual assessment by human administrators.
  4. 1.6 There is a limited supply of high-quality training data: High-quality labeled data are needed to train machine learning models for leather defect detection.

Blue Wet Leather Stage:

Leather that has been tanned but has not yet been dried is known as “blue wet.” Due to the tanning process, the leather is still wet and has a bluish hue at this point. Tannins are added to hides or skins during the tanning process to stabilize and preserve them. The “blue wet” stage of leather processing is crucial because it’s when the leather is stretched and shaped to get the thickness, texture, and size you want.

The structure of the paper is as follows: In section 2, various use cases of deep learning are discussed, and in section 3, the related work on deep learning in leather defect detection is covered. Section 4 illustrates the existing leather detection. The proposed word on deep learning-based leather detection is presented in Section 4, and the conclusion is presented in Section 5.

Use cases of Deep Learning

Neural networks with multiple layers are used in deep learning, a subset of machine learning, to solve complex problems. It has emerged as a crucial instrument in a number of fields, including:

Recognizing images and videos: With high accuracy, deep learning models can recognize things, people, and activities in images and videos.

Natural processing of language: In order to comprehend and generate human language, deep learning is utilized.

Robotics: Robots can be taught to perform complex tasks like grasping objects, navigating environments, and interacting with humans using deep learning.

Healthcare: Analyzing medical images, diagnosing diseases, and creating individualized treatment plans are all possible applications of deep learning.

Related Work

In the existing leather detection system, to deal with voltage fluctuations brought on by an unstable power grid and speed changes brought on by transmission roller damage, Li Hongwei’s The Internet plus leather shotcrete machine system makes use of the Internet of Things’ CMT-SVR-200 technology, which features error-resistant transmission, double closed-loop speed regulation, and more (Jiyi et at., 2022). The shotcrete machine can precisely spray leather and simultaneously measure the leather as it goes through the photoelectric detection box. Customers will find it easier to inspect the goods as a result of this system.

The detriments of the ability to prepare in view of conventional businesses slowly become evident because of the quick progression of science and innovation. Universities’ efforts to cultivate talent face new challenges as a result of the profession’s slow growth, which frequently results in a lack of professional identity(Aslam et al., 2021). The impact of the leather industry on information technology and the direction of higher education for leather professionals are examined. Automation’s expansion in the leather industry, automated leather defect classification has received a lot of attention. In recent years, numerous novel strategies to improve the automated defect classification pipeline have been presented (Mantari et at., 2022). The creation of new ideas is the primary objective of this study, as methods for the detection of leather defects, and the formulation of recommendations for the identification and selection of models.

A novel approach to resolving a number of tasks related to the labor market is provided by CNC machine control. One of the processes is sorting crust leather from various animal species used to sort leather. This procedure is typically carried out by hand and takes a significant amount of time by a group of experts (Vasagam et al., 2022). Consequently, the authors created INT_LEA_IMG_CLRI_UNOM, a brand-new dataset consisting of 609 images from the Training and Testing datasets. The LAPLACIAN, MEDIAN, SOBEL, ROBERTS, SCHARR, PREWITT, and GAUSSIAN pre-processing filters and Contrast Limited Adaptive Histogram Equalization (CLARE) are used to improve the images. The proposed approach’s classification accuracy is significantly confirmed by employing a 79% accurate Naive Bayes classifier.

Existing Model for Leather Defect Detection

Over the past ten years, numerous machine-vision-based methods for inspecting surface imperfections, including surface imperfections in leather, have been developed. The two primary types of these techniques are machine learning, which is based on handcrafted features or shallow learning techniques, and traditional image processing. In machine learning-based approaches, feature extraction and pattern classification are typically combined. The defect-detection feature vector’s design is based on an examination of the input image’s characteristics. Visual review is emotional and can be affected by variables like lighting conditions and individual mastery. Image processing algorithms can be effective at detecting specific types of defects, but may struggle with variations in lighting or color.

Convolutional neural networks (CNNs), which are based on deep learning, have demonstrated promising results for accurately identifying various leather defects. With more training data, these methods can get better over time, learn patterns, and analyze a lot of data.

Proposed Leather Defect Detection using CNN

Defects in leather are analogous to flaws in the leather surface. The majority of leather defects are brought on by problems with machines or processes. The sale and use of textiles are greatly diminished when leather has defects. In order to continue expanding and remaining competitive, textile manufacturing businesses need to upgrade their technology and equipment. The image was converted to greyscale using the sharpening, median, smooth, binary mask, RGB extraction, histogram, and Sobel operator algorithms.

A Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) is a type of neural network that is mostly used to process images, classify, segment, and deal with other auto-correlated data. It has one or more Convolutional layers. Start with a straightforward CNN that has one hidden layer with approximately ten kernels in dimension 3 and one max pooling layer as a general rule to find damaged components and transmit them thru the microcontroller and store them in the IOT webpage. IoT (Internet of Things) can be highly relevant in leather defect detection by enabling real-time monitoring of environmental conditions such as temperature, humidity, and pressure.

Working of leather detection:

  1. The initial step in leveraging the Internet of Things for defect detection involves installing sensors in the leather processing line, which can monitor various parameters such as temperature, humidity, and pressure. In order to ensure the ideal environmental conditions necessary for accurate defect assessment and prevention, leather defect detection necessitates the capture of pressure, humidity, and temperature.
  2. The sensor data can be collected and transmitted to a centralized server or cloud-based platform for processing.
  3. To enable real-time defect detection, the trained models can be deployed on edge devices such as cameras or sensors.
  4. The edge devices can capture images of the leather, which can then be sent to a central server for analysis.
  5. Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) and other deep learning methods can be used by the central server to examine the images and spot any potential flaws.
  6. Upon categorizing the identified defects into various categories, a report can be generated to guide operators in taking the appropriate action.
  7. To optimize the production process and minimize wastage, the system can be integrated with other systems, including the production management system.
  8. By leveraging the data collected by sensors, the machinery used in the leather processing line can benefit from predictive maintenance.

Conclusion

Due to the diverse nature of leather defects and the lack of annotated data for algorithm benchmarking, automated visual inspection faces significant challenges. Transfer learning and data augmentation techniques can improve performance on limited data, and CNNs can automatically learn features from raw data. The proposed leather defect detection system using CNN makes the process easier and simpler as the results of defects are communicated using IoT module directly to the administrators. This CNN-based defect detection method for finding flaws in blue wet leather defect detection using DL, produces high accuracy rates of up to 93.4%. The data set consists of near 1000 images and the experiment is done 6 to check the accuracy the data set consists of peepholes, folding of leather, etc. The experimental results show that detection of leather defect in earlier blue wet stage waives the processing cost and yields profits to manufacturers compared to other detecting methods which detect defect of completely processed leather. The future work will be extended by detecting the defects in the earlier stage of leather with fur using deep learning approach.

Attack Detection for Stock Trading Application Using Unsupervised Machine Learning

V. Ajay Sam, Nikita Singh, S. Revathy, M. Shakeel, and S. Sathya Priya

Department of Computer Science & Engineering, Hindustan Institute of Technology and Science, Chennai, India.

E-mail: ajaysam600@gmail.com, nikitasumo2000@gmail.com, srevathy@hindustanuniv.ac.in, mohamed.shakeel14@gmail.com, sathyap@hindustanuniv.ac.in

DOI: 10.1201/9781003430452-40

Abstract

The use of stock trading applications are widespread among users and plays a crucial role in the global economy. Any attack or disruption in stock trading can incur serious consequences for businesses, investors, and the economy as a whole. The existing stock trading applications are collecting sensitive information from the users and storing it in their centralized servers which are vulnerable to various active attacks. The conventional supervised machine learning algorithms which are used to detect the attack in stock trading applications are only suitable to detect known attacks. To detect the unknown attack and to reduce the computational time of the attack detection, the One-Class Support Vector Machine (OCSVM), is an unsupervised machine learning model with feature discretization and feature selection proposed. The model outperforms the existing model with an accuracy of 99.1% by reducing the computational time of attack detection by identifying and mitigating the potential threats against investors.

Keywords: Attack detection, One Class SVM, Stock trading, Unsupervised learning, Feature discretization

Introduction

Numerous stock trading platforms gather all the sensitive and behavioral information of the users and store it in centralized servers. Supervised machine learning algorithms are used for detecting well-known attack types and their variants. The known and unknown attacks are only detectable by unsupervised machine learning techniques. In active attacks, the attacker tries to sabotage the message’s content by intercepting the connection. In the passive attack, the attacker spoofs the traffic information without causing damage to the network. The detection of attacks in the network is efficient when it detects with a higher accuracy rate and lesser computational time.

Characteristics of Attack Detection

Anomaly detection

Attack detection should be able to detect peculiar patterns of behavior and network activities that deviate from the normal pattern.

Multi-level detection

The attack detection should detect intrusions at multiple levels, including network, application, and user levels, to ensure comprehensive coverage.

Scalability

The attack detection should be able to manage vast volumes of data and scale up to meet the needs of a growing organization.

Low false positives

The attack detection should have a low false positive rate to minimize the number of false alarms and allow security teams to focus on real threats.

Integration

The attack detection should be able to integrate with other security tools and solutions to provide a comprehensive security framework.

To enhance the security and integrity of the stock market, a more efficient attack detection system is developed utilizing OCSVM along with feature selection and discretization techniques. The new system aims to address the limitations of the existing attack detection systems and enable quicker identification and mitigation of attacks. Its ultimate goal is to provide better protection to the stock market against potential security threats.

The structure of the paper is organized as follows, Section 2 covers the use cases of attack detection and 3 covers the related work of attack detection in stock trading, Section 4 illustrates the current attack detection model for stock trading, Section V provides the results and discussion of the proposed model, and Section VI provides the conclusion.

Use Cases of Attack Detection

Individual Investors

Individual investors can use attack detection systems to monitor their investments and protect themselves from financial fraud. By analyzing market data for anomalies or patterns that indicate an attack (Zhang et al., 2017), investors can adjust their investment strategies and avoid making costly mistakes.

Hedge funds and Asset Managers

It relies on accurate and timely market data to make investment decisions. Attack detection systems can help these firms identify potential threats to their portfolios, such as market manipulation or insider trading, and adjust their investments accordingly.

Regulators

Regulators such as the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) are responsible for monitoring the stock market for illegal activity (Hu et al., 2018) and ensuring that market participants follow the rules. Attack detection systems can help regulators identify potential violations of securities laws, investigate suspicious activity, and enforce compliance.

Trading platforms

Trading platforms such as stock exchanges or electronic trading networks are responsible for maintaining a fair and orderly market. Attack detection systems can help these platforms identify potential threats to market integrity, such as algorithmic trading glitches or market manipulation, and take appropriate action to prevent further harm.

Financial news outlets

Financial news outlets rely on accurate and timely market data to report on stock market trends and provide analysis to their readers(F. Aslam and H.-G. Kang, 2015). Attack detection systems can help these outlets identify potential threats to market stability, such as sudden drops in trading volume or sharp price movements, and provide timely updates to their readers.

Related Work

In the Network Anomaly Detection Algorithm solely analyses unlabeled data to identify traffic anomalies (Casas et al., 2012). By using the trace modification program called Flame, the authors have built many attack types to test the methodology (Wagner et al., 2012). Additionally, the true positive and average accuracy rates are insufficient to identify the intrusion in order to preserve the availability and confidentiality of the network resources. It is also necessary to evaluate false positive and false negative rates(Almseidin et al., 2017) for attack detection. To identify attacks without any prior knowledge, the SSC-OCSVM unsupervised anomaly detection system coupled with one-class support vector machines and subspace clustering (Pu, et at., 2021). This algorithm’s use of feature selection has been successful in accelerating testing, although it will somewhat impair accuracy( [L. Hakim et al, 2019). With the Kaggle dataset, supervised learning, which involves utilizing techniques such as Random Forest, Decision Tree, and Logistic Regression, is employed to make precise predictions about stock prices. This method relies on historical data from the preceding year and daily trading prices to forecast the stock prices of the target company (Yelne and Theng, 2021).

The market is highly unpredictable, and making forecasts based on disorderly and time-sensitive data is challenging, making stock movement prediction a difficult problem. Using a fresh stock movement prediction dataset, cutting-edge performance is proposed in the suggested model (Xu and Cohen, 2018). Artificial catastrophes and terrorism have drawn the public’s attention to how these events affect the economy and the stock market. This study investigates how natural disasters affect people (Tavor and Teitler-Regev, 2019). The above study brings out the challenges of the existing attack detection models by stating that unsupervised machine learning models are the finest for detecting unknown attacks. To reduce computational time, unsupervised learning can be integrated with feature selection and feature discretization methods.

Proposed Attack Detection model

The various phases of the proposed attack detection model are illustrated in Fig. 1.

Initialization

Initialization phase involves setting up the necessary hardware and software, installing any required libraries or frameworks, and configuring the system to connect to relevant data sources. It is also important to ensure that the system is specifically engineered to effectively handle vast quantities of data efficiently and effectively since the stock market generates vast amounts of data daily.

Feature Selection

Feature selection might involve identifying key market indicators, such as trading volume or price changes, that are likely to be affected by attacks. Different techniques can be used to select features, such as statistical analysis, domain expertise, or machine learning algorithms. The goal of feature selection is to decrease the complexity of data while obtaining as many relevant details as possible, which can improve the accuracy and efficiency of an attack detection system. Chi-square test has been an important phase in the feature selection method that identifies relevant features.

Feature Discretization

Feature discretization involves dividing trading volume into high, medium, and low categories, or dividing price changes into positive, negative, or neutral categories. Different methods can be used for feature discretization, such as binning, clustering, or decision trees. The goal of feature discretization is to simplify the data while preserving important information, which can make it easier to detect anomalies and attacks.

One Class Support Vector Machine (OCSVM)

One-class SVMs might be used to identify unusual patterns in trading volume, price changes, or other market indicators that could indicate an attack. One-class SVMs are trained on normal data and can identify outliers that are different from the normal patterns. They can be useful for detecting attacks that are not well-defined or for which there is limited training data.

Attack Detection

Many different types of attacks can occur in the stock market, such as insider trading, market manipulation, or distributed denial of service attacks. Detecting attacks requires a combination of domain expertise, statistical analysis, and machine learning algorithms. Once an attack is detected, the system should alert users and provide them with relevant information, such as the type of attack, the time it occurred, and the potential impact on the market.

Results and Discussions

The proposed attack detection model uses the NSL-KDD dataset. The following outcomes are attained using the supervised machine learning techniques like support vector machine (SVM), K-nearest neighbor (KNN), and random forest (RF), as well as our suggested method OCSVM with feature selection and feature discretization as illustrated in Fig. 2. Recall is defined as the ratio of true positives to false negatives. Precision refers to the accuracy of detection of genuine attacks without false alarms. Calculating accuracy is done by dividing the total number of forecasts by the number of accurate predictions. The Recall, Precision and Fl score of the model is 98.3,99.7 and 99.1 respectively. The computational time of the model is reduced from 235s to 101s by the use of feature selection and discretization methods.

Conclusion

The proposed attack detection system for stock trading applications using unsupervised machine learning has the potential to detect unknown attacks efficiently with accuracy of 99.1% and reduce computational time. It ensures investor confidence and prevents financial losses due to attacks. The efficiency is achieved by including the feature selection and feature discretization methods. Future research work will be extended by capturing real-time data from various sources to automatically detect potential attacks using machine learning.
