Application Development for Solving the Farmer Yield Problem Using Cloud Computing

J. Jeron Berselin, R. Muthukani, N. Arunthathi and J. Frank Vijay

Department of Information Technology, KCG College of Technology, Chennai, India

E-mail: jrnbrsln@gmail.com, mahirajan279@gmail.com, jeirus.jeff@gmail.com

DOI: 10.1201/9781003430452-52

Abstract

The absence of warehouses and proper market places, suppress the farmers, and they are not able to sell their yields for a reasonable price. So, they are in a situation to depend on a mediator and local traders for selling their crops. Farmers are not given reasonable prices by the mediators and farmers are unable to live a happy life. They are really affected by some external factors such as broker commission, transport charges, and importantly they are completely dependent on the rate/price that the broker fixes. This paper presents an approach to create a farmer-friendly application that would enable them to sell their commodities to clients directly at a fair market price without the need of any middlemen. The buyer and seller concept is implemented and the yield of the crops are sold to the buyers without any hurdles. The Google app engine is used to find the location of the farmers and the customers can easily identify the crop products which are near to them.

Keywords: cloud computing; agriculture; Google app engine.

Introduction

Cloud computing is an on-demand Automatic Data Processing system resource that is one of the biggest human resource providers and also particularly contains knowledge storage and computing power. The term Cloud mostly wants to describe the knowledge centers on the current market to several users via the internet. The main benefit of Cloud Computing is it mainly reduces the IT costs that is it reduces the cost of maintaining the IT system. Clouds are limited to a single organization which is enterprise clouds or are offered for sale to numerous enterprises via public cloud. Cloud computing is mostly based on resource sharing and also includes sharing of databases, networking, and software.

Farming is the backbone of any country. In agriculture, the yield is the activity of the amount of crops adult or a product created per unit space of land. the most drawback of the farmers is marketing their yield crops with profit. The farmers cannot bear the transportation charges and lots of farmers cannot ready to afford storage facilities. And also, the most significant issue faced by the farmers is promoting competition and also the demand for the merchandise. The yield from the farmers is stored in a storage go down (Warehouse) and it takes a lot of time for them to sell the yield in a certain quantity and finish them without any wastage. This application presented in this paper will remove the concept of waste and get the yield sold in the correct amount and the full amount. The intermediate seller often known as broker, is avoided in this application as the selling of yield is happening directly between the farmers and the buyers. The application is designed and created for easy and profitable usage for the farmers.

This application will help the farmers to sell their yield products directly to the customers without any hurdles. There will be no fear to lose income for both the farmers and buyers whose livelihood is dependent on this field. The Application helps the farmers to sell their yield through this platform and also, they can determine their price to the buyers. This helps in faster selling of their yield without it going to ruins, and yield profit also. Buyers who are looking for a yield product also can get the yields they want for a reasonable price. The information of both customers and farmers is stored in the Cloud and the product is sold with the amount and Quantity recorded for future clearance. This helps in calculating the profit from this application process.

Related Work

A methodology and an application can be developed to assist the farmers by producing reports on weather forecasts, information about crops, and farming tools and trends. It was a cloud-based application that supports the farmer to know about the weather condition and cultivate accordingly (Peng & Wang, 2014).

Cloud Agro System (Jansirani et al., 2022) gcontributes to the agriculture of Bhutan. This cloud-based technology concentrated on e-knowledge for farmers, communication between farmers and traders, connecting demand and supply, and research outcomes of farmer-related issues. Sunidhi et al., (2018) presented a detailed survey on Cloud based Android applications that provide a solution for the day-to-day issues and challenges faced by the farmers. The authors suggested that an application must have information on soil, crop varieties to grow, market pricing, types of fertilizer and pesticides, and instructions on how to boost agricultural yield in order to be valuable to farmers. Soil Water Content (SWC) measurement technology was presented in Bo & Wang (2011). It offered a cloud based IoT system which used M2X from AT&T, an Internet of Things (IoT) data storage, service, and management system. Information including the kind of soil needed for plantations, details on the seasons, the optimal fertilizer for growth, etc. was presented in the system Vijayaraghavan & Kumaresan (2015).

The attractive feature of this work is that the system provides information in native regional language which can be easily understandable for farmers. Peng et al., (2014) introduced the idea of GIS based on cloud computing; based on the most popular trends in developing GIS applications today and essential cloud GIS technologies that store Geographical based data in the cloud. It was discussed how we handle agricultural data, examine its qualities, and develop a smart farm management information system

The farmer buyer/seller existing system only has the means to sell the yield with the price. The existing application has weather forecasts and other crop-related videos and news. The Security of the existing application is simple authentication with passwords and storage of data is not vast. Also, the existing system does not provide an option to chat with farmer directly. So, communication is a great barrier. Due to this, there may be a chance of getting a misunderstanding between the customer and farmer. And mainly the existing system does not provide any sort of live location tracking.

Farm Management Process

Farm management is a difficult and time-consuming job that entails a variety of tasks. Figure 1 depicts the farm management business process. In addition to managing crops, farms must also manage inputs, quality, and inventories. They must also analyze profitability and manage finances

Farm managers create standardized technical planting instructions to direct and guide fieldwork. Thus, technicians oversee workers as they plant crops in accordance with a sowing plan and technical sowing guidelines. At the same time, they record field operations data and images using Mobile Operation Records System on smartphones or Personal Digital Assistants, including the overall agricultural input, such as labor. These records are then collected in production archives after being uploaded to a distant data server. These production archives serve as informational documentation of the entire process, from product planting to delivery for each batch. Raw materials are selected, delivered, weighed, and stored in accordance with the daily harvest plan. Various product batches may be produced or packed with various material batches before being delivered for sale.

Farm managers can acquire information about the production process and create statistics summarizing sowing areas and cost of production based on the collected data. When acquiring agricultural goods, information on each type of agricultural resource is put into the DFMS. Information on each pesticide’s safety window is available in the agricultural material information database. To help with pesticide use, the HTTP protocol can be used to download safety interval data for pesticides to the MORS. Additionally, farm managers can study the use of pesticides and assess the safety of the production process. Managers can examine each batch of products, analyze the cost structure of the product, evaluate, and award planting technicians based on the whole process of the information for planting, processing, and delivery.

Proposed System

The mentioned architecture diagram consists of admin, client, user, database, and functionalities present in it. The proposed architecture diagram (Fig. 2) represents the basic components when the application is in use & (Fig. 3) explains the detailed structure of the working system. The data for this application is supplied to the server by the user module. The data components include things like location data and login credentials. All queries to the database are passed from the server and are sent to the database, which is linked to the server, where the data is obtained. The user has the option to select the crop yield that the customer genuinely needs. Additionally, the user has the option of selecting their current location manually or automatically. After successfully selecting the crops the customer can chat with the farmer directly through this application. The live location is very comfortable for the customer to choose their yield crop products within their location. Between both the user and the system, the API serves as an intermediary. It is also used to ensure security, control, and authentication. Servers, clients, and resources make up the client-server architecture, and HTTP is used to manage requests. The crop details, farmer’s and customer’s details, and transaction history are stored in the database.

The Application will help selling/buying the yield directly without any intermediate sellers. Additionally, the scope of increasing the profit for the farmers is high with this solution. The Application has the exact location where the yield/product is and the buyer can contact and get their product. The security of this application is high compared to the existing system as it uses cloud storage for storing seller data and buyer’s data. Without any wastage to their yield due to intermediate resources to carry their yield, this application helps in selling the yield quickly without wastage.

The application has a search algorithm where the different yield products are searched according to the buyers and the results will be displayed. The Application has the location of the sellers (farmers), it shows the location and the quality available to them. The Live location of the yield and farmers are used with Dijkstra’s Algorithm: Shortest path. Chat facilities are also available through which the farmer and the customer can communicate easily.

The Advantages of this application are First, it is easy to use and the User Interface is adaptable for all types of users. Secondly, the Security in this application is secure as it uses the firebase. Thirdly, the media files and other data can be easily stored with the use of Firebase database. And also, the overall Storage in this application is easy and constantly maintained. Importantly it is more flexible for the customers to use day-to-day. And finally, the product and price can be legit compared with other third-party sources.

Results & Discussion

In this paper, the proposed system was developed in Java, and JAX-WS (Java API for XML Web Services) was used to create the required web services. A cloud-based system consisting of a five-tiered architectural model was adopted for the system in order to handle a sizeable number of users, credibility, security, and expandability. Any terminal device (laptop compute; tablet, or smartphone) with a web browser and an Internet connection can access the proposed system because it has a browser-server design. Every field operation sequence’s agricultural inputs and labor details were monitored and noted to keep track of the planting process for concurrence with technical standards. (Refer Fig. 4)

The proposed system integrates mobile phone, cloud computing & past details to arrive at the precise management needs for multi-batch and multi-crop products found on the farm. The proposed system (Fig. 5) not only complies with farm data management requirements, but it also makes it possible to effectively and precisely track and trace each batch’s production process.

Conclusion

Commission agents conduct their own business by proclaiming high interest in the yield crops. With this situation, a farmer cannot afford such high interest without any gain to their own products. In this project we conclude by saying, the agricultural sector is one of the main sources of income of a country, and the undergoing process of e-communication with the recent IT technologies can bring about many changes. This application will increase the economic development in farming with selling the agricultural product at good and value prices. This application can also help the agriculture development in our country with techniques that evolved over time. Also, this application will help to maintain a balanced relationship with farmers and customers. Also, each and every farmer can gain high profits in a legit and simple way.

AI Enabled E-Commerce Studio Website

V. Rajkumaran,40

Abstract

Artificial Intelligence can automate tasks and simplify complex processes to make decisions based on customer’s reviews and comments. The application of artificial intelligence in the website gives a user-friendly approach to the customers. This paper focuses on how to build up a site with the help of AI technology in which individuals can be ready to distinguish the studio, photographic artist, and editor’s dependent on individuals like magazines, corporate occasions, birthday celebrations, weddings, occasions, and so forth. AI algorithms now evaluate user data and influence millions of people’s decision-making processes in areas such as loan rates, employment, and criminal justice (Vijayaraghavan et al., 2021). They play crucial parts in a variety of businesses. Still they have drawbacks that can lead to discrimination (Akter & Wamba, 2016) and erroneous decision-making. For example, news recommendations and algorithms to target certain audiences in online sites have recently gotten a lot of press for exacerbating the lack of knowledge variety on the platform (S. I. et al., 2020). An important problem is that decision-making systems that run via algorithms provide relevant information and the best options themselves instead of letting the users choose based on the list of recommended items like how recommender systems do. To bring this to notice, In order to mitigate the potential adverse effects of nascent AI autonomous systems, Vlasselaer et al., (2015)proposes the use of collaborative task representations that incorporate both machine learning models and human expertise. They provide instances of interactive systems that have active computational assistance. They argue that context-aware systems should not replace human decision-making. To ensure accountability for both the system and its users, they advocate for granting users control over the system. Being transparent can assist avoid blind trust by providing crucial information for decision-making that would otherwise be unavailable to end-users (Ignatov et al., 2019). The advantages of algorithmic openness and comprehensibility are manifold, including the detection of partiality and prejudice (Bahnsen et al., 2015; Dhanalakshmi & Devi, 2020), enhancing user cognizance of the system’s conduct (S. I. et al., 2020), offering understandable actions by intelligent systems (K. N. et al., 2020), and guaranteeing user answerability (Ignatov et al., 2019). There is also a growing body of evidence highlighting the negative effects of algorithmic decision-making, particularly with regard to discrimination and legal challenges. Consequently, researchers are advocating for AI to be subjected to legal oversight and accountability in order to promote openness and transparency (Halbe & Joshi, 2015). Recommender systems, which may be found in news channels, social networking sites, and e-commerce, have become more and more important in consumers’ day-to-day online activities. By proposing more of what we desire, machine learning algorithms that learn from our preferences and biases enhance those preferences and biases.

Although the term “recommendation system” might seem to be brand-new, it was first used in the 1990s. His early research, which was inspired by people’s challenges in finding and choosing products in the face of the overwhelming amount of information available on the internet, concentrated on Information retrieval, forecasting theory, management, and marketing are all related to cognitive sciences (Vijayaraghavan et al., 2021).

As a result, the recommendation system has evolved as a business opportunity that uses the vast amount of data and knowledge accessible to generate profit desirably, in addition to solving a problem. Many consider Tapestry, which was developed at the time, to be the first recommendation system. Because in this approach, information was filtered by a team of people working together, he coined the term “collaborative filtering.” Initially, the term “collaborative filtering” was used to refer to any suggestion technique, but the creators started referring to it as a “recommendation system” since not every system requires the usage of the collaborative technique. Almost every service we use on a regular basis now uses recommendation algorithms, including social networks, ecommerce, and even app stores. Despite their differences, they all have one thing in common: the necessity to deal with a significant volume of data. The technology then assists in organizing the data in some more appealing manner, therefore improving EXPERIENCE of the user. System Process Flow

This paper explains the process of applying AI memory based techniques for a website and the suggestions for the products are based on the user’s comments and reviews. The entire architecture flow of the process is diagrammatically shown below (Fig. 3).

Technology Adopted

A set of tactics and algorithms known as recommender systems enable users to receive recommendations for “relevant” content. The recommended products should be applicable towards the user to encourage interaction. Recommender systems prioritize the most important information and arrange it in order of relevance for the user. The system must evaluate relevance primarily based on past data. Recommender systems apply two sorts of machine learning computations, namely content-based and collaborative filtering, to sort the data.

While collaborative approaches leverage interactions, methods based on contents use item attribute similarity to determine similarity (Fig. 4).

This webpage was generated using the collaborative filtering technique. The initial step in creating a system that can recommend products to customers based on similar users’ interests is identifying analogous individuals or items. The second stage involves predicting ratings from users for products that have not yet been rated. A collection of methods known as collaborative filtering uses various ways to find comparable individuals or objects as well as various ways to generate ratings that are relevant to ratings of alike users. The similarity is not calculated in collaborative filtering utilizing parameters, examples of such data could be user age, film category, or any other relevant details on clients or goods. The explicit or implicit rating of a product is used to calculate the similarity. One technique to assess the outcome’s accuracy is to look at the square root of the mean of the squared differences between predicted and actual values, commonly referred to as RMSE that allows users to forecast ratings for test datasets of consumer pairings with previously identified rating values. The error would be the difference between the known and projected values. (Fig. 4).

Computing the RMSE involves calculating the square root of the mean of all standard errors in the test set.

To compute the rating (R) that a customer (U) is likely to assign to an item (I), the subsequent procedures are followed:

  • Identify other users who have reviewed the same product (I) as user U.
  • Use the ratings of those users to calculate The R (rating) that U (user) would allocate to item I.
  • The algorithm utilizes a roster of users who share similarities with user U. to determine their rating (R) for a given product I.
  • As per the algorithm, the rating (R) provided by user U for item I is expected to be in proximity to the mean of ratings given to I by the top 5 or top 10 users who share the highest similarity with user U.

The equation used to compute the mean of evaluations provided by n users is expressed as:

(1)
$$R_{U} = (\sum\limits_{u = 1}^{n}R_{u})/n$$

The formula for determining the mean score given by n comparable users is as shown below:

Average Rating = Sum of Ratings Provided by n Similar Users / n

In other words, the mean rating given by the n comparable users can be obtained by dividing the total sum of the ratings given by them by the number of users similar to user U. The above-mentioned equation is frequently utilized in collaborative filtering methods to anticipate the rating that a user might assign to a specific item by taking into account the evaluations provided by comparable users.

Correlational and Sentimental Analysis Using LSTM to Forecast Stock Price

E. Pavithra41

DOI: 10.1201/9781003430452-54

Abstract

This research paper proposes an innovative technique for forecasting stock market trends and analysis by incorporating the interdependence of stocks, risk-identification, and sentiment analysis of financial news. Our approach utilizes data analysis techniques, correlation identification, natural language processing used for sentimental analysis with long short-term memory (LSTM) model. We apply Pearson correlation coefficient to identify the correlation between the top stocks and their interdependence. The proposed model incorporates identified risks associated with market movements, such as political instability, and economic changes to enable more comprehensive stock market analysis. Sentiment analysis is performed using natural language processing techniques, which allows the model to analyse financial news sentiment scores to predict the coming trend in the market. LSTM, a type of deep learning algorithm, is applied to analyse time series data, including historical data and trends, to predict future stock prices. The proposed model improves the accuracy of stock market forecasting and provides investors with a more informed decision-making approach that reduces their risk exposure. Overall, the proposed model for stock market prediction and analysis provides a comprehensive, efficient approach to analyzing the stock market movement, and it has the potential to help investors make profitable trading decisions.

Keywords: LSTM, Correlation, Risk identification, NLP

Introduction

The stock market is an essential element of the financial industry that greatly boosts the economic development of a nation. The stock market is used as a benchmark to compare the economic growth of different countries, and its performance is closely monitored by investors, speculators, and financial analysts. Forecasting the movements of the stock market can be a difficult undertaking as it involves dealing with the intricate workings of the market and the unpredictability of constantly changing data. However, accurate predictions can provide valuable insights into the market’s trends and enable investors to make informed investment decisions, thus helping to improve the country’s economy and the financial status of everyone. Since the profit from stock market benefits for the country’s economy status also its citizens. The non-stationary nature of stock market price series presents a significant challenge for accurate prediction It is typical for stock price sequences includes lot of noise and oscillations. These characteristics making it difficult for representing the data in a meaningful way. Several techniques involve utilizing manual features like stochastic technical indicators and moving averages. Also, the advanced techniques using deep learning neural networks, and reinforcement learning have some limitations and need to be improved for the model to work more accurately. Hence, a fresh strategy for stock market forecasting and analysis is required. So, this research considers the interdependence of stocks, risks associated with market movements, and sentiment analysis of financial news.

This research paper presents a methodology for predicting and analyzing the stock market that leverages advanced data analysis techniques. Our approach utilizes the Pearson correlation coefficient to identify the co-dependency of the top stocks and identify the risks associated with market movements. We also employ natural language processing to analyze the sentiment scores of financial news for the stocks which are identified having low risk, enabling us to make more accurate predictions about the market’s future trends. Finally, we use long short-term memory (LSTM) algorithms to estimate the future values of stocks which have less risk, their sentiment scores, and the times series data. By combining these analyzed data, our proposed model aims to provide better accuracy for predictions which will give higher profits for investors.

Methodology

In this section, the proposed method has been described in detail. In our proposed model, to reduce risk correlation analysis is performed.

3 Corelation Analysis

Correlation analysis is an important statistical technique used to measure the strength of the relationship between two variables.

The Pearson correlation coefficient measures the strength of the linear association between two variables. A score of +1 represents a perfect positive correlation, while a score of 0 indicates no correlation between the variables. A score of -1 represents a perfect negative correlation.

The Pearson correlation coefficient can be calculated using the formula:


$$r = \frac{\sum\limits_{j = 1}^{n}\left( {\left( {x_{i} - \overline{x}} \right)\left( {y_{i} - \overline{y}} \right)} \right)}{\sqrt{{\sum\limits_{i = 1}^{n}\left( {x_{i} - \overline{x}} \right)^{2}}{\sum\limits_{i = 1}^{n}\left( {y_{i} - \overline{y}} \right)^{2}}}}$$

r - correlation coefficient, n is the number of observations,

Σxy - sum of the products of the paired observations,

Σx and Σy - sums of the x and y observations,

Σ^2 and Σy^2- sums of the squared x and y observations.

Correlation analysis can provide valuable insights into the relationships between different variables in research, but it is important to note that correlation does not necessarily imply causation. Other factors that are not being measured may be influencing the relationship between the variables, so it is important to interpret the results of correlation analysis carefully and consider other possible explanations for the observed correlations.

Sentimental Analysis

Sentiment analysis is a technique used in natural language processing (NLP) to identify and extract subjective information from text data. One of the most widely used sentiment analysis tools is VADER (Valence Aware Dictionary and sEntiment Reasoner) uses grammar rules and lexicons to analyze sentiment in the textual data. Unlike traditional methods that rely solely on keyword matching, VADER uses a combination of lexicon-based analysis and grammatical rules to determine the sentiment of a given text. VADER uses a sentiment lexicon that contains a list of words and their associated sentiment scores. The lexicon is specifically designed to handle sentiments expressed in social media, where conventional rules of grammar may not always apply. Each word in the lexicon is assigned a sentiment score based on its polarity (positive or negative) and intensity. For example, the word “good” has a positive polarity and a high intensity score, whereas the word “bad” has a negative polarity and a high intensity score.

To determine the sentiment of a text, VADER first tokenizes the text into individual words and punctuation marks. It then applies a set of rules to determine the overall sentiment score of the text. These rules consider factors such as capitalization, punctuation, and degree modifiers (such as “very” or “extremely”) that can affect the sentiment of a sentence.

The final sentiment score is a continuous value between -1 and 1, with negative values indicating negative sentiment, positive values indicating positive sentiment, and values close to zero indicating neutral sentiment. In addition to the overall sentiment score, VADER also provides scores for the positive, negative, and neutral sentiment expressed in the text.

Overall, the VADER algorithm provides a fast and effective way to perform sentiment analysis on textual data, particularly in the context of social media where traditional methods may not be as effective. Bottom of Form

LSTM

An LSTM (”Long Short-Term Memory”) model is a form of artificial neural network that is designed to solve the vanishing gradients issue which is occurring in traditional RNNs, that can make it difficult to train networks on long sequences of data.

The LSTM architecture (Fig. 1) consists of memory with ReLU as it activation function except for the candidate state. The LSTM model includes multiple gates which regulate how information moves through the network.

Forget Gate: The forget gate selects which data to keep or discard from the previous cell state. It receives the previous hidden state and the present input as an input and uses ReLU as an activation function.

The forget gate equation:


fg(t) = ReLU(Wm_fg ⋅ [h(t − 1), x(t)] + bv_f)

Wm_fg - weight matrix, by_f - bias term, h(t-1) previous hidden state, and x(t) - current input.

Input Gate: The input gate determines which data is added to the cell state. It also receives the previous hidden state and the current input as input and uses ReLU as an activation function. The input gate equation:


ig(t) = ReLU(Wm_ig ⋅ [h(t − 1), x(t)] + bv_i)

Wm_fg - weight matrix, bv_f - bias term, h(t-1) - previous hidden state, and x(t) - current input.

Candidate State: The candidate cell state calculates the new candidate values that can be added to the current cell state. It uses tanh as an activation function.

The candidate cell state equation:


c_hat(t) = tanh (Wm1c ⋅ [h(t − 1), x(t)] + bv_c)

Wm_c - weight matrix, bv_c - bias term, h(t-1) past hidden state, and x(t) - current input.

Current Cell State: The current cell state updates the previous cell state by removing the information that the forget gate wants to discard and adding the information that the input gate wants to add. It uses element-wise multiplication and addition operations.

The current cell state equation:


c(t) = fg(t)*c(t − 1) + ig(t)*c_hat(t)

fg(t) - output of the forget gate, fg(t) - output of the input gate, c(t-1) - previous cell state, and c_hat(t) - candidate cell state.

Output Gate: It decides which data from latest cell state to output as current hidden state. It receives past hidden state and the present input as input

The output gate equation:


$$\begin{array}{l} {out\_ g(t)\, = \, ReLU(Wm\_ out\_ g \cdot \lbrack h(t - 1),\mathbf{x}(\mathbf{t})\rbrack +} \\ {bv\_ o)} \\ \end{array}$$

Wm_og - weight matrix, bv_o - bias term, h(t- 1) - previous hidden state, and x(t) - current input.

The training of an LSTM model involves iteratively updating weights and offset values using an optimization algorithm to reduce the discrepancy between the expected output and the actual output.

Data cleaning

Times series data

For time series data, data cleaning includes removing the null values, Checking, and removing duplicate data to avoid skew analysis, handle missing data using backfilling method. When a company undergoes a stock split or pays dividends, it can affect the price and volume of data. To account for this, the data needs to be adjusted for these events. Examining extreme values and remove outliers.

Textual Data Cleaning using NLP

Data cleaning ensures that the text data is uniform, consistent, and free from any unnecessary noise. We have used NLP techniques. Table 4 shows the comparison of word counts in collected tweet dataset that was compiled before and after data cleaning process.

Table 4 Comparison of Word counts
Data cleaning Before NLP After NLP
Length 1180 1180
Words Count 28967 23200
  • The process involves removing any irrelevant or redundant information.
  • Stop words are articles or frequent words that have no meaning, such as “the,” “and,” and “a.” need to be removed.
  • It also involves removing punctuation, converting all text to lowercase, and stemming words to their base form.
  • Regular expressions can be used to remove any unwanted characters, such as HTML tags or URLs, from the text data.
  • Identifying the language of the text and filtering out non-English text as non-English words can introduce noise.

Proposed Methodology

Proposed methodology aims to reduce risk before building the model. It would help the investors to majorly focus on the least risk stocks for analyzing and prediction. Its is achieved by collecting the overall stocks on each sector or specifying index using Yahoo tickers. The proposed architecture (Fig. 2) is shown below:

After collecting the data, pre-processing should be done to avoid including invalid data. Using Pearson co-efficient, it would form a co-relation matrix for the whole collected index. Identify the positive correlation between stocks and choose those particular stocks for risk analysis and further processing.

Using the risk analysis method identify least risk data and collect times series data including (High, Low, Open, and Close) indicators. For the same identified stocks scraping tweet data and any other related data relating to the particular stocks. Vader analysis is used to calculate the sentiment scores. Integrate time series dataset with sentiment scores which is major factor in stock market for better prediction.

Experiment and Results

Correlation Matrix and Risk Analysis

Correlation matrix (Fig. 3) is constructed using Pearson co-efficient method to identify highly co-dependent stock data. This correlation matrix for 30 parameters shows positively correlated data which is data containing above 0.5 as co-efficient. Those parameters are TCS, Wipro, Bajajfinserve, Bajajfinance, IndusInd Bank, Bajajfinance, and Tech Mahindra.

Between these positive correlated data, calculate the risk value using standard deviation.


$$s = \sqrt{\frac{\sum^{}{(X - \overline{X})}^{2}}{n - 1}}$$

s- Standard Deviation,

X - Daily return,

X̄ - Average of daily return,

n - Total number of samples

It measures the degree to which an investment’s returns deviate from its average return (Fig.4). This figure represents the company risk level of each stock. It shows that TCS has a low-risk value and Induslnd Bank has a high-risk value among the correlated data.

Sentimental Analysis

In this study, we employed the VADER tool to analyze the sentiment scores of a large corpus of text data collected from Twitter. The entire sentiment of the text is captured by the compound score, which is a single value. It is determined by adding up the valence scores assigned to each word in the text and adjusting for the intensity of the sentiment, and normalizing the score to be between -1 (most negative) and +1 (most positive). The compound score provides an overall measure of the sentiment of the text, considering both positive and negative sentiment. The Vader analyzed contains positive, negative, and neutral sentiment values from the collected tweets, and compound scores is displayed as sentiment score in table 5.

Conclusion and Future Works

The proposed multi-fusion information model presented in this research paper can assist investors in minimizing the risk of loss in the stock market. The model suggests identifying co-dependency among stock data and choosing the least risky stock data for different sectors, thereby providing valuable insights to investors for choosing the least risky stock in each sector which could be ideal for making long-term or short-term investments. Using VADER analyzer, Sentimental scores were identified for the stocks and integrated with historical data of the particular stock to identify patterns and analysis using LSTM algorithm. Above factors enhance the accuracy of future stock predictions. Since the model has an accuracy level of 95 percent. Overall, the proposed model can potentially improve investment decision-making and help investors mitigate risk in the stock market. A data-driven approach is crucial in stock analysis, and investors need to carefully consider various factors when making investment decisions. Future work should focus on choosing the dataset and approach by doing extensive research on stock market domain and its trading techniques and strategies. Developing an algorithm that incorporates stock market strategies can potentially enhance the efficiency of analysis. To enhance time-series data analysis, it is necessary to detect significant patterns in different technical indicators such as on-Balance Volume, Moving average, Average directional index, oscillators. Also identifying fake contents before calculating sentiment scores. Fake contents can be avoided using information from verified accounts and reliable social platforms.

A Novel Authentication System Based on CNN and IoT

Suraj Golthi,42

Department of Computer Science and Engineering, Hindustan Institute of Technology and Science, Chennai, India

DOI: 10.1201/9781003430452-55

Abstract

For many years, researchers have been interested in the use of biometric authentication in voting systems. This study suggests an anonymous voting system that makes use of deep learning techniques and finger vein detection to enable secure and reliable voter authentication in light of the growing demand for secure and anonymous voting processes. In order to ensure voter security and authentication, this paper suggests an anonymous voting system that makes use of deep learning techniques and finger vein recognition. Voters’ finger vein images will be captured by the system, which will then classify and extract features using Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) models. An Internet Of Things (IoT) - based alert system that can alert authorities to any fraud during the voting process is also integrated into the proposed system. In conclusion, the proposed system offers a secure and anonymous voting process that uses finger vein recognition and deep learning techniques. This paper presents a detailed methodology for the development of the system, including the dataset, the CNN model, and the IoT-based alert system.

Keywords: Anonymous Voting, Biometric Authentication, Finger Vein Recognition, Deep Learning, Convolutional Neural Network, IoT-Based Alert System, Secure Voting, Fraudulent Activities

Introduction

Electronic voting systems have grown in popularity in today’s elections throughout the world with the advancement of technology. Electronic voting systems have been discovered to be open to attacks like hacking and fraudulent voting (Pooja & Anuja, 2022), raising worries about security and privacy. An anonymous voting system that uses Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) and Internet of Things (IoT) technology to distinguish verified and unverified users via finger vein recognition has been offered as a solution to these issues.

The finger vein images, which are obtained using a finger vein recognition device, serve as the system’s main dataset. The images are first cleaned up to get rid of any noise before being converted into numerical data using a variety of mathematical methods. With the help of this numerical information, a CNN model is trained to categorize the images as belonging to verified or unverified users. The system’s IoT component is used to monitor the voting process and send notifications in the event of any fraud. The data is gathered from various sensors and devices, including the finger vein recognition device, and transmitted to a central server using an Arduino microcontroller.

The proposed system differs from conventional voting procedures in a number of ways, including increased security, anonymity, and transparency. It eliminates the need for paper ballots, lowering the possibility of fraud or counting errors. The system can now provide real-time feedback thanks to the use of IoT technology, which could help to increase the effectiveness of the voting process.

The primary benefit of this system is its capacity to deliver anonymous and secure voting processes, preventing fraud while protecting voters’ privacy. For the implementation of a secure voting system, the use of finger vein recognition and deep learning techniques offers an accurate and dependable method for authentication.

This novel authentication system ensures anonymity and security during the voting process and addresses the problems with conventional voting systems. Experimental findings show the effectiveness of the proposed system, which makes it a workable option for putting in place a safe and dependable system.

Literature Survey

Artificial neural networks are used in deep learning, a branch of machine learning, to model and resolve complex issues (Boucherit & Zmirli, 2022). It is a technique for teaching artificial neural networks to spot patterns in sizable datasets, enabling machines to gain knowledge from their mistakes and become more accurate with practice (Pooja & Anuja, 2022). Deep learning models are well suited for tasks like image and speech recognition, natural language processing, and anomaly detection because they have multiple layers of interconnected neurons that can process and classify data hierarchically (Boucetta & Boussaad, 2022; Ardak & Bardekar, 2022; Khan et al., 2020).

CNNs use a set of filters that are convolved with the input data to automatically learn and extract features from raw data, such as images (Ardak & Bardekar, 2022). The feature maps that result from each filter’s detection of a particular feature—such as edges, corners, or textures—are then combined and processed to produce higher-level representations of the input data (Sruthi & Shanjai, 2021).

Merge Convolutional Neural Network (Merge CNN), an improved deep network that makes use of several CNNs with short paths is used in finger vein identification using CNN (Boucherit & Zmirli, 2022). The method is based on combining the outputs of multiple identical CNNs with various input image qualities into a single layer (AboSamra et al., 2017). They created various networks and trained them using the FV-USM dataset to accomplish this. In final they merged CNN labeled A, which combines the original image with an image enhanced using the Contrast Limited Adaptive Histogram (CLAH) method, and was constructed using the most optimal CNN architecture (Boucherit & Zmirli, 2022; Sruthi & Shanjai, 2021)

A biometric technique called finger vein recognition uses distinctive vein patterns in people’s fingers to identify them. It is a very accurate and secure authentication method that is challenging to forge or tamper with Syazana-Itqan et al., (2016); Ayed (2017). A near-infrared light source is used to take pictures of the veins in a person’s finger as part of the finger vein recognition process. The distinctive vein patterns and characteristics, such as their size, shape, and location, are then identified through analysis of these images (Cruz & Kaji, 2017; Hassan et al., 2020).

Methods for identifying finger veins fall into three categories: traditional methods, machine learning-based methods, and hybrid methods. A conventional system can function in identification mode or verification mode depending on the application’s context (Khan et al., 2020). The three main steps of the traditional recognition process are image pretreatment, feature extraction, and comparison (Picciuco et al., 2019; Ismail & Mohamed, 2019). The main benefit of the proposed system is its capacity to offer secure and anonymous voting processes, preventing fraud while protecting the privacy of voters. For the implementation of a secure voting system, the use of finger vein recognition and deep learning techniques offers an accurate and dependable method for authentication (McCorry et al., 2017).

Proposed Methodology

Convolutional neural network (CNN) and Internet of Things (IoT) technologies are used in combination in the proposed methodology for the anonymous voting system using finger vein recognition. In order to maintain voter anonymity, the system attempts to categorize users as verified or unverified based on the pattern of veins in their fingers.

System Architecture

Figure 1 depicts the basic structure we intend to achieve finger-vein inputs are taken from the datasets and processed in MATLAB for authorization using deep learning algorithms such as Convolution neural network. This is sent to a microcontroller with power supply such as Arduino. This gives access to the IoT webpage and GSM using the ethernet shield which is casted upon the microcontroller and buzzer to activate for any of the fraudulent votes being casted.

Dataset

Images from verified and unverified users are included in the dataset which are nearly about 200+ images with both left and right images of the sample users. Whether or not the user is verified is taken into account when labeling these images.

A training set and a testing set were then created from the dataset. The CNN model was trained using the training set, which includes 80% of the images. The performance of the trained model was assessed using the testing set, which includes 20% of the images.

Link: https://wwvv.kaggle.com/datasets/ryeltsin/finger-vein

Features of the Dataset

  1. Vein Patterns: This includes the arrangement, orientation, and size of the veins in the fingerprint.
  2. Intensity values: This can include the brightness and darkness of the veins, which can be used to differentiate between different regions in the fingerprint.
  3. Texture features: This can include measures of the roughness, smoothness, and regularity of the veins, which can be used to distinguish between different types of fingerprints.
  4. Wavelet transforms: This can include the decomposition of the fingerprint vein data into different frequency components, which can provide additional information about the underlying patterns in the data and so on.

Way of Approach

  • Data collection: An infrared camera is used to take pictures of the finger veins, which are then saved as a dataset.
  • Pre-processing: To reduce noise and improve the quality of the acquired images, filters like Gaussian, median, and average are applied.
  • ROI Extraction: By segmenting the vein pattern using the line tracking method, the region of interest (ROI) is extracted from the pre-processed image.
  • Feature extraction: Gabor filters, local binary patterns (LBP), and histograms of oriented gradients are some of the filters that are applied after the ROI has been extracted to extract features (HOG).
  • Classification: A CNN model is trained for classification using the extracted features. An assortment of verified and unverified users are used to train the CNN model. The test images are then categorized as verified or unverified using the trained CNN model.

Results and Analysis

The first step in preprocessing is to turn the color images into grayscale. This conversion increases contrast while reducing image data size, which can help the feature extraction algorithm perform better. The overall brightness of the image can be changed using the brightness adjustment technique. The contrast of the image may be improved, which may help the vein patterns stand out more clearly.

Contrast Limited Adaptive Histogram equalization (CLAHE) is a method that uses histogram equalization to enhance the contrast by breaking the image up into smaller sub-regions.

Image noise can be eliminated using the non-linear filtering method known as median filtering. By using median filtering, each pixel’s value is changed to correspond to that of its surrounding pixels. This method can be used to reduce noise in finger vein images and enhance the visibility of the vein patterns.

Processing finger vein images for feature extraction and classification requires important steps like edge detection and segmentation as in Fig. 6. Edge detection is the process of locating the borders between various areas of an image that could be veins or other structures. These algorithms highlight edges and other regions with a strong gradient or change in pixel values.

Here, Segmentation is the process of dividing an image into various areas or objects based on their traits or characteristics. Segmentation can be used to separate the veins in finger vein images from the surrounding tissue or other structures. Techniques like thresholding, region growing, or clustering can be used for this.

The graph that is produced can be used to determine the threshold grey value that distinguishes the vein region from the surrounding area. The image can be processed further using this threshold, such as by segmenting it or extracting its features. Overall, the vein extraction frequency graph provides a simple and effective way to identify the ROI in finger vein images, allowing for accurate and reliable vein extraction and recognition.

The accuracy of the suggested system is represented by a graph with success rate on the y-axis and the label on the x-axis. The number of images that were correctly classified is divided by the total number of images in the dataset to determine the success rate or accuracy.

The success rate is plotted against various labels or dataset categories on the graph. The labels in this project are users who have been verified and those who have not. The accuracy of the system’s classification of images under each label will be displayed on the graph.

The predictive error of classification models is measured by classification loss functions. A lower loss indicates a better predictive model when the same type of loss is compared across numerous models. Think about the situation that follows. The weighted average classification loss is denoted by L.

Conclusion and Future Work

In conclusion, this project suggests a safe and private voting system that makes use of deep learning methods and finger vein recognition. Finger vein images from verified and unverified users make up the system’s dataset, and a CNN model is used for feature extraction and classification. An IoT-based alert system that can quickly alert authorities to any potential fraud activity is integrated into the proposed system.

The integration of the IoT-based alert system further improves the proposed system’s accuracy in classifying finger vein images as verified or unverified, according to experimental results. The system’s success rate is determined by how well it can distinguish between verified and unverified users based on the images of their finger veins.

The primary benefit of the suggested system is its capacity to offer voters a private and anonymous voting process. The implementation of a secure and reliable voting system is made possible by the use of finger vein recognition and deep learning techniques, which offers an accurate and dependable method for authentication.

Future work may involve enhancing the CNN model’s accuracy and incorporating other cutting-edge deep learning methods to optimize the performance of the suggested system. Additionally, by creating a user-friendly interface and integrating it with current voting systems, the system’s usability and user experience can be enhanced.

Cryptocurrency Price Prediction Using LSTM and RNN Techniques

Raguru Madhan,43

Department of Computer Science and Engineering, Hindustan Institute of Technology and Science, Chennai, India

E-mail: tharun29072001@gmail.coml; johndp@hindustanuniv.ac.in; jaravindhar@hindustanuniv.ac.in;

DOI: 10.1201/9781003430452-56

Abstract

The use of cryptocurrency has been steadily increasing in recent years. Cryptocurrencies such as Bitcoin (BTC), Litecoin (LTC), and Ethereum (ETH) are currently a thriving open-source community and payment network used by millions of people. As the value of these cryptocurrency prices varies every day, technically it would be difficult to predict the buying and selling prices, at the same time investors must forecast the cryptocurrency pricing on a daily basis. Existing techniques for predicting cryptocurrency values use Convolution neural networks (CNN) which are suitable for classification, and might produce suboptimal accuracies in prediction when working with sequential data. Recurrent neural network (RNN) and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) are used in this work to obtain more accurate and efficient price prediction. This work considers Mean Squared Error (MSE) matrix as the metric to evaluate the quality of predictions. The RNN algorithm is implemented in the first layer of LSTM. The algorithm is implemented using streamlit library in Python fetching live data from yahoo finance cryptocurrency data. The algorithm produces better accuracy when compared with the existing models.

Keywords: Bitcoin (BTC), Ethereum(ETH), Long Term Short Memory (LSTM), Mean Squared Error (MSE), Recurrent neural network (RNN).

Introduction

Many uncertainties influence cryptocurrency coin prices, including political issues, economic issues, and natural disasters (Ibrahim, 2020). These are the primary causes of the high volatility in the day-to-day price. To solve this problem regarding the fluctuations in the prices there is a need of a model to make accurate and efficient predictions that help the investors to gain certain knowledge over the drastic changes in the prices so that they can move their investments towards profits. In the cryptocurrency financial services sector, blockchain technology is frequently referred to as distributed ledger technology (Chinnasamy et al., 2021).

Cryptocurrency price data is a time series that changes over time. As a result, predicting the price of cryptocurrency is difficult. The model is implemented with LSTM and RNN. The RNN algorithm has the capability to store the previous data and it uses that data to predict present prices. The LSTM model provides more memory support to the RNN.

Existing model has less accuracy because of using CNNs ( Pokhrel et al., 2022; Kang et al., 2022; Cavalli and Amoretti, 2021). Sequential data, on the other hand, such as time series, audio, or text, are one-dimensional and lack the same spatial structure. Due to this applying CNN directly to the sequential data may not always give results in optimal performance.

RNN is a feed-forward neural network that was created to predict sequence problems by analyzing continuous changes in patterns. RNN has a feature that if it produces an output, this result is fed back into the memory of RNN’s hidden layer to make the next prediction, This makes RNN more accurate in the sequence prediction (Pant et al., 2018; Chinnasamy et al., 2023). LSTM is a popular deep-learning technique in RNN for time series prediction. It has four layers: an input layer, a hidden layer, a cell state layer, and an output layer.

Abstract

In recent years, digital watermarking of interactive media content has become an active experimentation area. In addition to reviewing some of the techniques for multiple media types that have been developed, a general framework for watermark engrafting and identification is described. We emphasize few of these application-oriented distinctions, some of them are copyright protection, substantiation, tamper detection, and data hiding, as well the technological and system prerequisite for various media kinds, such as digital photos, digital files, digital audio, and text. In this approach, we outline a general structure for digital watermarking-based image copyright protection. In this paper, we specifically outline the key components of an effective watermarking scheme, talk about concerns with robustness, and outline the key phases of tide marking mechanism.

Keywords: Robustness, Copyrights, Data Hiding, Confidentiality, Embed, Encryption, Recovery

Introduction

In this paper, we have discussed that digitalized watermarking is an enclosing procedure of a unique imperceptible identifier into digital media such as images, videos, audio, or documents. The objective of a digital tidemark is to recognize and protect the ownership and integrity of the digital content. A digital watermark can take various forms, including visible or invisible text, images, logos, or a combination of these elements. The watermark is added to the digital media during the creation process or after it has been created using specialized software (Sisaudia and Vishwakarma, 2021). Digital watermarking is commonly used to prevent copyright infringement, piracy, and unauthorized use of digital media. It can also be used for tracking and monitoring the distribution and usage of digital content. Watermarks can be designed to survive various forms of manipulation or transformation, such as compression, cropping, or resizing, and can be used to identify the original source of the content. Overall, digital watermarking provides a way to protect the rights of creators and owners of digital content and to make sure the reliability and integrity of the content (Wang et al., 2022). However, for the protection of copyright, traceability for anti-counterfeiting purposes, and information integrity, digital watermarking is widely used. Traditional watermarking methods could alter the originality of the image permanently. Reversible Watermarking (RW) is suggested as a way to recover the refuge image and extract the hidden communication (Dong et al., 2022), and it is receiving more and more attention. A digital watermark can contain information about the owner of the digital content, such as their name or copyright information. This can help identify the owner of the content and prove ownership in case of copyright infringement. In case of copyright infringement, digital watermarks can be used as evidence in court. By proving ownership and the presence of a watermark, the owner can prove that the content was taken or utilized without permission. Overall, digital watermarking is an important tool in copyright infringement and can help deter unauthorized use and distribution of digital content. It can also help protect the rights of content creators and owners and ensure that they receive proper compensation for their work. The reversibility of the cover canvas in the watermarking strategy can be achieved using a variety of techniques, such as lossless compression (Dong et al., 2022), histogram shifting (Hespanhol et al., 2021), robust reversible watermarking (Xing et al., 2022), compression strategy [13], and event-triggered dynamic watermarking approach (Xiao et al., 2022). Transparency

Transparency or constancy is the permanent comparability amidst the initial and the tide-marked form of the cover action (Xiao et al., 2022). The cybernetic watermark should not impact the classification and standard of the originality of the image and cover depiction after it is watermarked.

Robustness

Robustness has the capability of detecting the tidemark later than ordinary signal processing operations. Tidemark should be strong and vigorous in opposition to the viciousness of geometrical and non-geometrical attacks (Dong et al., 2022).

Capacity

Capacity or information payload that describes the total amount of bits a tidemark encrypted in a unit of time or work (Xiao et al., 2022). This category explains how much data should be engrafted as a tidemark to efficiently discover at the time of extraction.

Tamper Resistance

Tamper-detection in the watermarking methodology can be utilized to inspect authenticity or legitimacy. Any alteration to the watermark information impacts infringing of the image (Wang et al., 2022). Therefore, by evaluating integrity, the system decides in case the watermark data has been infringed or not.

Reversibility

The reversibility feature verifies the retrieval of the tidemark and clear-cut reformation of the host picture. Characteristics of Digital Watermarking

Security

Existing insecure watermarking techniques cannot be used to protect intellectual property, authenticate data, or track illegal digital content availability. As a result, if the attacker lacks knowledge of the key used to watermark digital assets using watermarking techniques and knowledge, the watermarking algorithm is secure and reliable. The information contained in the hidden watermark is therefore unbreakable. The privacy of the cover canvas can be protected using lighter-weight image encryption (Xing et al., 2022). Furthermore, the difficulty of the watermarking method may be referred to as security, as the attacker will be prevented from searching for the embedding space and protracted key position. To improve the algorithm’s protection, the embedded space and the scale of the keys which are segmented into small bits for the cover canvas can be increased (Wang et al., 2022).

Robustness

The robustness of the watermarking algorithms is an important consideration when examining and investigating the security of digitalized multimedia. The growing use of digitalized multimedia in all areas of business necessitated the need for copyright protection. Copyright protection is an essential feature of digital assets. In recent research trends of digital data security, the robustness of different algorithms and methods was used. The ability of watermarking to sustain non-malicious image analysis operations such as compression, filtration, etc., is termed as robustness (Xiao et al., 2022). That is, even in the presence of various attacks, the watermark extraction algorithm can obtain proper watermark extraction from watermarked images. The level of robustness varies by implementation, and not all implementations demand reliability against all processes. However, having an extraction technique that is resistant to any distortions that may occur would be ideal. Robustness may be completely irrelevant or even undesirable in some cases, such as fragile watermarking (Xing et al., 2022). However, semi-fragile watermarks share some traits with both robust and fragile watermarks.

Embedding Capacity

The amount of data that inserted watermarks can conceal up to the point at which they can be credibly extracted for authentication and copyright protections is the definition of capacity. The capacity is determined by the proportion of the original data under the conditions of imperceptibility and robustness (Xiao et al., 2022). The more unique patterns that can be created, the more bits that can be engrafted. Digital watermarking presents a more challenging task when it comes to incorporating as much watermark data as possible. A requirement for capacity is frequently dependent on the practical correlation used for watermarking. The capacity of clipping audio would be the implemented bits per second that are established. In other words, less capacity bits a watermark contains, the greater the likelihood that it will be computationally complex; larger capacity, lesser false positives, or fewer granularities will expand the potential operations of the data-inculcating method and build the authentication judgment more reliable (Ding et al., 2022).

Extraction

Several improvements of offensive intrusion are applied to the tidemark images to analyze the distillate tidemark in order to determine the strength of the postulated watermarking mechanism. The evaluation of the extracted watermark is classified as intrusive and non-intrusive (Ding et al., 2022). Here, attacks like clipping audio, circulatory, low-pass, high-pass, median filtering, volume deduction, and JPEG reduction are taken into account (Ding et al., 2022). Clipping involves removing half of the trademarked image and replacing it with false values to preserve its real size. It is to meet the input size requisite of the neural network. We store the primitive RGB values into a JPEG pictorial image with a quality of 95 percent for JPEG compression and as well as recuperate it for tidemark divergence (Ding et al., 2022). For the non-intrusive, we discover that clipping, and sound degrading can maintain the tidemark with adequate strength, whereas other attacks result in obvious perceptual distinction (Ding et al., 2022).

Tamper Resistance

The watermarking system’s tamper detection can verify the authenticity (Gong et al., 2021). The image is tampered with whenever the tidemark data is altered. Therefore, the method detects whether the tidemark data has been altered or not by testing integrity.

Copyright Protection

The very first applications for digital watermarking appeal to have copyright protection. In this instance, the metadata includes details about the copyright holder. The initial work that needs to be secured has it subtly incorporated as a watermark. Users of online content (music, images, and video) must be able to recognise and analyze the engrafted watermark and recognize the copyright holder of the marked information if they have better access to watermark detectors. Let’s see an example, the Digi Marc watermark detector will detect a watermark when a sender unlocks an image in a Digital mark-enabled application. It will then use the watermark as a key to search a remote database for a copyright holder and his credential details. A genuine sender can use that data to reach the image’s copyright holder and request authorization to make use of the canvas. Watermarking-Based Secure Plaintext Image Protocols promote cloud-based plaintext image storage with image copyrighted works, transparent display, lossless compression, and managed changes via homomorphic encryption and tide marking techniques (Dong et al., 2022).

Advantages of Digital Watermarking

Digitalise watermarking is the process of encapsulating a unique identifier, such as a code or image, into digital content to protect it from unauthorized use or distribution. Some of the advantages of digital watermarking include:

Copyright Protection: Digital watermarking can help protect the copyright of digital content such as images, music, and videos, by making it more difficult for others to use or distribute it without permission (Wang et al., 2022).

Branding: Digital watermarking can be used as a branding tool to promote a company’s products or services (Dong et al., 2022). For example, a company logo can be embedded into digital content, such as a video or image, to help promote the brand.

Tracking and Identification: Digital watermarking can be used to track and identify the origin of digital content (Xiao et al.., 2022). This can be useful for tracking the distribution of copyrighted material or for tracking the use of a company’s digital assets.

Authentication: Digital watermarking can be used to authenticate the source and integrity of digital content (Ding et al., 2022). This can be useful for ensuring that digital content has not been tampered with or altered in any way.

Evidence in Legal Proceedings: Digital watermarking can provide evidence in legal proceedings, such as copyright infringement cases, by proving the ownership of digital content and its unauthorized use (Gong et al., (2021)].

Overall, digital watermarking provides a powerful tool for protecting digital content and can be used to provide a range of benefits to individuals and businesses.

Disadvantages of Digital Watermarking

While digital watermarking has many advantages, it also has some disadvantages. Some of the potential drawbacks of digital watermarking include:

Reduction in Quality: Embedding a digital watermark into an image or video can sometimes reduce the quality of the content, depending on the type and intensity of the watermark [3]. This can result in a degradation of the user experience, which can negatively impact the perception of the content.

Vulnerability to Removal: Digital watermarks can be removed by individuals with sufficient knowledge and tools [7], which can render them ineffective as a means of copyright protection or tracking.

Complexity: Embedding digital watermarks can be a complex process, requiring specialized software and expertise (Hosny et al., 2021). This can make it difficult for individuals or organizations to implement, especially if they lack the necessary resources.

False Positives: Digital watermarking algorithms may occasionally produce false positives, identifying content as infringing when it is not (Ding et al., 2022). This can result in legitimate use of content being incorrectly flagged as unauthorized, which can negatively impact users and businesses.

Cost: Implementing digital watermarking can involve costs, including the purchase of software or services and the training of personnel. This can be a significant barrier for smaller businesses or individuals (Du et al., 2023).

Overall, digital watermarking can be a useful tool for protecting digital content, but it is not without its limitations and potential drawbacks.
