A Survey on Implementation and Development of AES Cryptography Algorithm In Various Fields

S. Giridharan,45

E-mail: mailtoogiri@gmail.com, dhiviyaaj@gmail.com, mehdirmuhammed2002@gmail.com, hajitha098@gmail.com

DOI: 10.1201/9781003430452-58

Abstract

Cryptography is a way of using secure communications techniques that provide confidentiality and allow only the sender and intended recipient of a message to view its content. Given the prevalence of the internet, regular internet users must remain aware of cyber security issues. Nevertheless, most individuals lack the essential knowledge of how cryptography is used in passwords and other online contexts. AES, DES, and Triple-DES are only a few of the many algorithms that are presently available for encrypting data, but it is still necessary to enhance the current algorithms to guard against potential attacks on encrypted data. The current Advanced Encryption Standard algorithm’s benefits and drawbacks are discussed in detail, as well as how it affects data security in numerous industries.

Keyword: Encryption, Decryption, Cryptography, AES, Cipher

Introduction

Security is the current top priority. Cryptography is crucial in the field of security. While the development and implementation of Advanced Encryption Standard algorithms in major domains are numerous, AES is implemented in both hardware and software fields to encrypt and secure various data. Every algorithm in cryptography has two sections. Encryption and Decryption. The act of converting plaintext to cipher text is termed encryption, while the process of converting cipher text back to plain text is termed decryption. The reason behind choosing cryptography in our survey is to create awareness among the general audience, who are unaware of the cyber attacks happening around them. The attackers steal the information without the authorized user’s knowledge, and the information is transferred without any kind of protection. On the other hand, the reason for choosing the AES cryptography algorithm is that it is more secure when compared to the DES (Data Encryption Standard), Triple-DES, etc., cryptography algorithms. The AES algorithm can never be cracked by a brute force attack (Brute force resistance). The number of transformation rounds required to convert plaintext into cipher text in AES encryption depends on the key size used. For a 128-bit key size, 10 rounds are needed; for a 192-bit key size, 12 rounds are required, and for a 256-bit key size, 14 rounds are necessary.

The AES includes:

  1. Key Expansion

  2. First-round key addition:

    • Add Round Key
    • 9, 11, or 13 Rounds: Depending on the key size, the data is processed via a specific number of rounds. The following four stages are included in each round:
    • Sub Bytes: A corresponding byte from a substitution table is used to replace each byte of the data.
    • Shift Rows: The data’s rows have various levels of translation.
    • Mix Columns: A matrix multiplication is used to change each data column.
    • Add Round Key: The data is updated with the round key for the current round.
    • Last Round: The Mix Columns step is not present in the final round, although it is comparable to the earlier rounds.
    • The encrypted data is the outcome of the last round. The same procedure is used in reverse order to decrypt the data using the same key.

These different rounds, key sizes, and methods produce distinct and complex keys that are strong enough to secure resources. AES is also flexible for development and produces or enhances different varieties in its algorithm, which makes AES dynamic.

Literature Survey

Altigani et al., (2021) proposed an effective, score-based, key-dependent P-AES algorithm of key avalanche as 0.496 and plaintext avalanche as 0.504. This methodology satisfied all NIST-recommended Statistical Test Suite (STS) criteria. The purpose of this proposal was to replace AES’ static properties and replace them with dynamic encryption. By manipulating the sub-bytes, shifting rows, mixing columns, and making it key-dependent, an Advanced Encryption Standard polymorphic variation was created. After implementing this algorithm, polymorphism was achieved and will not affect interoperability. As a result, cipher text can function in 128 distinct keys. There is a negligible difference in performance between the proposed P-AES and the standard AES.

Yendamury & Mohankumar (2021)proposed a Defense in Depth strategy on AES employing logic locking at the system level techniques. The lock blocks on AES are inserted in a subprocess of the AES decryption algorithm. The achieved output was 70% when an incorrect password was provided at the input. Three types of decryption algorithms are used depending on key size, and Key sizes of 128, 192, and 256 bits are supported by AES. The input text data size always remains at 128 bits. Insert logic lock blocks into corresponding sub-processes such as (1) inverse shift row, (2) reverse substitution byte, (3) add round key, and (4) reverse mix column. The analysis of Hamming distance, Levenshtein distance, and Jaro distance inferred that the output text is entirely corrupted with distances greater than 80%, 80%, and 50%, respectively. This technique provides flexibility to brute force, reverse engineering, and key sensitization assaults.

Kumar et al., (2022) proposed better protection of media transfers over social media and other modes of transfer. The implementation of this proposed work is a combination of steganography and cryptography to secure the information from unapproved access. To protect the information, the output obtained must have low Mean Square Error (MSE) and high Point Signal To Noise Ratio (PSNR) values. These values help in the better hiding of data in a media file, irrespective of its file format. In the suggested work, the MSE and PSNR values are improved when compared to the previous proposals. The PSNR value is 75.1375, while the MSE value is 0.0019922. from the proposed work. whereas the MSE and PSNR values from the previous proposed works are not even close to the work proposed here.

Mohammad & Abdullah, (2022) improved, developed, and proposed a Lightweight Cryptography algorithm (LWC) to increase the embedded systems’ and limited devices’ security. The enhancement of the AES algorithm was done by reducing the computation power of the algorithm and improving the cryptographic performance of constraint devices. In this procedure, which protects all types of data, the suggested technique was quick and lightweight. The mathematical fraction, or continuous fraction to compress, was used to process the ciphertext, making it more difficult and speeding up data transfer in the process. As compared to AES, the LWC-AES proved far more appropriate for speedy encryption and decryption. The computational power of the proposed algorithm was also less than the memory capacity of the Central Processing Unit (CPU). Together, the proposed algorithm is directly proportional to high security. On various platforms, the code for the LWC-AES text data type is fast and compact, with the programming result of the proposed algorithm being: idle CPU usage of 348.7 ms, memory size of 24 bytes, RAM size of 326 bytes, code size of 587 bytes, and bandwidth of 2.665 Mbps.

In this paper, Reis et al., (2022)propose IMCRYPTO, an in-memory computing (IMC) fabric for accelerating AES. In order to perform encryption and decryption in a single-hardware architecture with merged sub-bytes and mix-column processes, this article uses a unique technique with a unified structure. A modular Look-Up Table (LUT) fabric is designed by utilizing consecutive arrangement and high parallelism provided by several Random Access Memory (RAM) and Random Access/Content Addressable Memory (RA/CAM) arrays, along with specialized encoders. Without compromising space or power use, the suggested LUT fabric offers high throughput encryption and decoding. Integration with RISC-V enabled the flexibility of performing different modes of operation.

Chung et al., (2022) proposed Grover’s algorithm here for implementation of AES with the help of S-box (Substitution box). By using the substitution approach, the S-box substitution procedure converts the 48-bit input from the XOR operation, which contains the compressed key and extended RPT, into a 32-bit output. As compared to other ways, the group’s solution in this proposal makes use of the fewest qubits, greatly lowering its T-depth. A total of 8 S-boxes are used in order to get the output where the values of the S-box are calculated using the formula GF(28)=GF(2)[x]/(x8+x4+x3+x+1). When an oracle adds a negative phase to the solution states, Grover’s procedure resolves it. To be more precise, given every state in the computational foundation. The entry that corresponds to the indicated item in this oracle will have a negative phase. It will be a diagonal matrix.

Bedoui et al., (2022) proposed an efficient fault detection method for the AES algorithm. This approach was suggested regardless of how the S-Box and inverse S-box were constructed. The AES round design consisted of three pieces with two pipeline registers inserted in between to increase fault coverage. The proposed approach is designed to be compatible with different AES sizes, including AES-128, AES-192, and AES-256. The effectiveness of this approach was tested through fault injection simulations in VHDL to validate its ability to detect issues. The developed method can find 99.339 percent of randomly introduced mistakes. This paper’s main objective is to provide an AES implementation that is trustworthy, strong, and resistant to fault injection threats.

Kolate & Joshi (2021)proposed DNA-based security techniques as an information carrier. By integrating the advantages of both DNA-based and cryptographic AES, the new data-security approach may be put into practice. This offers many layers of protection. DNA cryptography is presented as an efficient encryption technique, which confirms non-vulnerable communication. Compression methods can be used with DNA cryptography and AES to secure sensitive data, such as military data. DNA cryptography is advantageous and advancing quickly, as evidenced by the employment of the four DNA bases (A, T, G, and C) to encrypt communications and boost performance in terms of parallelism and storage capacity.

Jang et al., (2022) proposed a Quantum computing analysis that enhances the resistance of secret key ciphers against a strong quantum opponent. This key recovery attack applies the Grovers algorithm’s quantum key search on three different AES variants (128, 192, and 256) in order to retrieve the key. As a consequence, it demonstrates improvement in the implementation pool and a decrease in the quantum costs for the AES variants across a variety of metrics.

Mane & Mulani (2018)proposed The AES algorithm is implemented quickly and securely on an FPGA (fast programmable gate array).

Advanced encryption algorithms are one type of cryptographic algorithm that is used to improve the security of system data and protect it from unauthorized access. This study presents an algorithm that aims to combine fast throughput with minimal power usage. Keys are produced by MATLAB. (a matrix-based programming language used to analyze and design the system), and the balance algorithm is designed using Xilinx SysGen, a Simulink add-on that enables the architecture level of FPGA designs using graphical block programming. Hence, at a maximum working frequency of 1102.536 MHz, the system only makes use of 121 slice registers. Moreover, the suggested system has a throughput of 14.1125 GB/s.

Discussion

Altigani et al., (2021),reveal details on the P-AES algorithm. By rearranging the rows and columns and creating as many different combinations as possible, we learned how algorithms function. There are 128 different ways that encrypted text can be used.

Yendamury & Mohankumar (2021 ),sheds information on the Defense in Depth approach for AES using techniques for logic locking at the system level. When a wrong password was entered, a 70% output was attained. AES is a popular encryption standard that allows for the use of key sizes of 128, 192, and 256 bits. To decrypt data encrypted with AES, different techniques are used depending on the key size. Specifically, three different decryption methods are employed, each tailored to handle a specific key size.

Kumar et al., (2022),provides an example of how steganography and cryptography aid in protecting media files from being intercepted when they are sent from one end to the other. Also, the results were better than in the earlier research.

To improve the security of embedded systems and restricted devices, Mohammad & Abdullah (2022) made an attempt and were successful in creating the Lightweight Cryptography algorithm (LWC). By reducing the method’s computational complexity and enhancing the cryptographic functionality of tested devices, the AES algorithm was improved.

IMCRYPTO was proposed (Reis et al., 2022) as a means of speeding up AES. IMCRYPTO technology is employed with a unified structure to carry out encryption and decryption in a mono-hardware architecture with merged sub-bytes and mix-column operations.

To implement AES using an S-box, (Chung et al., 2022 )this paper devised Grover’s method (Substitution box). The compressed key and extended RPT are contained in the 48-bit input from the XOR operation, which is converted into a 32-bit output using the S-box substitution technique.

For the AES algorithm, (Bedoui et al., 2022) they developed a flaw detection technique. The suggested method might be modified for other AES sizes (AES-128,192 and 256). To validate the suggested methodology for issue identification, fault injection simulations in the VHDL language were produced.

DNA-based security methods as a data carrier: The benefits of DNA-based and cryptographic AES may be used to create a new data-security strategy (Kolate & Joshi, 2021).

Jang et al., (2022), AES set in motion a Quantum computing analysis that enhances the resistance of secret key ciphers against a strong quantum opponent. This key recovery attack solicits the Grovers algorithm’s quantum key search on three different AES variants (128, 192, and 256) in order to retrieve the key.

Mane & Mulani (2018)proposed that the AES-algorithm is implemented quickly and securely on an FPGA (fast programmable gate array). Advanced encryption algorithms are one type of cryptographic algorithm that is used to improve the security of system data and protect it from unauthorized access.

Conclusion

Data breaches and data theft are the major and most important security threats emerging in every organization, which pave the way for cryptography’s implementation and development for securing various resources. Because of its flexibility and exponentially stronger key than DES and Triple-DES, one of the cryptography algorithms called AES is the one that is most commonly employed in a variety of areas. AES can be modified and transformed into a newly proposed algorithm, such as Defense in Depth, a system-level approach, and its polymorphic property transforms AES into a dynamic structure that can be combined as a hybrid structure in the field of AI. AES has also been used in many fields, such as telecommunications, data transactions, quantum analysis, memory computing, information security (DNA-based AES), and so on. This ensures that the AES can be one of the best algorithms for securing data and resources in every field.

A Survey on Alerting Using Honeyword System

Mr. E. Rajkumar,46

E-mail: raju.becs39@gmail.com, alluaravind87@gmail.com, muthaiah55555@gmail.com, pranavawm@gmail.com, pk2851764@gmail.com

DOI: 10.1201/9781003430452-59

Abstract

A security method called Honeywords is used to identify and stop website password assaults. This method involves including honeywords, or fictitious passwords, along with genuine passwords in a website. A warning is sent to the website administrator about a possible security breach if a hacker accesses the database and tries to utilize a honeyword. This technique is helpful because it makes it harder for hackers to distinguish between legitimate passwords and false ones, decreasing the occurrence of an attack. In order to construct multi-layered protection against password attacks, honeywords can be used in conjunction with other security measures. Overall, honeywords offer a practical solution to strengthen the backend security of a website and safeguard critical user information. Due to the rise in cyber attacks, honey words have become more common as a security solution. Internet security is still seriously threatened by password attacks, but Honeywords can help by strengthening the defenses already in place.

Keywords: Passwords, Honeywords, Legacy UI, Honey encryption, Honey-checker, Salting, Sweetword

Introduction

For years, passwords have been the standard practice for protecting internet accounts, but they have their own set of issues. Password theft is a significant problem that can occur through phishing or hacking. Once a password has been compromised, it can be used to steal identities or obtain illegal access to confidential data. A promising strategy being investigated by researchers in recent years for safeguarding internet accounts is the use of “honeywords.” Honeywords are fictitious passwords that are made to feel and look authentic but are actually fraudulent. The purpose of this technique is to make it so that a hacker who obtains a password will be unable to determine which one is the actual password and will therefore be I was unable to access the account. The idea of honeywords, how they function, and why they could be an effective tool in the battle against cybercrime are all covered in this article.

Although the usage of honeywords is a relatively new idea, the cybersecurity world has already expressed a lot of interest in it. The fact that honeywords give an extra layer of security without forcing users to remember complicated passwords or go through additional authentication stages is one explanation for this. Moreover, honeywords are a quick and affordable way to increase account security because they can be simply implemented into current authentication systems. The fundamental idea behind Honeywords is straightforward: if a hacker acquires a password database, they won’t be able to distinguish between actual and bogus passwords. They will have to try several passwords before they find the right one, which makes it much more difficult for them to log in to an account. This not only gives the account an additional degree of security but also serves as an early warning system for attacks. Also, users may not be able to tell the difference between genuine and fraudulent passwords, which raises questions about how they may respond to the use of honeywords. In conclusion, honeywords are a cutting-edge method of protecting online accounts that may add an extra layer of protection against hackers. The advantages of honeywords make them a viable instrument in the battle against cybercrime, notwithstanding the difficulties still associated with their application. We’re likely to see further advancements in this area as technology advances because the cybersecurity community is constantly looking for fresh and inventive solutions to protect our online accounts.

This method has drawn interest as a potentially effective means of safeguarding user data and preventing illegal access to backend systems. We will delve more into the idea of honeywords in this post, covering their operation, advantages, and any potential implementation difficulties. We will also look at some actual implementations of Honeywords and provide some helpful advice for website owners who want to use this method to increase security.

Literature Review

[1] This architecture connects the honeyword system to the Internet of Things framework. The security requirements may jeopardize one of the most crucial usability criteria, typo safety. This is because regular typing errors made by a legitimate user can be mistaken for malicious activity 38.09%–69.67% of the time. This method uses super words that may not always operate in the same way as the legacy UI. The strategy most likely belongs in the modified-user interface group as well and shows that the aforementioned approach may not sufficiently safeguard view of the enormous amount of associated username-password combinations that can be found when using this threat model, we present a simple technique that ignores any personally identifiable information (PII), such as a person’s name or birthday. Using data sets, the suggested method can find username-password pairs that are at least 5 to 22 times more related than expected. Finally, this approach gives honeyword-based authentication protocol for IoT devices with limited resources based on binary.

[2] For external attackers, HPAKE provides honeyword strategies for password leaks. If the server is breached, the hacker will gain access to a list of passwords that includes commonly used words, obtained through offline guessing methods. The attacker most likely utilizes HPAKE and a honeyword to get access to the account because they are unable to tell them apart. The process of authentication is specifically managed through the exchange of keys. Only the instruction that has been encrypted using the valid session key will be allowed with the right password, resulting in the creation of the actual key. Although the idea of HPAKE seems sensible, putting it into practice presents considerable difficulties. This claim highlights aPAKE and honeyword as two unique password management techniques. It continues by stating that the password must stay in plaintext on the client side and cannot be shared with the server when using the aPAKE method. The server then receives this password for verification. Each aPAKE instance that the authentication server runs has its own distinct password. For an aPAKE with explicit authentication, a session key will only be created when the client’s password and the server’s password are same.

[3] A fresh attack strategy called a “Multiple System Intersection assault considering Input” is what we suggest. Insufficient security exists for the “Paired Distance Protocol” against this attack scenario. This methodology produces honeywords that are interchangeable with genuine passwords and is effective and useful. In order to avoid false positives when a legitimate user accidentally types a honeyword, the Levenshtein distance is used to maintain a secure distance between the password and honeywords. It takes advantage of password databases that hackers disclosed to the public. We demonstrate the exact flatness of our suggested honeyword generating strategies through trials. We contrast our suggested methods with the current honeyword creation methods on a number of metrics to support the claim.

[4] In order to safeguard and manage the user’s password, one solution is a password manager. The data is encrypted by the password manager to preserve its security, but they are still susceptible to cyberattacks like brute-force attacks. All user passwords would be available to the attacker if they were to successfully guess the master password. As a way to enhance security methods and give password managers protection, honey encryption was one solution that was used. By identifying, stopping, and deceiving data breaches committed by brute-force attackers, the honey encryption method helps password managers solve various security challenges. In order to do detection, the suggested system generates and saves a number of automatically created honey words that are similar to the actual user passwords and which will be contrasted with the entered password. The system will recognize the intruder and bar them from accessing the account if the password matches any of the honey words. As a security measure, they are instead forwarded to a false account with fake information.

[5] This study looks at how commonly alphanumeric usernames and passwords are used in computer systems as a standard for authentication and intrusion protection. Yet, security threats have increased along with the growth of data sharing, internet use, data transport, and validation. Several salting and hashing techniques are used to store password files in databases to overcome these issues. Nonetheless, attackers continue to use brute force attacks, password guessing, and other methods to obtain user credentials. Others claim that password hashing is insufficient to withstand such attacks. While using password based authentication, the first encryption layer frequently requires that attackers successfully guess the password in as few attempts as feasible. Security experts are constantly creating password authorization techniques to stop hackers from cracking the password. Hackers use cuttingedge technologies in specific iterations to break passwords. This study uses distinct hashing algorithm with less complexity of the time with basic operations carried out using binaries.

[6] A hash function should be used to store the website password using one-way encryption in accordance with the privacy policy to prevent decryption. The collision of the MD5 and SHA-1 hash algorithms, however, occurred as the computer’s performance increased, signaling that a hash function like SHA-256, which was considered to be a secure one, would be used to decode data. Salting is the process of adding the hash function to the password at either the start or end. With the previous salt usage method, the salt is randomly assigned to each user, but generated only once and then stored as a constant value in the database. This creates a vulnerability as the password can easily be decrypted with the salt if the database is compromised. Access-based salts are constantly evolving to increase password security and hide the salting process.

Methods & Techniques

[1] This paper intends to provide accurate cryptanalysis of an IoT framework’s keyword system. Although integrating a password as an authentication element in an IoT framework has many benefits, it frequently inherits the security flaws of password-based authentication. Several of these flaws might be fixed by using honeyword-based authentication. While combining the honeyword protocol with the IoT infrastructure, careful design approach is required. This study contributes reference to the next two main goals in this way. This study shows that the researchers are continuously working to create a honeyword-based strategy that satisfies the requirements from both the security and usability viewpoints. Before anyone chooses the way to safeguard an organization’s password file, they must have a greater understanding of its security (and usability) standard.

[2] Security analysis: The suggested model offers defense against insider attacks in addition to password guessing assaults, which are both taken into account in the conventional aPAKE security model. By recognizing the similarity between the genuine and honey session keys, it can also identify password leaks. Compared to both Honeyword mechanism and aPAKE, this solution can provide more security. In the event of an authentication server compromise, HPAKE’s security is greater than Password-over-TLS utilizing OPAQUE because it can identify password leaks. In terms of defense against insider threats and password-guessing attacks, HPAKE is equal to OPAQUE. Our HPAKE technique uses honey words generated during the registration process to produce the user’s private and public keys. The server then stores both the honey public key and the genuine public key. The key exchange technique is used by the server to generate numerous session keys using the users’ different public keys during authentication. To find password violations, the server then determines whether the client is using the real session key or a honey session key. By decrypting the cipher text of the user’s initial Honeyword private key, our concept uses Honey encryption to produce user-specific Honeyword private keys. Our HPAKE system’s fundamental advantage is its ability to generate multiple session keys on the server while using the same ciphertext for both the real password and the honeywords, obviating the need for numerous OPAQUE output instances.

[3] Legacy-LH password changes: A important term used by the system is “Token,” which describes a group of letters that can be regarded as a single logical unit. A password’s “pattern” is made up of the different token combinations that it contains. The frequency of a token or password pattern in the password database is measured by the number of times it appears there. The system doesn’t keep track of the length of the alphabets and numbers, but it does keep track of the length of special characters in order to produce honeywords that are identical to a user’s actual password. As a result, the pattern representation adds “S” as a subscript to the special character’s length. By integrating specific information from the user’s profile and ensuring that it meets the minimal separation requirement from the actual password, honeywords are produced. The creation of various sets of tokens based on input from the user, such as: B. Strings of letters, Strings of digits, and Special Characters, is one way to generate honeywords. The components of each token set are then merged to create potential honeyword combinations. If a user profile-related substring appears in the password, this strategy is especially helpful. As a result, this method generates honeywords that are challenging to identify from the majority of user passwords.

[4] The password manager hashes the user’s entered password and generates a collection of honeywords that closely resemble the original password when a user registers and creates a username and master password. These honey words act as a signal to identify and stop intrusion by outsiders. OTP encryption, which encrypts all user app credentials, adds an additional layer of protection because the password manager holds the passwords for other programs and websites. When logging in, the password manager provides a login screen for the user to enter their details and allows three login attempts. The password manager uses OTP to decrypt the app passwords and grants access if the hashed master password given by the user matches the hashed master password that is already stored. After that, the user is sent to their account page, which contains all of their passwords. The password manager will recognize unauthorized access if a hacker tries to input one of the honeywords and route them to a phone lock password page. This keeps the app passwords OTP protected and secure while deceiving the hacker into thinking they have access to a legitimate account. The user’s account will be disabled and the program will end if they attempt more than three times without entering a valid honeyword. In order to defend against brute force attacks, the encryption technique known as Honey Encryption (HE) creates a fake message that looks real to outsiders who enter the wrong key. The true meaning is carefully hidden. A password manager (PM) is a piece of software that uses a single master password to lock all of the user’s passwords and store them securely. Besides protecting passwords, PM also helps minimize instances where users mistype their password, promoting better password quality

[5] User Registration: In order to initiate the registration process, you must create a new user account that will serve as a database record describing the means by which you can verify your identity. You must demonstrate that your identity matches your user account in order to be verified. Users must enter specific details while enrolling in addition to their desired username and password.

Encryption/decryption Passwords are encrypted into unintelligible text using techniques in order to identify hackers. Afterward, ciphertext creation is done to create ciphertext that will be used in the next step.

Adding salt ValuesA further layer of security protection is added by appending certain salt values, often known as irrelevant data. This increases the password’s length, adding another level of security.

Hash Function: Hashing of the password is done as the input string is initially used as the password. The password is then calculated for length, and the string is then turned around. The reversed text is then transformed into a binary string and, depending on the length of the password, is subsequently padded with extra bits. In order to create a safe and distinctive hash value, this method entails numerous steps of translating and altering the password in different ways.

[6] The benefit of the real-password unrelated design method is that it prevents the attacker from quickly determining the real password from a single sweet word. Also, it makes it possible for honeywords to be generated with an equal frequency, making it harder for an attacker to figure out the genuine password. Nevertheless, this approach makes it difficult to use probabilistic password models, and major adjustments must be made during the design and evaluation phases. When the attacker is aware of the user registration sequence, these alterations are considerably more difficult because it complicates the honeyword generating process. We have created four distinct honeyword generation techniques, each with its own special set of protection mechanisms, to solve these difficulties. To determine the most reliable honeyword technique, we extensively analyzed these strategies and compared their efficacy in various attack scenarios. Overall, our method of honeyword production has a lot of advantages over conventional ones. We have made it harder for attackers to guess real passwords even when they have in-depth knowledge of the user registration process by using real-password-unrelated design and creating various honeyword techniques.

Conclusion

We conclude that the honeywords system has been demonstrated to be a beneficial and successful tool for increasing security measures across a variety of fields. Businesses and organizations frequently use it because of its capacity to recognize and stop cyberattacks like brute force, phishing, and password guessing. The capacity of the Honeywords system to generate dummy passwords and notify security staff instantly when an attempt is made to access them is a key benefit. In high-risk industries like finance, healthcare, and government where data breaches can have serious repercussions, this method is very helpful. Notwithstanding its advantages, the Honeywords system needs to be combined with additional security precautions to offer complete defense against cyberattacks. In general, the honeywords strategy is a hopeful remedy for the data breaches

A Study on IoT Based Road Safety and Traffic Management

N. Jagadeesh47

Email: kavithad.mca@spiher.ac.in

DOI: 10.1201/9781003430452-60

Abstract

The IoT has a bigger important in many fields in the current situation. In which road safety and traffic management is the most needed area for proper management of vehicles on road and also for the safety of the people. As there is less human power these IoT devices are incorporated for providing assistance for human beings with regard to usage. The more the usage, there arises a problem of reliability as these data helps to avoid accidents in road. In this paper, we discuss the various challenges and issues faced when IoT devices are used and also about the solutions to be considered when the issues occur in these devices when used for Road Safety and Traffic Management for providing the utmost safety for the drivers and pedestrians. Keywords: Io T, Road Safety, Pedestrians, Reliability

Introduction

IoT is a collection of various sensors and components which are incorporated together for the process of making an object or device to work with less human interaction. Many sensors are incorporated to the IoT device in order to perform various tasks. In the case of road safety and traffic management, various sensors like (IR, ultrasonic, and accelerometer) are used for assisting drivers to avoid accidents in the road and help to provide the utmost safety for the pedestrians on the roads.

IoT in Road Safety

The roads are the backbone for many countries as they connect with many other countries which helps in the development of the country. As there is a need for many there should be proper safety in roads. According to the WHO around 1.35 million people die every year due to road traffic accidents, and up to 50 million more suffer non-fatal injuries [1]. So there is a need for better vehicle management guiding the drivers for smooth operation of the vehicles.

Connected Vehicles

  1. Assists with the condition of the vehicle.
  2. Informs the drivers in case of overspeeding
  3. In case of medical emergency, details are sent to save lives.

These are being done by the sensors which are being incorporated into the vehicles.

IoT in Traffic Management

Traffic plays a major role in many cities where the people are halted for many hours and many miles mainly during the peak hours or during festival times. It takes more time for crossing a small area which is a major issue in case of emergencies where ambulances and fire engines are supposed to move on in that area.

Literature Survey

Fabio Arena and Giovanni Pau-An Overview of Vehicular Communications”, January 2019, Article in Future Internet “. This paper proposes ideas about how communication can be carried out between vehicle to vehicle, vehicle to infrastructure and vehicle to everything. It also gives a glimpse about the Intelligent Transport System how well it can work if the data is reliable.” (Arena and Pau, 2019)

R. Sushmitha et al-Smart Roads System”, Vol. 2, Issue 7, July 2021, International Journal of Recent Advances in Multidisciplinary Topics. “This paper gives idea how to use the roads for pedestrian safety.” (Sushmitha et al., 2021)

Ning Lu et al. “Connected Vehicles: Solutions and Challenges,” August 2014 IEEE Internet of Things Journal, This paper proposes an idea about wireless communication with vehicles, Infrastructure, etc. There is a need to check how efficient it is when compared to wired communication. In wireless, there arises a problem of too much information providing more workload for the users.” (Lu et al., 2014)

Juan Guerrero-Ibariez et al.” Sensor Technologies for Intelligent Transportation Systems,” 2018, Multidisciplinary Digital Publishing Institute, This paper provides an overview of various sensors which can be incorporated with vehicles for Intelligent Traffic System” (Guerrero-Ibanez et al., 2018).

Mubashir Murshed et al. An IoT Based Car Accident Prevention and Detection System with Smart Brake Control” International Conference on Applications and Techniques in Information Science (iCATIS2019), 19-23 Jan 2019, Dhaka, Bangladesh “This paper gives information to the users with the email provided as soon as abnormal behavior detected. Even if the driver does not respond the sensors will make the actions to be carried on to the vehicles for effective movement” (Murshed et al., 2019)

Naresh et al. (2020). Smart Traffic management system using IOT “International Journal of Engineering Trends and Technology (IJETT-Scopus Indexed) — Special Issues - ICT 2020” This paper proposes about smart traffic management and how to manage traffic in case of emergency vehicles passing through the traffic.

Existing Issues

The various challenges and Issues being faced by road safety management are

  1. Frequent access:

    When there is a frequent movement of vehicles in junctions’ without any proper intimation to other vehicles and persons on the road.

  2. Inadequate Footpath:

    There is no proper footpath for pedestrians, which makes them to go through on the main road which leads to accidents

  3. No proper bus stops:

    There are no proper bus stops which makes the people to stand on the roads causing fatalities that result in severe injuries and death.

  4. Line marking in roads:

    As many roads do not have proper line markings to indicate the separation between both side of roads which causes overtaking of vehicles leading to accidents.

  5. Uncontrolled parking:

    The drivers parking the vehicles on either side of the road without proper indication lead to the crashing of vehicles which is approaching.

  6. No proper sign boards:

    With minimum and unfamiliar signboard marking the vehicle drivers and pedestrians face the issue regarding the understanding of the sign boards which proves to be an issue for causing accidents.

  7. No proper speed control:

    The drivers lack speed control which makes them go through rash driving which leads to crashing with the vehicles and pedestrians.

  8. Usage of Alcoholic substances:

    The usage of various alcoholic substances during driving makes drivers drive in a rash manner causing accidents [8].

The various challenges and Issues being faced by traffic management are

  1. Usage of Old traffic signals:

    The outdated traffic signals are still being used in various places even if it is worn out causing malfunctioning of the traffic lights.

  2. No proper manpower

    There is a lack of traffic in charges that are to be available near traffic signals to assist the vehicle commuters for smooth crossing of vehicles in signals.

  3. Lack of traffic discipline

    Bus stops which are situated near intersections of traffic signals cause’ traffic which proves to be a major concern in traffic management.

  4. Less education by drivers

    Some drivers are less educated to understand the signs, and boards which are used which makes other drivers suffer in traffic.

  5. Traffic conflict between vehicles and pedestrians:

    The pedestrians cross the signals without noticing which leads to fatality. The pedestrians do this due to lack of knowledge, when other people cross the roads they also tend to cross without seeing to the signal.

  6. Traffic near signals in public places:

    As many people are supposed to be in a public place there requires high traffic management by using sensors, traffic personnel etc. Due to lack of all these, there arises traffic and causes lot of congestion

Proposed Solution

Some of the proposed solutions for overcoming road and traffic safety management is

  1. Smart Traffic Lights

    These lights will give a clear indication of the signals from a longer distance and indicate the changes that are supposed to happen (changing of lights).

  2. Telematics

    This is like a real time GPS which is used to know the actual speed, acceleration, parking and other operations on a vehicle.

  3. Autonomous vehicles

    Many sensors like GPS, Sonar are all installed in these vehicles to understand the surrounding environment and help to guide the driver about ongoing object and upcoming objects.

  4. Emergency services

    Certain vehicles are incorporated with fatigue sensors which detect abnormal and emergency behaviors among the drivers and inform the emergency centers and to the relation of the drivers regarding their status.

  5. Separate Lanes

    The usage of different lanes for different vehicles in road as in case of toll booth, where two-wheelers, four-wheelers, and emergency vehicles are given separate lanes. This method helps to reduce traffic.

  6. Street Lighting

    The usage of sensors for street lights to adjust with that of the normal lighting which is already available. The sensors must act accordingly with the natural light.

  7. Signals with audio

    The usage of audio in signals to indicate vehicular movement which helps the less educated driver [9].

Steps to be implemented for Road Safety and Traffic Management using IoT

  1. Providing individual path for the different types of vehicles
  2. Usage of proper signal facilities in intersection points and injunctions.
  3. Providing basic knowledge about the traffic system to the users.
  4. Improvement in Traffic control management system.
  5. Improvement of Traffic safety management system
  6. Strengthening traffic police and improving their operations.
  7. Providing proper parking facilities to the vehicle and avoiding roadside parking.
  8. Adjustment of roadside light with accordance with the natural lighting.

Discussion

The smart usage of sensors in Road Safety and Traffic Management provides improvement in these fields. As and when in the starting stages there are chances of many accidents happening due to poor facilities in road safety and traffic management.

As nowadays, all are updated and people are mostly dependent on sensors for their vehicles for parking, and vehicle tracking which proves to be an improvement in the technology. The vehicles at present can be combined with more and more sensors for providing safe vehicle movement on roads.

The vehicles which are connected ones, they communicate with themselves for avoiding a collision.

In the case of people proper educational knowledge to be given during their school days regarding how to move on in roads and also the importance of traffic signals and why it is to be followed.

Conclusion

The main challenges Issues in Road Safety and Traffic Management is being addressed and how these can be solved by using IoT and sensors has been discussed which provides a clear idea that improvement in technology and other aspects helps to provide vehicles with the utmost protection and knowledge to common people about road safety and traffic management makes them follow the rules.

As many new sensors are found and incorporated into vehicles there are more chances that these will be available at minimum cost and it will be affordable to all in future. The more the technology gets developed the efficiency of these sensors are to be maintained even during the availability of these sensors at lesser amount. If done then the accidents will be minimized on roads and it becomes a safer place for both vehicles and

Image-Based Steganography for Android: Concealing Secrets in Pixels

Ms. S. Sivasankari,48

E-mail: shankarirathnam@gmail.com, akashcyber2020@gmail.com, aakshayapriya27@gmail.com, hariharanmadesh1802@gmail.com

DOI: 10.1201/9781003430452-61

Abstract

Steganography is a technique used to hide sensitive information in mediums like images, audio, videotapes, etc. Steganography is really a useful concept for maintaining the security principles like confidentiality and authentication. The word is derived from the Greek word `steganographia.” With this method, concealed data discovery is eliminated. The benefit of employing data encryption is that it allows us to conceal any material behind the original data (stego file). Our Android-image-based Steganography is going to enhance security in secret communication using AES algorithm.

Keywords: steganography techniques, AES algorithm

Introduction

The common platform for steganography is image data due to high redundancy, resulting in digital image capacity for embedding. In early works in image steganography both in spatial domain and transform domains, non-adaptive methods were proposed.

Advantage of stego image, is using simply encrypted text is that message is kept inside the image and the quality of the image is not so much affected, so the chances of attacks possible on hidden messages become low.

In stego image data in internal image is not visible to any other person without processing an image. Here we implement stego image in Android applications using AES methods.

The software we use XML, java, and android studio.

The hardware we use 13 processor system, 8 GB RAM, 100 GB ROM or higher, Android Phone.

Related Work

Literature Review

Manohar and Kumar (2020) proposed a steganography technique for data hiding. Their paper explains that steganography is a technique for secret communication by hiding data in another form, making it undetectable without revealing it.

Aloraini et al. (2022), Subramanian et al. (2021) has developed a technique for hiding images and text using the Least Significant Bit (LSB) method in image steganography. Their paper describes how digital steganography conceals information within other data to ensure secure transmission.

Cogranne et al. (2022) proposed a quantized technique. Their paper explains how their approach embeds hidden messages by lowering deformation or analytical discern, improving the security of the omniscience optimal detector.

Nahar et al. (2021) studied the LSB technique and added Advanced Encryption System (AES) to enhance the security of the stego image. Their work aimed to embed data into a stego image with greater security.

Subramanian et al. (2021) and his teammates worked on increasing the data capacity for embedding user key values. Their work aimed to improve the data-hiding capacity of steganography techniques to enhance robustness.

Yang et al. (2020) researched on LSB-based techniques. In their paper, they discussed how to improve the strength of the stego image, fixing higher capacity, and undiscernible of secret gatherings can be achieved.

Advantages of image steganography

Security: Image steganography provides a high level of security, as it can be used to hide sensitive data within an image, making it difficult for unauthorized users to access or detect it (Manohar and Kumar 2020; Zhou et al., 2020; Subramanian et al., 2021).

Undetectability: Since steganography hides data within an image, it is difficult for an observer to detect that there is any hidden data at all. Thus, Subramanian et al. (2021) steganography provides a high level of secrecy and confidentiality.

Large Capacity: Images have a large storage capacity, so a lot of data can be hidden within them without affecting the image’s visual quality.

Disadvantage of Image Steganography

Vulnerability to detection: Although steganography is difficult to detect, it is not impossible. Advanced techniques and software tools can be used to detect hidden data within an image (Saxena and Maheshwari, 2021).

Loss of data: When data is hidden within an image, it may result in a loss of quality in the image. This is because steganography involves making subtle changes to the image, which can result in a degradation of the image’s quality (Cogranne et al., 2022).

Limited to specific types of files: Steganography is limited to specific files to embed the data.

Methods Used in

There are various techniques used in image steganography, some of which are:

Least Significant Bit (LSB) Embedding

This is the most commonly used technique in image steganography. In this method, the secret data is hidden in the LSB of the pixel merit of an image. The least significant bit of a pixel is the bit that has the least effect on the overall value of the pixel (Zhang et al., 2022).

Spread Spectrum Technique

This technique involves embedding the secret data by modulating the amplitude, frequency or phase of the pixels of an image using a carrier signal (Tian et al., 2022).

Transform Domain Techniques

This technique involves embedding the secret data by transforming the original image into a different domain, such as the frequency or wavelet domain, and then hiding the secret data in the transformed coefficients.

Distortion Techniques

This technique involves distorting the image slightly in any ways that the deformity is subtle to the naked eye but can be detected by a steganalysis tool (Pan et al., 2022).

Randomized techniques

This technique involves using a random generator to select pixels or groups of pixels to embed the secret message within, making it difficult to detect the presence of hidden data.

There are many other techniques used in image steganography, but the ones listed above are the most commonly used. The choice of technique will depend on the level of security required, the size of the message to be hidden, and the type of image being used (Meng et al., 2009).

Life Cycle of the Project

This model is said to be a Waterfall model. This model approach only down phases, as we cannot process the previous steps.

Advanced Encryption Standard Technique (AES)

Widespread use of AES is found in the symmetric key block cypher created by the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST (Nahar et al., 2021; Subramanian et al., 2021). It works with 128-bit static-size data blocks and encrypts them in a way that makes it difficult for unauthorized parties to decipher.

Data is encoded and decoded using AES and use a secret key (single key). The key range can be 128 bits, 192 bits, or 256 bits, and the encryption is more secure the larger the key size. Using the key and a sequence of mathematical operations on the plaintext, AES encrypts the data. These operations comprise, among others, substitution, permutation, and matrix multiplication.

The design of the works is a symmetric key which means single key is used to conceal both plain text and images (Subramanian et al., 2021).The unencrypted text and key values are 512-bit (64 bytes). To cope with the increasing computational power, we progress a strategy that works with 512 bits in a single block. Our algorithm uses a sub-box and XOR function to provide good reliability and effecting.

We first construct a 44-block matrix and then convert the key into its hexadecimal counterpart in order to do row shifting. Left circular shifts of 0 bits are represented by Row 1, 1 bits by Row 2, 2 bits by Row 3, and 3 bits by Row 4. The matrix is expanded into an 88-block matrix by applying the XOR operation to extra blocks if the key block size is larger than one. The matrix values are then replaced using S-Box after the entire matrix block has been inverted.

The matrix values are first categorized, after which they undergo hexadecimal, row, S-box, and reverse S-box transformations. Then, an s-box is created out of the matrix using row shifting=k and k = k’. The final key values were determined by substituting this significance using S- Box, even though K’ is the polar opposite of K (K’ = K) (Aloraini et al., 2022; Tang et al., 2022).

The 512-bit algorithm’s encryption procedure goes like this:

  • Take the text key of any size and plaintext.
  • Create an 8x8 block matrix with 1=0 and j=0, designated as M.
  • Hexadecimalize the message character to get its value.
  • Use XOR to combine the hexadecimal value with the key matrix.
  • Complete Interchange 1 by replacing Columns 1 and 2 with Columns 3, Columns 2, Columns 5, and Columns 6, and Columns 7 and Columns 8, respectively.
  • Switch the matrix’s complete block.

Conduct Interchange 2 by switching rows 1 through 3 by switching rows 2 through 4, switching rows 5 through 7, and switching rows 6 through 8.

Use the Substitution box to do the mix column operation, which is to XOR the constant matrix with the outcome of step 8. (S-box).

  • Use XOR to combine the secret text and step 10’s output.
  • Go through steps 6 through 11 up to four times.

In order to demonstrate how this method works, we organized the secret message “steganography” into an 8*8 matrix.

Conclusion

Wegatheredvarious image steganographytechniques and analyzed their advantages and disadvantages. From all the steganography methods, we selected the AES algorithm for its stronger encryption. We implemented image steganography in Android applications using Java programming languages. Our Android-based image steganography system is developed to facilitate secure secret communication without arousing undue curiosity.

Various Methods of Injection Attacks

Ms. G. Sathyadevi,49

Abstract

False Data Injection attacks cause series threat to web applications. The injection attacks are in the top ranks in dangerous vulnerabilities that can cause potentially severe damage. The proposed protection mechanism is based on an input filter. To prevent the entry of malicious commands and codes, this filter employs a restricted use of common expressions and characters used in SQL queries. The filter works by limiting the entry of fundamental characters, which helps to restrict the input of malicious codes and commands.

As a security scanner for frequent injection attacks, the filter code is employed. Requests are routed by the filter in two steps. The character is first checked against the blacklisted characters after a request to the filter is sent. If the character is invalid, it will be replaced by an empty string. If it is valid, the entered string will be set to its work. By this way, the input of malicious query codes and commands is restricted. Finally, the string entered will be ready for post-processing work. It is an effective way to prevent SQL injection attacks and is a valuable contribution to the community in the ongoing effort to secure web applications.

Keywords: SQL injection, False Data, SQL Queries, Vulnerabilities, Blacklisted Characters, Post Processing.

Introduction

A major security risk is the SQL injection vulnerability, which attackers can use to run malicious code and access a database without authorization. An attack known as SQL injection involves putting malicious SQL code into a website’s input field so that the backend database of the web application can use it to execute the code. A filter that checks characters submitted into input fields and filters out any that aren’t valid is suggested as a solution to this problem. Characters are categorized as blacklisted or whitelisted by the filter, and any blacklisted characters are replaced with an empty string. By doing this, popular symbols and characters that are frequently used in SQL injection attacks can’t be used to conduct injection attacks.

The proposed work comprises a simple character restriction filter that compares inputted strings to potential risk characters and replaces any matches with an empty string. This filter offers at least a first line of defense against SQL injection flaws. After the filtration process, the string is sent for input validation before being processed by the web application. This step is necessary to ensure that the input is valid and does not contain any malicious code that could bypass the filter. Input validation is an essential step in securing web applications and preventing SQL injection attacks.

Overall, the suggested filter offers a straight forward but efficient way to guard against SQL injection vulnerabilities. Organizations can safeguard their databases from malicious attacks and stop unauthorized access to sensitive information by validating and filtering input. To guard against SQL injection vulnerabilities and ensure the security and safety of their data, organizations must implement strong security measures.

Password Protection and Recovery

Mr. E. Rajkumar,50

Abstract

Password protection is the practice of using secret codes or phrases that are known only to the user to secure digital information or accounts. The value of password protection in protecting sensitive information, such as financial information, personal information, or secret documents is frequently discussed. A few of the password security methods suggested include the use of long, complicated passwords, password managers, and multi-factor authentication. It should also be noted that using weak or stolen passwords makes fraud, identity theft, and data breaches more likely. This paper further talks about several methods for regaining forgotten passwords, such as password resets or email or security question confirmation. This paper concludes by highlighting the critical role password protection plays in safeguarding digital information and providing readers with a summary of the key concepts involved.

Introduction

The most popular user authentication method is passwords, which are frequently used to protect sensitive data. Passwords are essential for ensuring data security as they act as the first line of defense in securing online accounts. Yet, using incorrect passwords makes it easy for hackers to crack them might result in security issues and data breaches. It’s crucial to make sure that passwords are adequately secured and to have efficient recovery methods in place to prevent password loss or theft. Requiring strong passwords, password hashing, and multi-factor authentication are all examples of password protection techniques. Password hashing ensures that the password is not stored, and requirements for password strength promote the usage of complicated, challenging passwords. Rather than being hashed into plaintext instead of being changed into a hashed value, making it difficult to decipher the original password’s plaintext. whereas multi-Factor authentication establishes extra security by requiring users to provide added authentication factors in addition to their passwords, such as a fingerprint or a one-time code generated by a mobile app. Regaining access to a device or account that has been locked or rendered inoperable because of a forgotten or lost password is referred to as password recovery. In digital devices and online services, password recovery techniques are routinely used to stop data loss, reduce service interruptions, and provide users access to their accounts after they have been locked out.

Typically, during password recovery procedures, the user is confirmed using a variety of ways, such as email or the confirmation of personal data. Upon user authentication, a password reset, or recovery option is displayed. This could entail answering security questions, submitting a verification code, or receiving a link to reset your password Techniques for password recovery include those for phone, email, and security question confirmation. To confirm a user’s identity, security questions are frequently used in conjunction with email and phone verification. Email and phone verification can be used to update a password or unlock an account.in ensuring that crucial data and the internet. The accounts are safe. To prevent unauthorized access to sensitive data, it is crucial to be attentive and continually enhance password protection and recovery procedures. One of the underlying problems with password protection is that traditional password-based authentication systems are vulnerable to attacks like brute force attacks, dictionary attacks, and phishing attacks. In recent years, attacks on online websites have increased, often exploiting poor password management on the websites. Registered users are often the victims of these attacks and are required to quickly change their credentials due to a generic leakage compromising their current ones. Even if users choose strong passwords, the websites’ password storage must respect basic security guidelines for it to be effective. Two examples of major data breaches in recent years are LinkedIn and Yahoo.
