A Hybrid Model for Guided Filtering-Based Edge Preservation of Fused Multi-modal Medical Images

S. Sandhya,55

E-mail: Corresponding Author: sanrsn@gmail.com, msen1982@gmail.com, profbcr@yahoo.com, suseekannan07@gmail.com

DOI: 10.1201/9781003430452-69

Abstract

The process of generating quality visual information by integrating the salient features of the medical images captured from multi-modalities is said to be medical image fusion. In such a process of fusion of medical images, the biggest challenge lies in combining the significant features into a single fused image as it possesses limitations like cost of computation, the distinction between several multi-modalities, artifacts of fusion, and then the base hardness. In order to overcome such limitations in the process of fusing multimodal medical images, hybrid model has been proposed. The hybrid model uses contourlet-based transform method NSCT along with PCA and then the GE The medical images that are taken as sources from multi-modals are decomposed into low-frequency and high-frequency components respectively using NSCT. To the two levels of frequency components that are generated, principal component analysis is applied in order to retrieve the superlative components for the procedure of image fusion. Rules for fusion are applied then to the principal components generated to which the inverse version of NSCT is applied and the resultant fused image is retrieved with visual quality. Finally, information present in the edges is retained in the fused image with the assistance of guided filter.

Keywords: Medical Image Fusion; Guided Filtering; Principal Component Analysis; Contourlet Transform; NSCT

Introduction

In order to make an accurate medical diagnosis, clinical experts require more details of the medical images captured with the help of multimodalities. Modern medical imaging has revolutionized clinical diagnosis by providing a range of diagnostic images. CT, MRI, PET, and SPECT are just a few examples of imaging techniques that focus on different aspects of the body to provide critical information (Bharath & Suganthi, 2018). All these modalities concentrate on different aspects in order to furnish wide range of information. With the limitations of modalities of medical imaging, an integrated medical fusion of multimodalities to generate a single fuse medical image is required with which the accuracy of clinical diagnosis can be improved and achieved to a great magnitude. For such purposes of multimodal medical image-fusion techniques like transformation, neural networks, directed image filtering, and spatial image fusion can be used. In pixel level of fusion, manipulation is performed directly on the image’s pixels to generate the fused image which constitutes the lowermost level of fusion (Liu et al., 2018). Pixel level image fusion has been a topic of study for more than 30 years, resulting in a vast scientific literature. In recent years, deep learning has made remarkable progress in various computer vision and image processing problems, including image fusion for digital photography and multimodality imaging. In decision level, information about the probabilistic decision obtained through the help of local decision producers which operates on the outcomes of feature-level computation of images that are created from sensors is considered. In the feature level of fusion ( (Huan et al., 2020; Rajalingam et al., 2020), significant features from the images are extracted based on information like texture, pixel intensity, and edges. Extracted features will be fused together to generate the final image. Each method of image fusion has its own limitation. In order to overcome the limitations, fusion is performed by adopting a hybrid model to the medical images considered from multi-modals that are anticipated in medical imaging applications (Du et al., 2016).

Materials and Methods

Literature study shows like transform-based methods like DWT (Discrete Wavelet Transform), CT (Contourlet Transform), DCT (Discrete Cosine Transform), ST (Shearlet Transform), neural networks are widely used for the process of fusion of images. In Ullah et al., (2020) DTCWT along with SOFM is used to perform the process of fusion. Concepts of deep learning and convolutional neural networks are gaining significance in recent years (Ullah et al., 2020; Hossain et al., 2019; Liu et al., 2017 a; Liu et al., 2017b). Image fusion is modest and tranquil while it is being performed using the principal component analysis. But it suffers from the problem of color distortion of the images (Li et al., 2018). Low contrast fusion of images is done with the help of the color space transformation technique. Information about the direction cannot be obtained while using the pyramid based transform technique. Sparse representation-based techniques take much time in the phases of training and optimizing the dictionary being constructed. Neural network-based methodologies rely upon training the network by adjusting the parameters accordingly. Non Subsampled Shearlet Transform is used in Xia et al. (2020); Xi et al. (2018) in which the source medical images are disintegrated into coefficients at both the frequency levels of high and low. Then the high-frequency coefficients and low-frequency coefficients are fused using parameter adaptive pulse coupled neural network (PAPCNN) and convolution sparse representation (SR) respectively. Over the few years, hybrid methods for image fusion gains its importance as it yields efficient and better results (Kumar et al., 2018). Fuzzy approach along with stationary wavelet transform was used in Yin et al. (2019) thus performing the fusion process with the outstanding cost involved for the time of execution. DTCWT techniques along with high-boost filtering are used in Stephan et al. (2020) which preserves the information of the edges in the resulting image. In Li et al. (2019); Liu et al. (2017) medical images are integrated using the functionalities of NSST along with the technique of adaptive neural spiking. Though several techniques are available for performing the task of fusion, limitations like noise in images, loss of edge information, and images with low contrast still persist. A hybrid technique is proposed in this paper which comprises the features of NCST [19], PCA, and Guided Filter Gao et al. (2021); Li et al. (2019) to perform multimodal medical image fusion with efficacy.

Proposed System

NSCT is a contourlet-based transform method that is used to visualize the effects as geometrical images (Yin et al., 2019). Contourlet transform is a transition-based technique in which it uses both the up and down samplers at the levels of laplacian pyramid and the dimensional bank filter. Once the frequency components are generated at the high and low levels, principal component analysis is used to generate the coefficients at their best for further processing thus by reducing the redundancy (Zhu et al., 2019). NSCT is completely a multi-scale, shift-invariant, and multi-direction transform technique and it uses the non-sub-sampled pyramid filter bank (NSS-PFB) and non-sub-sampled directional filter bank (NSS-DFB) to achieve the shift-invariance. The NSS-PFB is a structure that is based on shift-invariant filtering to retain multi-scale property of NSCT by deploying 2-channel non-sub-sampled 2 dimensional filter bank. NSS-DFB is fabricated by eliminating the up and down samplers that is available in the 2 channel filter bank. Principal component analysis involves the conversion of correlated variables into several uncorrelated variables. Once the coefficients are formed, they are applied with fusion rules. Average of the components and their related details are generated by involving fusion rules at the levels of average, maximum, and minimum which form the respective fusion rules. The edge details of the images are preserved by applying guided filtering to the high frequency components constructed using NSCT. Next, the inverse of NSCT is applied on integrated components to obtain the fused image as shown in Figure 1. Information containing details of edges present in the images are retained with the help of guided-filter and also smoothening of image by taking the second source image as guidance to perform the process of image filtering. The second source image considered for guidance is also known as guidance image. The benefit of using a guided filter is that it outperforms the artifacts of gradient reverse as well as for the necessity in retaining edge information of the final fused image as medical imaging comprises noises..

Experimental Evaluation and Discussion

Experiments are conducted to obtain the result images of size 512 × 512 by avoiding the use of medical images with low contrast and guidance image. For the evaluation of proposed hybrid model CT and MRI images are taken into account as image of source which is obtained from the Medical School of Harvard for the whole brain. MATLAB R2017b was employed to conduct the experiments on a computer with an i7 CPU and 4GB of RAM. The input images considered are a kind of gray-scale images. Initially, fusion results are obtained without using the guidance image by lowering the contrast of images at first and finally, the quality of a fused final image is enhanced by these images with low contrast visually. Performance metrics details are as follows:

  1. Standard Deviation: During the transmission, it constitutes the source image as well as noise. High value for a standard deviation of an image implies high contrast of the fused image. Standard deviation is signified in equation (1),

    (1)
    $$\begin{array}{l} {\text{STD} = \sqrt{\frac{1}{axb}{\sum_{i = 1}^{a}{\sum_{j = 1}^{b}\left( {F_{ij} - MEAN} \right)^{2}}}}} \\ {\text{In}\,\left( 1 \right),\,\text{MEAN=}\frac{1}{axb}{\sum_{i = 1}^{a}{\sum_{j = 1}^{b}\left| F_{ij} \right|}}} \\ \end{array}$$

  2. Spatial Frequency: The entire level of activity in the image space is measured using spatial frequency. Higher value of spatial frequency entails that the information present in the final fused result image is also high and therefore the performance of fusion is achieved better. Spatial frequency is defined as in equation (2),

    (2)
    $$\text{SF} = \sqrt{RF^{2} + CF^{2}}$$

    RF-row frequency and CF-column frequency in the space of images considered.


    $$\begin{array}{l} {\text{RF} = \sqrt{\frac{1}{ab}{\sum_{i = 1}^{a}{\sum_{j = 2}^{b}\left( {F_{ij} - F_{i{({j - 1})}}} \right)^{2}}}}\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\text{and}} \\ {\text{CF=}\sqrt{\frac{1}{ab}{\sum_{j = 1}^{b}{\sum_{i = 2}^{a}\left( {F_{ij} - F_{j{({i - 1})}}} \right)^{2}}}}} \\ \end{array}$$

  3. Entropy

    The content level of the information that exists in the fused image is measured using entropy. Fused images possess information with rich content that holds a higher value for entropy and it is given in equation (3)

    (3)
    $$\text{EN=}{\sum\limits_{l = 0}^{L - 1}{p_{l}\log_{2}}}\left( p_{l} \right)$$

L represents the count of intensities of gray in the source image and Pl represents lth intensity value as a probability value present in the image.

Two sets of input images CT and MRI are taken for the purpose of fusion is carried out independently with PCA, NSCT, DWT, GIF. The fusion results are depicted in Figs. 2 and 3.

Conclusion

The proposed fusion technique aims to overcome those limitations thus by providing fused images with high contrast by retaining the most significant features or information of the images that have been considered. The idea behind preserving edge information is achieved by incorporating the guided filter into the final fused image. The usage of a guided filter helps in preserving the edge information of the images considered for the process of fusion by taking the high-frequency components generated by NSCT. As high-frequency components consist of more details of the images like texture and other details, it is also possible for those components to have noises. Thus appropriate fusion rules are chosen to handle the noises present in images.

State of Art Survey on Memory Forensic Acquisition & Techniques

Ms. K. R. Nandhashree,56

Email: nandhashree29@gmail.com, aadhisiva65@gmail.com, selvabala21m@gmail.com, yuvanesh05k@gmail.com

DOI: 10.1201/9781003430452-70

Abstract

Computer forensics is majorly dependent on disk-based forensics, and it has become less effective due to various storage devices like flash drives. Memory forensics has become an important area of research in digital forensics due to the increasing use of computers in criminal activities. RAM and ROM are the two primary types of memory in a computer system, and they play a crucial role in the forensic analysis of digital evidence. In this paper, we present a survey of memory forensics techniques on live acquisition, dead acquisition, data acquisition, and memory acquisition, highlighting their strengths and limitations. Finally, the proposed survey is to study the current growth of the memory forensics framework for the investigation of Volatile and Non-Volatile memory.

Keywords: Memory Forensics, Memory Acquisition, Live Acquisition, Dead Acquisition

Introduction

Digital forensics has commonly focused on artifacts that are stored on workstations (computers), mobile phones, cameras, and several electronic devices. Yet on past ten years, researchers have developed many numbers of memory forensic tools that assist in the investigation of volatile memory also, expand the purview of memory forensics. This article reviews the numerous studies in storage (memory) forensics, offers a critical evaluation of modern methodologies, discusses significant advancements in an operating system architecture that have an impact on memory forensics and identifies key topics for further study. Storage forensics techniques are often employed with bit-perfect copies of storage media and are mostly focused on “dead” examination. These copies are used to recover deleted files or file specks, to identify file access samples, track previous web surfing behavior, and perform other operations. There has been a gravity growth in the number of forensic targets, and more cases are pending because of increased criminal activity. These include fashion in malware development, where malware now regularly leaves no footprint on Volatile storage devices, a momentous increase in the size of forensic targets, huge case backlogs as more misconduct (criminal) activity involves the use of computers, and the use of forensics techniques in incident response to tackle malware. Process lists, network connections, chat message fragments, lists of open connections, and combing material for drive encryptions are some examples of this evidence.

Literature Survey

In this section, a survey of Memory forensics process is explained. Figure 1 represents the types of memory forensic processes.

Live Acquisition

By a storage component, the real-time gathering of data and its processing are separated. One of these emerging technologies is 3D XPoint (Gupta, 2017), which claims to bridge the opening between memory and conventional repository(storage) and it provides non-volatile data with unheard- of high throughput. In this paper, we describe the functionality of 3D XPoint-based permanent memory devices in the framework of the DAQ system for the Deep Underground Neutrino Experiment (DUNE), one of the largest ever conducted. Also, a high-level application that makes use of Data Center Persistent Memory (DCPMM) was created and combined with a test setup to confirm its possible application for the DUNE supernova repository(storage) buffer. It was observed that the overhead added by the PMDK software library had an impact on overall performance. Hence, software improvements that as a result, software enhancements that make use of the MOVNTI instruction set were added, and the following performance was up by 20%. It was observed that the system behaves individually of the entry(access) size and, it confirms the memory state of the DCPMM. In Kumar et al. (2018), the author uses several Hash functions in mathematical algorithms so that the forensic investigator can prove whether the file has been tampered or not.

Volatile Memory Acquisition

Volatile memory, which holds some store of valuable information including the ordinary text of application data, dynamically presents the current state of the OS and applications. It is an overall analysis object in the field of memory forensics. This research (Ullah et al., 2020) provides an Android OS application volatile memory data collecting technique termed as Private Application Storage Memory (PASM) that can be used in computer forensic settings as well as on unprepared Android devices. PASM utilizes the system-level data migration functionality made available by the Android Original Equipment Manufacturer to import the application’s private data into a middle device (OEM).

The findings of the experiment show that PASM can acquire some private information kept in primary memory, but top-up crucially, PASM can crossover the majority of practical limitations, creating it additionally useful than the Android OS memory acquisition techniques that were now in use.

In this paper, a private data loggers(acquisition) technique for Android mobile devices called PASM is proposed. It is based on memory forensics and system-level data migration. This essay provides a thorough introduction to PASM’s principle, framework, implementation, and process. Six types of thirty applications are tested in seven different experimental settings. The results of the trial demonstrate that our suggested PASM can successfully access various programs installed on unmodified devices’ memory data, including account usernames, passwords, and other confidential information.

Memory Dump Analysis

Examining a computer’s memory at the time of a crash, a system failure, or any unusual occurrence is known as memory dump analysis. The dump file is captured in .mem file. The memory dump is typically recorded to a file on the hard disc, which can then be examined using specialized software like the Volatility Framework. In Xia et al., (2020) authors propose a two-step approach to memory dump analysis that involves firstly acquiring the volatile memory data and non-volatile memory data. It then combines the extracted contents and converts them into 3D memory systems.

Dead Acquisition

Non-volatile memory is a kind of computer memory that keeps the data it contains even if the power is lost or turned off. Because of this, non-volatile memory can be used to store data including operating system files, software code, and user data that must be kept for a long time. When a system cannot be safely shut down in a way that enables live acquisition, such as when the system is thought to have been compromised by malware that may destroy or hide its presence in memory when it detects an attempt to acquire it, dead acquisition may occasionally be required in memory forensics. Dead acquisition entails physically removing the memory modules from the system and extracting the stored data using specialized tools. File system metadata includes details like file names, timestamps, permissions, and sizes of the files and directories that are kept on a file system (Rajalingam et al., 2020). File system metadata in memory forensics can be a useful source of data for comprehending system behavior and spotting potential security concerns. The following are some applications of file system information in memory forensics:

1 Flex capacity in memory forensic technique.

Timeline analysis can assist discover patterns of behavior or suspicious activity by allowing analysts to generate a timeline of file and directory activity on the system using file system metadata. It can locate deleted files and perhaps retrieve them. File system information can assist analysts in tracking out which files have been viewed, updated, or executed on the system. Understanding user or system behavior and spotting possible security incidents can both benefit from this information.

2 System configuration identification

File system metadata can offer useful details about the setup of the system, such as the placement of crucial system files or the presence of programs or applications. In memory forensics, file system metadata is a significant source of data that may be used to recreate a system’s activities and spot potential security incidents. Nonetheless, it’s crucial to keep in mind that file system metadata can get the accurate timestamp of the modification time.

3 Finding deleted files

A file’s information could still exist in memory even after it has been removed from the file system. Analysts may examine file system metadata stored in memory by means of the Data regarding the files and directories on a storage device, such as timestamps, file names, and file properties, is included in file system metadata. In addition to approaches for recovering lost files and for analyzing data from unallocated disc space, the article discusses several ways to recover file system information. It also talks about difficulties that detectives could run into when trying to recover file system metadata, like file system damage or encryption. A variety of electronic devices, including smartphones, digital cameras, and solid-state drives, utilize flash memory, a sort of non-volatile memory.

Non-Volatile Memory Acquisition

Dong et.al. uses a certain approach for retrieving data from a NAND flash memory device is referred to as a “copy-back program”. Data is copied from memory to another location, modified if necessary, and then written back to the original location by the copy-back software (Bharath and Suganthi, 2018). This method can be used in forensics to recover data from memory cells that have been destroyed or corrupted. Analyzing file systems and data structures includes assessing how data is organized.

To retrieve data from NAND flash memory devices, a copy-back technique is used. To use this method, the data must first be copied from the memory device to another location, where it can then be modified as necessary before being written back to the original location. Data recorded in NAND flash memory that is damaged or corrupted may no longer be accessible or may even be lost. The data from these damaged memory cells can be recovered using “copy-back approach” by transferring to another location, fixing or changing it as necessary, and then writing it back to separate memory. When memory cells are damaged or corrupted, it can be a helpful strategy for recovering data that might otherwise be lost.

NAND flash memory Analysis

A memory forensic method known as Flex Capacity technology takes a snapshot of the memory of an active system and examines it on a machine with larger storage (Huan et al., 2020). This method enables analysts to examine larger dumps that might not be possible on the system where the dump was created owing to storage constraints. This method has the benefit of allowing the investigator to examine a larger dump, which might have more information pertinent to the investigation. When the system being studied has little room for storage or the dump is too big to be examined on the system from which it was taken, the Flex-Capacity approach is extremely helpful. Investigators may be able to conduct a more thorough storage analysis and find more evidence relevant to the investigation by using a separate system with additional storage space. To maintain dump integrity, it should be noted that the flex-capacity technique necessitates careful consideration of memory acquisition and transfer processes. Dump capture and transmission should be done with tools and techniques that maintain data integrity since changes or modifications to dumps can affect inspection results.

Discussions

To evaluate perfection and distinctness, digital forensic tool findings must be quotable and consistent. Table 1 shows the forensic method used by the authors. Repeatability assures that independent test outcomes are obtained over a short time frame using the same process, identical test samples, the same laboratory, the same operator, and the same equipment.

Table 1 Memory Forensics Literature Review
Reference Forensic Method Author Contribution
[1] Copy Back program approach It explores how these operations can be used to analyze the contents of NAND Flash Memory.
[2] Flex Capacity Tells us about forensic issues and techniques used to enhance accuracy in retrieving in SSD.
[3] File system metadata signatures Recovering metadata from unallocated space on storage devices
[4] Virtual Machine (VM) memory dumps Analyze the dumps to extract information about ransomware behavior.
[5] Deep Underground Neutrino Experiment (DUNE) Proposes data retrieval with low latency and implementation of persistent memory module.
[6] System level data migration Acquiring private data from various applications.
[7] Flash memory technology Potential environmental impact on flash memory and its advancement.
[8] Mathematical model to describe the behavior of storage systems Analyze the reliability of different storage systems and identify their potential weakness.
[9] Near Volatile and Non-Volatile Memory Processing(NVNMP) Hybrid architecture that combines both memory types into 3D memory system
[10] Cryptographic technique and Access Control mechanism Proposes a secure key management system and periodic data backups.
[11] Digital Signature and Hash Function Uses several cryptographic algorithms to verify integrity checksums after data acquisition process.

Reliability ensures that the test solutions (results) are acquired using a similar procedure on the same test objects in various labs by various operators using various pieces of apparatus. As an outcome, the credibility and perfection of the results generated by these toolkits were not evaluated in this research because we relied on data from providers and users of investigation software.

Conclusion

Based on the study of the survey papers, it can be concluded that memory (storage) forensics was used to acquire, analyze and generate report for digital investigations and analysis, particularly for analyzing volatile memory (RAM) dump and analyzing the collected data. Memory forensics techniques and tools have evolved significantly over the years, and they are now capable of extracting valuable information such as running processes, open network connections, registry keys, and even encrypted hashes from RAM. However, the process of analyzing ROM can be more challenging due to the complexity of firmware, the lack of standardized extraction tools, and the need for specialized skills.

Product Review System using CNN & MERN Stack

Karnati Bhavesh Kumar Reddy, Tondapu Sumanth Reddy, M. Sambath, and J. Thanga Kumar

Department of Computer Science Engineering, Hindustan Institute of Technology and Science, Chennai, India

E-mail: sumanthreddyt719@gmail.com, msambath@hindustanuniv.ac.in, tkumar@hindustanuniv.ac.in, *bhavesh03042002@gmail.com

DOI: 10.1201/9781003430452-71

Abstract

The e-commerce sector has grown quickly over the past ten years. AI significantly influences client purchase decisions and behavior in a favorable way. User experience and user interface research and development are always developing in order to draw in clients. The goal of user experience is to maintain a user’s loyalty to a product or brand by offering satisfying experiences. By offering a variety of tactics for voice control and a system for product reviews, the branch of artificial intelligence known as Natural Language Processing enables firms to customize their e-commerce applications and improve customer experience. Using MERN Stack, the application platform may be built with smaller package bundle sizes, which enhances performance. MongoDB, the Express.JS framework, the React.JS library, and Node.JS make up the MERN Stack. Understanding online customers’ wants and behaviors is essential given their increasing rise. Thus, to determine client demands and preferences for online goods and services, E-Commerce companies combined AI enabled technology. Artificial intelligence keeps track of the customer’s preferences, buying habits, frequency of purchases, and average dollar amount during a certain time period. As a result, this data enables firms to tailor their goods and services to their consumers’ specific needs and preferences.

Keywords: Natural Language Processing, Sentiment Analysis, Speech Recognition, User Experience

Introduction

Technology has become an essential tool for Internet marketing. The majority of individuals throughout the world are interested in making online purchases. Furthermore, buyers may select from a range of items depending on their tastes and cost, and online shopping allows them to compare prices between different businesses. The voice control functionality of the fully developed e-commerce application with AI algorithms allows it to function as a segmented system for online product reviews. Natural Language Processing (Danenas and Skersys, 2022; Shaik et al., 2022) techniques such as sentiment analysis, which classify text or product reviews as good or negative, are used to enable voice-controlled systems and product review systems. Convolutional neural networks were used in the development of the sentiment analysis (Jain et al., 2021; Shaik et al., 2022; Jadhav and Jadhav, 2020; Li et al., 2020; Chakraborty et al., 2018; Chen et al., 2017) model because they are more accurate than recurrent neural networks at accurately identifying key traits. The preceding model, the Elman Recurrent Neural Network, requires far more data than any other conventional machine learning method, requiring hundreds or even millions of labeled samples. As a result, it is computationally expensive. Additionally, there is no set formula for figuring out how ENN is structured. Using the IMDB review data set, product review software extracts an integer value from the review string and uses it to categorize the review as positive or negative. It also creates custom emoji based on the integer value. As the application uses MongoDB, which stores and transfers data in form of JSON, and React also uses JSON, there is no need for type casting, which minimizes complexity. As a result, data can be shared much more quickly between the database and the client application.

Literature Survey

Zhao et al., (2021) produced the Local Search Improvised Bat Algorithm-based Elman Neural Network, a novel, enhanced Machine Learning method for the SA of internet product reviews. The “4” primary procedures that comprise SA’s intended work are data collection (DC), pre- processing (PP), feature extraction (FE), feature selection (FS), and sentiment classifications (SC). To begin, the Web Scrapping Tool is used to harvest customer reviews of items for which data is obtained from E-commerce websites (WST). The pre-processing step follows the data gathering from the web scraping. Finally, the LSIBA-ENN categorizes customer reviews as positive, negative, or neutral using the HM-EWA data.

Jain et al., (2021) completed a comprehensive survey of the literature on uses using machine learning for analyzing consumer sentiment. The authors reviewed the existing literature on several machine learning algorithms and their applications in consumer sentiment analysis. They explained how different machine learning algorithms solve important issues in consumer sentiment analysis, such as data sparsity and imbalance

Danenas and Skersys (2022) investigate the feasibility of using natural language processing into visual model-to-model (M2M) conversions. As a result, report our research findings on information extraction from text labels in process models represented in Business Process Modelling Notation (BPMN) and use case models expressed in Unified Modelling Language, making use of the most recent advances in natural language processing (UML). To achieve these aims, they employ proprietary BERT-Bi LSTM-CRF and EL Mobi LSTM-CRF implementations that have been trained with relevant data augmentations, as well as the most recent cutting-edge NLP tools. These methods are also used to extract noun and verb phrases from brief text labels.

Shukla et al., (2022) designed to build an e-commerce platform utilizing the MERN Stack, a new technology that combines NodeJS, Express JS, MongoDB, and React JS. The fundamental e-commerce platform includes a number of tools and techniques for offering home delivery services for goods, including online payment, selection, and product choice. Utilizing MERN Stack, Sign In/Login methods are utilized to distinguish one user from another when generating a dashboard for a list of products. Since then, research has been conducted to develop an online web application that may be used by small-scale vendors worldwide. Customers can easily look for urgent products from the stores in their area.

Soni (2020) formulated data that enables firms to cater their goods and services to the unique requirements and preferences of their clients. The AI assists the user in selecting and purchasing the best suggested items and services by providing a choice of product suggestions, discounts, and various offers. 200 individuals from varied socioeconomic backgrounds in Haryana provided data for the current study. For online shopping, the results show a strong relationship between Artificial Intelligence and Consumer Buying Behaviour.

Proposed System

The clusters of the databases for items and customers are connected to the particular front-end elements in the proposed system shown in Fig. 1. The product review is transmitted to the back-end via REST API services when the user opens the product and submits it. The back end computes the sentiment value, categorizes the review, and changes the relevant database.

The REST API essentially serves as an interface for safe data transmission between two information systems via the internet. This API delivers both the model’s output to the front end and the data to the server where the model is deployed. Emojis are also provided by the component based on sentiment value, enhancing the user experience. Additionally, to carry out voice-controlled tasks, the speech recognition-enabled microphone component accepts voice instructions as input and translates them into text.

The product review is collected as input in the proposed system shown in Fig. 2. All necessary libraries, including NumPy, Pandas, and TensorFlow, are imported during the data preparation process.

To eliminate noisy data from the obtained text, data pre-processing is done. Convolutional neural networks are trained once the texts have been tokenized. As a result, text is categorized more accurately by using the learned numerical value instead of a manual method.

In the suggested system shown in Fig. 3., voice command inputs are gathered as inputs and cleaned and removed from noisy data prior to processing. The speech tensors are segmented to words, and feature extraction is performed.

Feature extraction improves the accuracy of model by reducing the redundant data and also boosts the speed of learning. The tensors with words are trained on speech recognition model and are converted into text.

Algorithm:

INPUT: Text File (comment or review) T, The sentiment lexicon L.

OUTPUT: Smt= {P, Ng, or N} and Strength S, where P: Positive, Ng: Negative, N:Neutral.

INITIALIZATION: SPos and SNeg=0, where

SPos: builds up the positive tokens’ polarity in ti-Smt.

SNeg: gathers the negative polarity of tokens in ti-Smt

Begin

  1. For each ti € T do
  2. Search for ti in L
  3. If ti€ Pos-list then ← SPos Spos + ti-smt
  4. Else if ti€ Neg-list then ← SNeg SNeg+ ti-Smt
  5. End If
  6. End For
  7. If SPos>|SNeg| then
  8. Smt = P
  9. S = SPos/(SPos+SNeg)
  10. Else If SPos<|SNeg| then
  11. Smt = Ng
  12. S = SNeg/(SPos +SNeg)
  13. Else
  14. Smt = N
  15. S = SPos/(SPos +SNeg)18. End If

End

Results and Discussion

The accuracy percentage is measured for the two models CNN and Res Net with the data augmentation producing an accuracy score of 91% and 75% respectively as shown in Fig. 3.

The model’s accuracy is determined by comparing its predictions to the actual output. In this case, the accuracy was recorded at different epochs, which means that the model’s accuracy was calculated and recorded after each epoch.

Finally, “attained the maximum accuracy at epoch count 3 as you can see in Fig. 4” indicates that the best accuracy was obtained after three epochs of training, as shown in a graph or chart (presumably Fig 4) that shows the accuracy at each epoch. The review is provided as input, and the tokenizer converts the review string into tokens, which are then sent to the model for output. The model assigns a positive and negative value to the review. If the positive and negative values are roughly equal, it assigns an average tag; if the positive is greater than negative, the review is classified as positive, and vice versa.

Conclusion

It explains how to use IMDB data and deep learning techniques like Word2Vec and Convolutional Neural Networks to analyze sentiment (CNN). Before being imported from a TSV file, the data is first pre-processed to convert text data into a numerical form. The text data is then cleaned, tokenized, and converted into word vectors using the Google Word2Vec model. After that, a Cony Net is created to train and categorize text input. The findings show that the model performs well on test data, with an accuracy of roughly 88 %.

Abstract

The method of addressing the automated finding of information inside the database is known as data mining. The capacity to keep and record personal data on service users and people has rapidly increased as a result of recent breakthroughs in hardware technology. The danger of disclosing data to third parties during data mining operations has grown due to data sets that contain sensitive personal information. Data mining that protects privacy strives to maintain the value of the data without violating respect for the privacy of private or confidential data. An extension of maintaining privacy when mining data that takes care of both quantity and utility is referred to as maintaining your privacy Utility mining. Because perceptive data must be kept private for analytical purposes, privacy preservation in data mining with high-utility sets has grown in importance and difficulty. Several industries, including a basket of goods, trading, analysis of click-streams, medical surveys, and computational biology, generate a large number of data using utility-oriented patterns and analytics by taking into account precise information. Perturbation is a technique that adheres to the data owner’s privacy regulations while changing the database’s contents within certain restrictions. In this research, the Frequency Count supply an excellent method for privacy preservation that is utilized for fast perturbation and provides a simple technique that we employ to conceal all highly sensitive item sets. This also cleanses the transaction database and employs a unique perturbation technique, distinct structures for item set tables, and a sorted list of sensitive items. Our paper is focused on the effectiveness shown by contrasting the Fast Perturbation Using the Frequency Count method with the Using Tree Structures and Tables for the Rapid Perturbation approach, it can be extended and implemented using different criteria.

Mining of Data is the procedure for studying enormous volumes of data to find buried important ideas. A data mining technique called frequent pattern mining is used to find pertinent patterns or item groups in a database. The item sets that appear most frequently in a database are those with relevant sequences. High-Utility Item Set Mining is a utility mining approach that creates transaction database item sets with a high profit. In real-world circumstances, it is more practical than routine item set mining. The availability of data can be referred to as the term utility.

There is a huge explosion of information today. As a result, it is critical to extract meaningful knowledge from enormous volumes of duets for upcoming use or to create upcoming forecasts. These records should be examined to look for trends that might be utilized to forecast future behavior. Yet, for privacy reasons, Owners of data are reluctant to disclose their primary data sets. Utility Mining with Privacy Data Mining with Privacy Protection is an expansion of Data Mining. Utility Mining with Privacy Protection is designed to conceal sensitive high-utility item setups. Literature Review

Data Perturbation Technique

This method modifies accessible data before passing it along to data mining. The quality of the provided data is preserved even after the data has been modified in a variety of ways, such as swapping, adding noise, etc. In the instance of the noise addition approach, the data owner adds some noise in the form of random numbers. To preserve the original data’s characteristics, this arbitrary number is frequently drawn to have a zero mean and a tiny standard deviation from a normal distribution. When it comes to data mining, the data owner shares this noisy data. The data owner is also aware of the spread of the noise inserted into the original data. Mining of Data can reconstruct the distribution of the real data set utilizing this distribution plus noisy data. Real data values, however, cannot be retrieved via data mining. Because of this, a Data Mining algorithm might provide a significantly more accurate result without disclosing the real data (Aggarwal and Yu, 2008).

In the instance of the data swapping approach, it preserves every original value in the data set while also making record re-identification extremely difficult. When data is swapped, attribute values are changed between several records. Similar attribute values are swapped out more frequently. This method’s distinguishing characteristic is that all original values are retained inside the data set just the placements are changed. Data Mining with Privacy Protection

Data Mining with Privacy Protection techniques has been developed to extract information from data sets without disclosing the identity of data subjects or sensitive information. Moreover, Data Mining

with Privacy Protection allows several researchers to collaborate on a dataset (Nayak, 2011; Verykios and Gkoulalas-Divanis, 2008). To protect privacy, the great majority of these solutions rely on original data. This refers to the inherent trade-off between data quality and level of privacy. Data Mining with Privacy Protection techniques is being investigated in order to do effective data mining while maintaining a certain amount of privacy. Many different taxonomies have been proposed for these approaches. In the literature, data mining outputs are classified according to the data life cycle phases (data collection, publishing, distribution, and data mining output) (Yun and Kim, 2015) or the method used based on Anonymization, perturbation, randomization, condensation, and cryptography (Yun and Kim, 2015). In this paper, Data Mining with Privacy Protection approaches is used to study input data and processed data (output information) that are suitable for data mining.

Frequency Counting for Fast Perturbation

The major purpose of the Frequency Counting for the Rapid Perturbation approach is to lower the utility value of each sensitive item set by altering the quantity values of each item in each sensitive item set. The Frequency Counting for the Quick Perturbation must discover the item with the most usefulness in the transactional database and minimize its count while causing the least amount of information loss for each sensitive item in the sensitive item set. The procedure is repeated until all sensitive item sets utility values to fall below the minimal utility criterion (Jisna and Salim, 2018).

Utilizing Tree and Table Design with Rapid Perturbation

Using the tree and tables, Utilizing Tree and Table design with Rapid Perturbation creates perturbed data before returning the associated perturbed database containing the data. Sensitive item sets are hidden using the Utilizing Tree and Table design with Rapid Perturbation (Gan et al., 2018), which uses two structures to expedite the perturbation process. It simply needs to scan the database three times to complete the perturbation process. To create the head table, Frequency Counting for Fast Perturbation first examines the database. The items must be included only by sensitive item sets in the head table.

After that, they are ordered by count values in descending order. The database is then rescanned one more, and a Utilizing Tree and Table design with a Rapid Perturbation tree based on the head table is created. The sensitive item sets are then individually hidden after the Utilizing Tree and Table Structures for Rapid Perturbation tree have been constructed. It conceals the delicate item sets one by one after constructing the entire Utilizing Tree and Table design with Rapid Perturbation tree. The target items may be rapidly located and adjusted based on the sensitive item set. The mining efficiency is affected by the count of conditional trees, as well as the expenses of creation and traversal. The production of a large number of conditional trees, which has a significant computational and memory consumption cost, is one of the speed bottlenecks.

Conclusion

We present a complete evaluation in this publication of the Data Perturbation Technique, Utility Data Mining, utility mining with Privacy Protection and Data Mining with Privacy Protection, Frequency Counting for Fast Perturbation, and Utilizing Tree and Table design with Rapid Perturbation. This work proposes Frequency Counting for Fast Perturbation, a quick technique for privacy protection. To cleanse the transaction database, it makes use of a selected list of sensitive items, various item set table formats, and a sophisticated perturbation technique. It turns out that Frequency Counting for the Fast Perturbation runtime outperforms Utilizing Tree and Table design with Rapid Perturbation and offers a straightforward and elegant method of altering a database to satisfy the privacy requirements of the data owner and uphold privacy standards. Table and multi-list structures are used by Frequency Counting for the Fast Perturbation for quick perturbation. Anonymization, data stream mining, and other fields can benefit from this work’s contributions.

Plant Disease Detection Using Stochastic Gradient Classifier With RBNN

K. P. Sreelakshmi,59

School of Computing Sciences, Vels Institute of Science, Technology and Advanced Studies (VISTAS) -Chennai, India

DOI: 10.1201/9781003430452-74

Abstract

A nation’s life is in its agriculture. Because of this, crops need to be protected from many diseases. No matter the cuisine, tomatoes may be found in a variety of forms, therefore, they were used as a sample crop for our research. Many different diseases cause tomatoes to lose quality. This paper presented a method for employing ML algorithms to predict and detect tomato plant leaf disease early. With the aid of various ML algorithms, they work systematically on a database and carry out various functions such as feature extraction, performing testing, etc. An estimated range of tomato leaf disease prediction performance is 67%–99%. This provides a solid framework for our ongoing study of the conception and creation of a novel method for the prognosis and early detection of tomato leaf disease.

Keywords: Plant Disease; Deep Learning; Early Prediction; Feature Extraction

Introduction

Many illnesses hinder plant growth in the fields, potentially drastically lowering the quality of the end product. Early leaf fall or disease-related leaf infection causes damage to cotton crops (Delnevo et al., 2021). To address issues like Maintainable Environmentalism, undesired elimination, and topsoil optimization, it is necessary to collect various agricultural data and conduct analysis to build manufacturing techniques (Ouhami et al., 2021).

Various AI techniques, including KNN, logistic regression, decision trees, SVM, and DCNN, are used to detect and classify plant diseases. These approaches were integrated with other picture pre-processing techniques to improve feature extraction. K-NN classifies the data using a similarity metric and is a straightforward memory-based classification technique (Li et al., 2021). Based on statistical learning, the ML method SVM was characterized by a dividing hyper-plane applied to regression and classification problem tasks based on statistical learning ideas (Garikapati et al., 2021).

Related Works

Deep Learning (DL) is an exceptionally well-liked technology since it produces accurate findings when taught on vast amounts of data (Latchoumi et al., 2019). DL’s significant benefits are its ability to automatically select the right features (Wani et al., 2022). Image processing was used to identify three illnesses in the corn crop. The results of an automatic SVM analysis of images performed in MATLAB are displayed before (Anand et al., 2021). The same methodology is employed by decision support systems for hydroponic farming to identify characteristics of plant leaves. It is being created into user-friendly software to employ image processing technologies to detect jute plant disease. In this study, the application will take pictures and upload them to the server (Saleem et al., 2019). The impacted area is identified on the server using hue-based segmentation. The R-CNN method incorporates a feature extractor to find regions of interest proposes. The area proposed were standardized (Saleem et al., 2019). To extract characteristics in area proposes, AlexNet was employed. Lastly, for the suitable dimensions of the standardized area propose, Support Vector Machine (SVM) was employed for categorization & regression analysis of the good coordinates of the standardized area proposals (Rehman et al., 2021). On the other hand, an R-CNN extracts feature for every potential region proposal individually and then repeats the same process for numerous area proposals, leading to many parameters. Furthermore, the properties of the outcomes have been influenced by the standardization of candidate region proposals (Jin et al., 2018). To solve these challenges, use a Region of Interest (Rol) layer based on the pyramid principle; the Faster R-CNN unifies the typical vector’s length of numerous region proposal recommendations. the Fast R-CNN only needs to compute the whole prior picture once, eliminating a substantial amount of recurring calculations (Prakash et al., 2022).

ML Algorithm

One of the strongest and most used categorizations and prediction algorithms is the decision tree

Proposed Workflow

The proposed ML techniques for categorizing various tomato leaf diseases are described in this section. Image acquisition, image preprocessing, and feature extraction are used to create a rich feature dataset. These features are afterward supplied to several classifiers to classify tomato leaf diseases. Figure 1 depicts the workflow.

Classification Analysis

A classifier with 1615 characteristics, 84 input neurons, and 19 output neurons was trained and evaluated using stochastic gradient descent to optimize the negative log-likelihood loss function. Accuracy for the first 15 qualities is 1, except for the brown spot. 40 instances had a classification error totaling 5.8565%, which is considered satisfactory. Pre-processing was used to improve image quality, with imported images being a 2D array of three colors. The first image was reduced to 128 x 128 pixels and underwent an RGB to HSV conversion.

The project utilizes preprocessed photos and employs a histogram system to improve classification accuracy by extracting features. The combined features are then passed on to classification after normalization and flattening into a 1D array. Image pre-processing and feature extraction are shown in Fig. 2, while a few examples from the dataset are displayed in Fig. 3.

Result of Model Training

The proposed system was evaluated using tomatoes, achieving a training accuracy of 99.54% using the Gradient descent algorithm with RBNN. Table 1 and Fig. 4 show the system’s name and accuracy, and comparison to an existing system respectively. Figure 4 enables selection of the best technique for different diseases.

Table 1 Performance Measures
S. No. Algorithm Name Accuracy ( %)
1 Logistic regression 87.02
2 Random Forest 81.99
3 Gradient descent boosting with RBNN algorithm 99.61
4 SVM algorithm 90.64
5 Decision tree 96.13

Conclusion

The article explores the advantages of using ML in agriculture, with algorithms developed to diagnose plant diseases using leaf area and feature extraction histograms. The Gradient descent boosting with the RBNN method achieved 99.54% accuracy, aiding farmers in preventing disease spread and improving crop quality.

Autonomous Assistance for Alzheimer's Patients

R. Julian Menezes,60

E-mail: julianmr@hindustanunic.ac.in; nithinkumar.c44@gmail.com; rishwanthpraveen@gmail.com; slakshmi@hindustanuniv.ac.in

DOI: 10.1201/9781003430452-75

Abstract

Alzheimer’s disease (Ad) is a disease that becomes more and more inhibiting of memory with a progressive course over time it also affects thinking and causes visual impairment. Visual impairment is a customary symptom of AD, and recent studies have shown that visual interventions may improve the functioning of AD patients. This paper aims to use image processing techniques to detect AD at an early stage using Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) of the brain. The proposed technique also includes camera-based detection for visually impaired or AD individuals to recognize text, objects, and known people in real-time using face recognition and sign language. Optical Character Recognition (OCR) method is used to transform pictures into text, and ML is used to detect known faces, objects, and sign language. The output will be expressed in the form of an audio stream with the help of text-to-speech.

Keywords: Face detection, Ocr, Sign detection, Tesseract, MRI, API, AD

Introduction

Visually impaired individuals face many challenges in their daily lives, including difficulties in reading printed text, recognizing faces, and identifying objects. Assistive technology has the prospective ability to alleviate challenges and enhance the standard of living for individuals with visual impairments. The number of people with near or distant vision impairments worldwide is estimated to be at least 2.2 billion. One billion or almost half - of these cases are yet to be treated for vision impairments. Recent advancements in OCR and face recognition technologies have made it possible to develop camera-based systems that can accurately recognize text, faces, and objects. However, these systems have not yet been fully explored for their potential to assist visually impaired individuals. Several studies have developed OCR and face recognition systems for the visually impaired, but these systems have limitations such as not being able to recognize text in real-time, and not being able to recognize faces and objects. We additionally add sign-to-speech as an additive functionality in the integrated system that will help other people understand the sign language being expressed by the affected

Evans et al. (2007) conducted a study in which 13900 individuals resulted showing that the presence of depression was rife between individuals who were visually impaired to those who are not visually impaired. This suggests that there may be a link between visual impairment and depression. Likely individuals with visual impairment may be to a greater extent prone to experiencing difficulties in functioning their daily lives. These difficulties can hurt an individual’s mental well-being, leading to depression which could lead to social isolation, which is another risk factor for depression. In conclusion, this research highlights the importance of recognizing the potential impact of visual impairment on mental health and the need for interventions that can help alleviate the burden of depression in this population.

Mashiata et al. (2022) conducted an all-inclusive sweeping review of the status quo and anticipated prospects of assistive technology catered to visually impaired individuals. The review aimed to provide an overview of the various assistive devices that are currently available, as well as their features and limitations. Various types of assistive devices are being used for visually impaired individuals, including capturing devices, working hours, response times, coverage areas, and feedback. The devices reviewed include those that use image processing, computer vision, and machine learning techniques to assist users with visual impairments. The review also discussed the features of the assistive devices, such as the type of sensors used, their working hours, response time, coverage area, and feedback mechanisms. The devices were also evaluated on their ability to assist users in different scenarios, such as indoor and outdoor environments. However, the review concluded that at the time of the review, there was no single device that met all the requirements for designing assistive technology for visually impaired individuals. In conclusion, the review highlights the need for continued research and development in assistive technology for visually impaired individuals to create devices that can meet the needs of all users. The review suggests that it is important to consider the trade-offs between different features when designing assistive technology for visually impaired individuals, in order to provide the best possible assistance to users in different scenarios. For this reason, we aim to provide a fully provisioned system for persons with visually impaired that will contain 5 modules which are MRI Alzheimer’s detection, OCR, Sign to Speech, Object detection, and face detection that will help the visually impaired to perform basic functions

Three pre-trained networks were shortlisted to detect Alzheimer’s in an MRI image VGG-16, Resnet50, SE Resnet50 of which Resnet seemed to be more accurate than the others Theckedath and Sedamkar (2020). The Haar cascade classifier is used due to its quick result, low computational costs, and reliability (Hyun et al., 2021). The Haar cascade for face detection then uses the LBPH (local binary pattern histogram) algorithm for face recognition due to its known performance and ability to recognize the face from the frontal, rear, or side view (Hwang et al., 2019). The sign-to-speech module will be carried out using a regular CNN with tuned pre-trained models (Ahmed et al., 2022). Pytesseract the wrapper for google ocr and Python will be used for the OCR module (Tafti et al., 2016; Hegghammer, 2022). Object detection is carried out using the Caffe model (Ikeda et al., 2019). The output is in the form of an audio stream which is converted with the help of GTTS (Google text to speech) Kaur and Singh (2022).

Related Works

In the field of assistive technology for the visually impaired, there have been several studies and projects related to camera-based text recognition and object identification that has ranged over a long period of time with significant developments. Martinek et al. (2019) presented an OCR system that can perform two crucial tasks: analyzing the layout of a page, including identifying text blocks and lines and recognizing text using OCR. Hyun et al., (2021) An architecture for face detection using a Haar classifier was proposed that aims to enhance the computational speed of the system. This is achieved by eliminating unnecessary iterations during the classification process hence increasing the processing speed by 4.46%, which can be beneficial for real-time applications such as security systems and video surveillance. Additionally, the use of Haar classifiers in this architecture is a conventional system for detecting faces in images, making it a reliable and robust solution (Wu and Zhang, 2021) an experiment with a 99.85 accuracy rate achieved by the improved facenet in the experiment which demonstrates the ability to effectively recognize faces in real-time. A face detection and recognition system that uses this technology can detect and recognize faces with high accuracy.

Sustainability is a key concern in face detection systems, as they often rely on small processing units.

Holanda et al., (2018) proposed a reading system was proposed that utilizes a portable device and combines ML techniques, segmentation, and feature extraction to achieve an accuracy of 99.86% and a specificity of 99.3%. The system integrates a central moments extractor with a multi-layer perceptron.

Wang et al., (2022) 400 training images and 100 gaze attention maps were classified using a classification algorithm that has Resnet 50 as a backbone. The first initial epochs don’t show considerable improvement but after 10 epochs there was significant improvement Resnet 50 proved to be a conventional system to classify medical images.

Proposed Methodology

Our objective is to develop a Dual Aid system that comprises two main components: the Doctor’s Aid and the Patient’s Aid. The Doctor’s Aid module is designed to offer doctors a preliminary understanding and a starting point for analyzing MRI scans of patients with Alzheimer’s disease. This model can be deployed on a server to provide local access within the hospital’s network. Considering that visual impairment is a common symptom of Alzheimer’s disease, the Patient’s Aid is divided into four sub-modules that can help patients with Alzheimer’s perform basic activities. These sub-modules include face detection for identifying family members, object detection for recognizing common objects in the environment, OCR for reading large print signs, and sign-to-speech, which allows patients who communicate via sign language to converse directly with their doctors.

Doctors Aid

We propose an ensemble method that concatenates Resnet 50 and Xception that will perform a multiclass classification of four categories of MRI images, namely Mild Demented, Moderate Demented, Very Mild Demented, and Non-Demented.

Resnet50 and Xception

The reason for choosing this approach is that ResNet50 and Xception have complementary strengths - ResNet50 is proficient at capturing long-range dependencies, while Xception excels at capturing local features. Since the details in MRI images are often subtle, combining both these architectures allowed us to capture both local and global features accurately. We selected ResNet50 for its complexity, having 50 layers, which makes it more effective at capturing complex patterns present in MRI images, crucial for dementia classification. Furthermore, ResNet50 is a conventional backbone algorithm for classifying medical images, making it a preferred choice. We leveraged the pre-trained weights of ResNet50 from ImageNet dataset to bring prior knowledge to the task of dementia classification. Similarly, Xception, known to work well with ImageNet weights, was combined with ResNet50. The availability of a wide range of resources for both ResNet50 and Xception made it feasible to use them together to form an Ensemble method. Resnet 50 is an adaptation of the Resnet model having 50 layers which consist of 48 convolutional layers with 1 Average pool and 1 Max pool layer. Furthermore, Xception uses skip or residual connections to facilitate the flow of information from earlier layers to later layers, allowing the network to preserve significant information throughout the training process. This is accomplished by adding shortcut connections between the layers of the network, allowing for direct communication between them.

Patients Aid

The primary module of the patient’s aid is the face detection module where the Haar cascade classifier is used due to its quick result, low computational costs, and reliability. The Haar cascade for face detection then uses the LBPH (local binary pattern histogram) algorithm for face recognition due to its known performance and ability to recognize the face from the frontal, rear or side view. Optical character recognition also known as OCR will be carried out by pytesseract that will help the patients read big signs. For object detection we are using the Caffe model that can detect multiple objects in a screen Sign to speech will be carried out with a Pretrained CNN Sequential model. These algorithms have been selected upon extensive literature survey so that the selected algorithms work properly in all conditions where speed or accuracy is not compromised for reliance.

Simulation and Analysis

We performed simulations to investigate the behavior of different algorithms with different optimizers. We experimented with several algorithms and optimizers, and after analyzing the results, we shortlisted two algorithms: Xception and Resnet 50. Xception is a variant of the Inception network, while Resnet 50 is a variant of the Resnet network. Furthermore, we shortlisted three known optimizers for these algorithms: Stochastic Gradient Descent (SGD) optimizer, Adaptive Moment Estimation (Adam) optimizer, and Root Mean Square Propagation (Rrnsprop) optimizer. These optimizers are widely used in deep learning for optimizing the parameters of neural networks. The shortlisting process was based on the performance of the algorithms with the different optimizers, computational efficiency, or other relevant factors. The shortlisted algorithms and optimizers were hence chosen to be further analyzed and compared to determine the best combination for a specific task.

As observed for the given dataset Resnet 50 performed better with the Sgd optimizer giving us a more stable test accuracy and also higher highs and less lower lows as compared to Adam optimizer. Similar observations were observed for Xception paired with Sgd and Adams optimizers It was additionally noticed that Xception wasn’t able to get trained effectively during initial epochs and there was an accuracy drop of around 10-12% in the testing accuracy. Resnet 50 and Xception concatenated with SGD optimizer performs with increased stability through the epochs. Extra Augmented data was added to the ensemble model. All the simulations were carried out for 10 epochs with a learning rate of 0.001. Rms prop doesn’t seem to be a competent optimizer for this ensemble method as we can see there is a difference of about 15 % and fluctuation in the test accuracy.

Fig. 2. Accuracy Table
Train Acc Val Acc Precision Recal. Auc
ResNet50 0.990190 0.933090 0.908413 0.882286 0.986544
Xception 0.952190 4.965220 0.954467 0.954286 0.996430
Ensemble 0.997197 0.999834 0.997212 0.997136 0.999954

The ensemble method had 10 % better training accuracy than Resnet50 individually and 4 % better training accuracy than Xception individually. The validation accuracies were also better by 6 % and 3% respectively for Resnet50 and Xception models.

The Patient’s Aid module was able to perform the respective functions during testing which was run on a simulative software that had 5 buttons that have different functions

Conclusion

In conclusion, an effective framework has been built for a multiclass classification where an ensemble method of concatenating the Xcpetion and Resnet 50 algorithm paired with the Sgd optimizer has proved to be a viable method to classify the available MRI axial cut images. However, we need to extend the functionality of this framework to include the coronal and sagittal brain slices and add other data modalities such as FDG-Positron Emission Tomography (PET), FDG-Positron Emission Tomography (PET), Structural Magnetic resonance Imaging (SMRI), Computer Tomography (CT) and Functional Magnetic Resonance (Fmri). The face detection module, Sign to speech, object detection, and OCR module are good solutions that can help the visually impaired to do basic functionalities which were achieved in a simulative process

Result and Discussion

With the field-sent sensor hub, the sensors’ information is accumulated hourly for 37 straight days. The analysis takes into account the minimum amount of soil moisture for the day and daily averages of air temperature, humidity, UV radiation, and soil temperature. The data also comes from a weather forecasting website that is used to predict soil moisture levels for the coming days.

The data are sent to the local host computer via a web service. The newly received data is then analyzed using the machine learning algorithms that were discussed earlier. Scikit-learn, Pandas, and Matplotlib, all Python-based analysis tools, are utilized.

The forecast of a field’s soil moisture over the next few days can help with planning and provisioning for appropriate irrigation, as previously stated. Learning about the environmental conditions and factors (such as temperature, humidity, and UV) for the upcoming day can be made easier with the help of online weather forecast information. Prediction models based on machine learning can be made from the sensor data that has been collected over time. These models can be used to estimate soil moisture for the next day based on the weather and environment that is expected.

This study discusses two approaches for predicting soil moisture. In the first method, in addition to the other weather-projection characteristics (air temperature, humidity, and UV), the anticipated soil temperature is used to predict the subsequent days’ soil moisture. The soil temperature is ignored by the second method for predicting soil moisture.

In Table 1, the RMSE of the applicable machine learning approaches are compared to determine their accuracy. The results demonstrate that when temperature is one of the parameters used to estimate soil moisture, the GBRT performs better.

Table 1. Comparison of the performance of predicted soil moistures using GBRT with and without taking into account soil temperature as a prediction parameter (based on r squared and MSE)
Parameter Predicted Soil Moisture considering soil temperature Predicted Soil Moisture not considering soil temperature
Mean squared Error 4.05 5.79
Accuracy (Rquared) 0.95 0.95

In Table 2, the RMSE of the employed machine learning approaches are compared to determine their accuracy. The outcomes demonstrate that the GBRT outperforms the RFR and ENR.

Table 2. ENR, GBRT, and RFR comparison of the r squared and mean-squared errors of anticipated soil moisture
Parameter Predicted soil moisture using GBRT Predicted soil moisture RFR Predicted soil moisture using ENR
Mean square Error 4.03 19.25 40.50

Research Methodology

Predictive models developed may be adapted for both agricultural irrigation and urbanized areas. The creation of a smart irrigation system changes a farmer’s life. This study presents an intelligent irrigation architecture based on For anticipating moisture content, a hybrid technique based on IoT and artificial training is used. Since soil moisture is a key factor in determining how much water should be utilized for irrigation, ML approaches are used to estimate soil moisture for the following days using data from field sensors and weather forecasts. When the results of several ML approaches are analyzed, the findings of the GBRT-based approach are highly positive. In many water-stressed countries like India, such techniques might help to maximize the use of irreplaceable fresh water supplies for agriculture.
