Mitigation of Threats in Cloud Using Ensemble Hybrid Machine Learning

S. Divya62

DOI: 10.1201/9781003430452-77

Abstract

Researchers have utilized a broad variety of machine learning techniques throughout the past few years in order to identify network attacks without having extensive prior knowledge about the characteristics of these attacks. Due to the complexity of the model, however, traditional machine learning methods are unable to generate one-of-a-kind feature descriptors. Consequently, this limitation applies to the entire field. The difficulty in characterizing the attack detection challenge is directly correlated to this fact. In this paper, various supervised deep learning models are combined to form an ensemble framework to detect and mitigate the attacks in cloud. The supervised deep learning models include generative adversarial networks, autoencoders, convolutional neural network, and recurrent neural network. These unsupervised ensemble models act as a base classifier and the output is obtained from the meta classifier to classify the attacks. The results of simulation show’s that the proposed method has higher rate of classification accuracy than the existing ensemble models.

Keywords: Threats Mitigation, Cloud, Machine Learning

Introduction

The benefits drawn from a wide range of sources are made available to a large number of users of networked computers thanks to the continuous growth and widespread acceptance of the Internet. On the other hand, as the number of people who are dependent on the networks continues to climb, the importance of taking precautions to keep them secure will only become more pressing. The goal of network security is to prevent unauthorized users from gaining access to resources like computers, networks, programs, data, and so on and making modifications to them (Ahsan et al., 2022).

However, when more and more systems related to finance, e-commerce, and the military go online, they become easier targets for network attacks, which puts them in great danger and exposes them to catastrophic damage. This places them in a position where they could be severely damaged (Berghout et al., 2022). It is vital to have effective tactics for identifying threats, repelling them, and preserving the safety of networks. Additionally, it is essential to have such strategies. An extra layer of complexity arises from the fact that various forms of attack typically call for a variety of responses. Therefore, figuring out how to recognize new and previously unknown forms of network attack is the most important task facing those who work in the field of network security (Singh et al., 2021).

Deep learning approaches, so-called because of the general design of deep layers used to tackle complex problems, represent a major development in the capacity of machine learning to mimic the structure of the human brain with the architecture of neural networks. Deep learning approaches are so-called because of the general design of deep layers used to tackle complex problems (Daghigh et al., 2021). The general design of the deep learning algorithms that are used to tackle complex issues is where the term deep learning derives from. One of the most notable initiatives for the game of Go to use the capabilities of a common deep-learning structure (Unal et al., 2022).

The objective is to give academics interested in applying deep learning methods to the study of network security a fundamental understanding of deep learning so they can get started. A substantial amount of work has been done that, in essence, focuses on the application of deep learning approaches to detect attacks. The term “deep learning techniques” refers to this Gupta et al. (2022).

Our research is based on the conclusions of several prior literature evaluations (Sharma and Singh, 2022; Alsoufi et al., 2021; Arul et al., 2021; Gheibi et al., 2021) that look into the potential of deep learning to address the problem of attack detection. These evaluations look into the possibility of using deep learning to the problem of attack detection. These reviews look into the several applications that deep learning could have.

With the support of IoT security approaches that have been trained with deep learning, we are able to obtain a clear understanding of how various hacks are carried out and how to defend against them. A method that detects breaches by utilizing deep learning and analyzing the similarities and differences across four very big data sets.

In order to accomplish the goal of explaining the deep learning algorithms and the applications to which they are most suited, this step was taken. This one, in particular, focuses on the specifics of attack detection, such as malware analysis, spam detection, and intrusion detection, amongst other issues that are linked to attack detection. In contrast to broader, more comprehensive overviews, this one is more focused.

In this paper, we develop a supervised machine learning framework that enables better detection of issues and threats in cloud computing services. The supervised machine learning framework uses an ensemble framework to detect the issues and threats for detection and mitigation in cloud.

Related Works

Convolutional neural networks have been the focus of a great deal of intriguing studies and applications in recent years, notably in the area of network security (Sun et al., 2022). The authors employ recursive and convolutional network layers to build a neural network that can mimic a malware detection system. This work is meant to lead to the acquisition of classification qualities. The method suggested combines two different types of feature extraction approaches to produce a hierarchical feature extraction architecture: the convolutional operation in the convolutional layer and the sequence modeling in the recursive network layer. The most desirable features of the two different styles of are combined in this architecture.

The input for their network is the original short strings, and it extracts features to classify the strings using character-level embeddings. The eXpose neural network (XNN) is a method that the authors in Aziz et al. (2022) present as a mechanism for identifying attack signals in advance. When compared to methods that serve as baselines and are based on the manual extraction of features, the design of eXpose self-extracted features emerges as the undeniable victor. It is stated that the wide diversity and high level of complexity of their initial inputs make algorithm processing difficult. In spite of this, it reduces the false alarm rate in contrast to these baselines, which suggests that the automatic feature extraction process in CNN is not robust enough and not fair enough without the addition of additional or even noisy input.

It is extremely necessary to have the ability to identify malicious web shells in order to guarantee the network continuing safety. The authors in Sayadi et al. (2021) provide a word2vec format as well as a CNN-based hazardous detection method for the analysis of HTTP request data. Because this is the very first time that word2vec and CNN have been attempted to be integrated in the context of malicious detection, this body of work carries a great deal of significance. They begin by discussing the word2vec software, which is distinguished by the fact that it makes use of feature representations of HTTP-obtained words. The web request is then characterized as a matrix of a size that has been calculated in advance by using the features that have been strung together. A model has been eventually built for the classification of shells, and it makes use of a CNN framework. Although many various kinds of experiments are carried out, the suggested method outperforms the relevant conventional classifiers in every single set of tests that are carried out.

A classification approach for end-to-end encrypted communication that is based on a one-dimensional convolutional neural network (CNN) is described in Qazi et al. (2022). This approach unifies the processes of feature extraction, feature selection, and classifier application under a single framework with the intention of attaining robust performance in attack detection using the CNN architecture. Additionally, it shows how the authors intend to employ 1D-CNN as the learning algorithm for the network. This enables the network to automatically learn the association between automatically extracted features and outputs that are associated with anticipated labels. This is made possible by the fact that the network is given this information.

An AE and DNN based hybrid deep learning technique was employed in Khan (2021) to identify malicious code. To be more specific, they make use of AE in order to move their emphasis from the excessive detail that was contained in the initial data to the most important components of the data. This is accomplished by shifting their focus from excessive information to the most crucial components of the data. Using a DBN- based learning model that includes multilayer RBM and a layer of BPNN in order to find the malicious code is the next step in the process. This step is necessary in order to move on to the next stage of the process. They were able to fine-tune the entire network to build the most effective hybrid model once they found out that each RBM layer had been trained unsupervised and that each BP layer had been trained supervised. This information allowed them to develop the most accurate results possible. We were able to achieve this by providing each BP layer with supervised instruction. Experiments have shown that their hybrid network is superior to DBN-based networks in terms of its ability to accurately detect threats. These DBN-based networks were previously employed.

The authors in Tran et al. (2022) outline an innovative technique for analyzing traffic that is centered around CNN. A two-dimensional representation of the data on network traffic is presented by this method. These researchers demonstrated their findings by utilizing the dataset provided by the USTC-TRC2016 flow competition. Specifically, they used it to show that their method achieves an average classification accuracy of 99%.

The authors in Hou et al. (2021) use an ensemble network to categorize the many forms of attack that have been documented. To be more specific, the neural network learns the knowledge necessary to classify things by applying a collection of classifiers. These classifiers help the neural network obtain the knowledge it needs to classify things. After that, it compiles the results of all of these classifiers into a single set in order to make accurate predictions. In order to increase performance when differentiating regular behaviors from abnormal ones, the technique that is being suggested incorporates not just an AE but also a BNN, a DNN, and an extreme learning machine. It has been demonstrated that the performance of employing a multitude of classifiers for the detection task is superior to the performance of employing just one classifier for the task. The results of their suggested ensemble technique are exciting in the right direction.

An ensemble structure is presented in Omer et al. (2021) as a technique of strengthening the stability of neural networks for the detection of malware. This is accomplished through the use of many networks working together. This structure is based on the principle that superior results can be achieved by integrating a large number of different classification methods. During the training phase, a collection of neural networks is built, and the individual classifiers are responsible for the maintenance and upkeep of their own statistics. This may involve the conversion of input data as well as the preservation of semantic context. A vote is taken from a range of classifiers to determine which samples will be labeled during the testing phase of the project. When applied to the task of finding a solution to the problem provided by the AICS 2019, their proposed ensemble structure demonstrates great levels of both accuracy and recall.

Proper Method

The output of the meta-classifier offers attack mitigation, in addition to the improved detection ability offered by the ensemble architecture base classifier. Datasets Processing

Data preprocessing involves the elimination of redundant information and data normalization.

Feature Selection

The CFS that is discussed in this research has the potential to not only improve the selection of features but also the precision with which they are classified. This method examines the selected subset of features to determine how relevant and redundant they are in relation to the search space that has been provided. This assists in locating the most optimal solution feasible.

Correlation-Based Feature Selection

Correlation-based feature selection refers to the algorithms that choose features based on evaluations that are based on correlations. These algorithms are also sometimes referred to as CFS algorithms. Repeating characteristics, on the other hand, are chosen for inclusion because they are linked to a number of other characteristics in the same category.

This method prioritizes subsets whose characteristics are strongly related to the class while being relatively unrelated to the characteristics of other subsets. In order for a feature to be included, it must be able to make predictions about classes that cannot be made using any other features that are already accessible in the instance space. The following is an illustration of one function that may be utilized to compare the characteristics of CFS subgroups:


$$M_{s} = \frac{kr_{cf}}{\sqrt{k + k(k - 1) + r_{f}}}$$

On the basis of the equation presented above, we are able to draw certain inferences regarding the following three variables:

Ms - feature subset evaluation,

rcf - mean correlation degree between

rf - average inter-correlation degree between.

The value of the CFS is determined by analyzing the correlations that exist between its various subsets of attributes. Finding the feature set that has the highest value rcf enables a large reduction rf in the overall size of the datasets that are used for training and testing purposes. This is possible because of finding the feature set that has the greatest value.

Ensemble Classification

The ensemble model consists of both supervised and unsupervised classifiers as illustrated in Fig. 2.

Unsupervised Autoencoder

AE design can be broken down into three main parts: In point of fact, it is able to begin by condensing the input into a representation in feature space, and then it is able to recreate that representation in the output after it has been compressed. Since AE is illustrative of a widespread category of learning methods, it has found widespread application in a variety of data analysis tasks, including the reduction in the number of dimensions in a dataset and the identification of outliers. It has also found widespread application in the field of artificial intelligence (AI). When it comes to cybersecurity, AE is also frequently used to describe unusual behaviors within its limited feature space. This is done within the context of the limited feature space. This method also has the advantage of being able to depict dynamic attacks that don’t fall into categories that are known in advance. The gradient is represented as:


∇ = y(t) − x(t)

Belife Network

One can classify deep belief networks into two groups: those that use backpropagation neural networks (BPNN or BP) with a single layer and restricted Boltzmann machines (RBM) with many layers of unsupervised learning networks. These two kinds of networks both train their models using constrained Boltzmann machines (DBN). The open and hidden layers of neurons make up this neural network, which is structured as an undirected graph model.

A neural network whose generation structure is selected at random is known as a random bit machine. Training that is done on a layer-by-layer basis is beneficial for DBN because it makes use of the components that are inherent to RBM. The distribution of DBN is represented as below:


J(θk + 1) = J(θk) + αk∇J(θk)dk + o(θk)

DBN was utilized by the researchers in this investigation in order to identify malicious software. The researchers trained a multilayer generative model using unsupervised learning in order to counteract the tendency of DBNs toward overfitting

Unsupervised Generative Adversarial Network

One of the most promising unsupervised learning systems that has been proposed in recent years is called the generative adversarial network (GAN). This system makes use of the property of finding intrinsic patterns in data in order to develop new examples, and it is one of the systems that has been suggested in recent years. The concept of a game in which there is neither a winner nor a loser was a significant motivation for the development of GAN. It plays a never-ending game within the setting of a deep neural network called who will generate and who will discriminate, which is necessary for it to get to the stage where it can learn a distributed representation of real-world data.

This is essential for it to get to the point where it can learn a distributed representation of real-world data. On the other hand, the objective is to ascertain whether or not a particular data set is the product of genuine data by simulating, modeling, and learning the distributional characteristics of real data. These two objectives are opposed to the objective of the task, which is to establish whether or not a particular data set is the product of actual data collection. Both their capacity for production and their capacity to differentiate between different objects can benefit from the ongoing rivalry between these internal models.

Supervised Cnn

The convolutional computation and the depth structure that they use make convolutional neural networks, more commonly referred to as CNNs, a technology that is emblematic of deep learning and is used extensively in this field. CNNs are also referred to by their more common name, convolutional neural networks. In particular, CNN makes advantage of a multilayer perception variant design, which calls for the user to perform essentially no preprocessing at all.

In addition to the input and output layers, convolutional neural networks (CNNs) contain a number of other levels that are not visible to the user. The convolution layer, the pooling layer, and the complete connection layer are all components of these layers. CNN has a number of benefits that other categorization systems do not possess. To make features, it does not require any prior information and does not require as much preprocessing as other methods do. These are two of the most essential benefits.

Supervised Recurrent Neutral Network

RNNs are a special kind of neural network structure that is endowed with a memory function in order to store information that was acquired in the past. This function was developed solely to be utilized with input that varies over the course of time. RNNs are particularly well suited for application with this kind of data. This choice in design is consistent with the hypothesis that human cognition is based on previous experience and memory. This hypothesis helps to explain why RNN performs so well when it is presented with time-series data.

RNNs still face substantial fundamental design issues, such as gradient disappearance and gradient explosion, which prevent them from remembering or modeling long-term relationships. This is one of the reasons why RNNs are not widely used. The first of these issues is referred to as gradient vanishing, and the second of these issues is referred to as gradient explosion. As a result of this, researchers have developed LSTM and GRU with gates and memory cells. Both of these types of networks are able to recall long-term relationships by successfully navigating essential elements of the flow of information.

Results and Discussions

The proposed method is evaluated over various other methods that include ensemble supervised and unsupervised model. The model is evaluated in python environment to test the efficacy of the model against various attacks like Denial-of-Service Attack (DoS), User to Root Attack (U2R) and Remote to Local Attack (R2L). the dataset used for the study includes NSL-KDD, KDDCup 99, and DARPA1998. The results are tested in terms of its accuracy, false positive rate, true positive rate, and area under region of curve. The results are illustrated in the following figures.

The results of the simulation show that the proposed method achieves higher accuracy (Fig. 3), false positive rate (Fig. 4), true positive rate (Fig. 5) and area under region of curve (Fig. 6). It is seen that with increasing test samples, the unsupervised classifier performs best than the supervised learning classifier.

Conclusions

In this paper, the ensemble architecture allows us to utilize supervised machine learning methods for improved problem and threat detection in cloud computing services. Using a supervised machine learning framework, vulnerabilities and risks in the cloud can be discovered and mitigated by employing an ensemble architecture. Using the meta-classifier output from the ensemble base classifier can help reduce the impact of attacks. The resilience of the model against different types of attacks is examined through the simulation. Simulations show that the proposed solution is superior to the status quo in terms of problem detection and assault prevention.

Detection of Insects, Birds, and Wild Animals in Farming Land Using Regional Convolutional Neural Network

Mrs. N. Rajeswari,63

E-mail: csrajee2007@gmail.com; kavithad.mca@spiher.ac.in

DOI: 10.1201/9781003430452-78

Abstract

In this paper, we aim to find the objects that create disturbances for farming in its area and this includes insects, birds, and wild animals. The suggested technique is created such that it facilitates the detection of these things and it performs theft monitoring in the farming area. This research work would involve a sensor used to detect obstacles like an animal or bird, temperature, and humidity of the farming area, and the information will pass to the mobile application using IoT. Obstacle detection can be proposed with the help Regional Convolution Neural Network.

Keywords: Detection, Farming Land, Wild Animals, Regional Convolutional Neural Network

Introduction

The first people to domesticate land and raise crops marked a significant turning point in the development of human history. Farming practices have been subjected to a considerable evolution over the past century because of improvements in agricultural technology and the expansion of global agricultural markets (Ramos et al., 2022).

These days, one of the most essential things for a farm to undertake is to take precautions to protect both its agricultural products and its livestock. Wild animals are responsible for a significant amount of the agricultural crop loss that occurs across most of India (Petrović et al., 2022).

The amount of food that can be gathered will drastically decrease because of animal interference on land used for agriculture. Because of this, a great number of farmers will experience huge financial losses. During field research, it was shown that wild animals were responsible for the loss of an average of 36% of the crop. As a possible solution to this issue, we suggest the creation of a robotic system that would prevent wild animals from entering farms (Faruque et al., 2022).

To overcome this issue, it is necessary to develop a region-based deep learning model that should detect the obstacles in the farming landscape (Naveen et al., 2022).

In this paper, the objects like insects, birds, or wild animals are detected using Regional Convolution Neural Network. The proposed method enables the detection of objects and it performs theft monitoring in the farming area. This research work would involve a sensor used to detect obstacles like animals or birds, temperature, and humidity of the farming area, and the information will pass to the mobile application using IoT.

Regional Convolutional Neural Network

With R-CNN, we can locate localized areas that provoke specific emotions. The defined local regions contain not just items and/or sections of objects, but also contexts that have been specially specified for those objects. In other words, defined local regions are a combination of the two.

The region proposal network, a neural network implementation, is created by combining all three of these processes into a single architecture. The construction of candidate boxes, the extraction of features, and the classification of the features that were extracted are the steps that make up these steps.

The RPN can complete the training in its entirety as well as the detection procedure in its whole. The RPN can process images of any size and generate a list of potential candidate boxes. The degree to which a candidate box matches the target box will be considered when determining a score for that box competition.

The output convolutional feature map from the previous layer is available to both the large and the small networks, but only the small network may slide over it. A low-dimensional vector is produced as the output of the sliding-window layer. This vector is then fed into two layers that are connected and have levels that are like one another. To carry out regression and classification, these layers make use of a rectangular frame.

Faster R-CNN proposes a novel approach to anchoring, according to their findings. At each position along the sliding window, Fig. 2. offers a graphical illustration of how the rectangular frame regression layer generates 4k outputs, also known as the coordinate values of K boxes. The classification layer for rectangular frames contains a total of 2k outputs that are ready for usage.

The placement of the center of the sliding window that is currently active is determined by the geometric center that lies at the k box (x1, y1, x2, y2). Even when employing three distinct sizes and three different ratios, For each possible point in the sliding window, k = 9 anchors are still employed, same like in faster R-CNN. This is the case even when k = 9 anchors are being used.

Convergence Feature Sharing

The RPN network and the Fast R-CNN network can be trained jointly rather than separately thanks to a recently developed piece of technology from the Faster R-CNN system. This is made possible by the RPN network. The flexibility to switch back and forth between two distinct optimization strategies is the engine that powers this four-stage method.

  1. Step 1 A pre-trained model is used during the first stage of the process to create initial values for the network parameters, and the RPN network is then subjected to fine-tuning.
  2. Step 2 In the second stage of the process, the initialized RPN network is used to extract the suggested region for training the Fast R-CNN network. The RPN network is utilized in this stage.
  3. Step 3 Re-initialize the RPN utilizing the Fast R-CNN N/W that was built in Step 2 with the main goal of optimizing the RPN unique layer.
  4. Step 4 Modify to the settings for the convolutional layer.
  5. Step 5 The fifth and final stage consists of applying the RPN extracted region proposal to the Fast R-CNN to make any necessary improvements.

Non-Maximum Suppression

It is possible to measure the degree to which two rectangular boxes overlap one another by utilizing a ratio known as the intersection-over-union (IoU) ratio. This ratio may be found in the below equation

(18)
IoU(A, B) = (A∩B)/(A∪B)

A technique known as non-maximum suppression (NMS), after locating the highest possible values, hides them all by a predetermined standard operating procedure. To get rid of unnecessary windows, the NMS is usually utilized in the process of target detection.

The study collects images from various farming land and a total of 500 images are collected. A total of 400 images are used for training the classifier and the remaining images are used for testing the classifier. The system is set up with the primary memory of 16GB RAM operating on Intel i5 processors of the 10th version.

The proposed method is compared with conventional animal detection methods like convolutional neural network (CNN), AlexNet model, and DenseNet model.

The comparison between the proposed RCNN and current techniques like CNN, AlexNet, and DenseNet is shown in Figs. 3, 4, 5 and 6 in terms of accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, and f-measure. The f-measure results demonstrate that the suggested RCNN offers better outcomes than techniques like CNN, AlexNet, and DenseNet.

Conclusions

The proposed system is built in a way that makes it possible to spot these Insects, birds, and other wild animals in the agricultural region. A sensor is utilized to monitor environmental factors like temperature and humidity in the farming area and then relay that data to a mobile application through the IoT. However, it is of minor concern in this work. With the use of a regional convolution neural network, a solution to the problem of obstacle detection is proposed.

A Trifold Authentication Using Elliptical Cryptography in Cloud Computing

K. Komathi64

DOI: 10.1201/9781003430452-79

Abstract

Processing in the cloud and storing data in the cloud are gaining a growing number of users as a direct result of developments in networking technology and the continuously rising demand for more computing power and storage space. In other words, the demand for more computing power and storage space is driving the adoption of cloud computing. Recent attacks have shown that personal information can be disclosed, computing tasks can be maliciously altered and cloud services can be disabled for users. In this paper, we develop a trifold authentication scheme to secure the data via proper authentication in cloud. This model uses hash chains to achieve the above aim. The simulation is conducted to test the efficacy of the authentication in cloud. The results show that the proposed method has a reduced rate of complexity than the existing methods.

Keywords: Cloud, Authentication, Elliptical curve cryptography

Introduction

Through the usage of cloud computing, consumers and organizations are liberated from the obligations of data storage and computation that have historically been their responsibility (Tiwari and Gangadharan, 2021). Users and organizations alike are now able to store data and carry out computations on computers located in remote locations thanks to the advent of cloud computing (Anuradha et al., 2021).

Users that sign up for the public cloud get access to the platform that is provided by the cloud service provider once they have completed the registration process. Users can save information in the cloud, which may later be accessed by other users and shared. Because it is stored in the cloud, your data is accessible whenever you need it and from any location you choose (AlAhmad et al., 2021).

Cloud storage has a lot of advantages, but it also has a lot of drawbacks because of the open nature of the platform and the absence of any security measures. Cloud storage is vulnerable to a wide variety of threats (Rangwani and Om, 2021). Many of the items that we save in the cloud, such as our profiles on various social networking platforms and our medical records, could be considered to be information that is either secret or private. It is of the utmost importance to make certain that these data are kept private and that implementation of safe data exchange is carried out (Safkhani et al., 2021).

Because the vast majority of cloud service providers have not yet installed necessary security controls, user data is freely viewable and can be accessed in a variety of ways. In order to achieve their goal of increasing revenues, they will even resort to utilizing the personal information of users. In addition to this, the attacker has the capability of accessing and stealing the private information of users that have been saved in the cloud (Fatima and Ahmad, 2021; Olakanmi and Odeyemi, 2021; Padmaj a and Seshadri, 2021).

The privacy of their information that has been outsourced must be protected at all times. Users also have the choice of making their information accessible to friends or to the person who initially launched the inquiry into the information. It is essential to have an access control system that is not only reliable but also adaptable. In this paper, we develop a trifold authentication scheme to secure the data via proper authentication in cloud.

Related works

Wang et al. (2009) advocated that cryptography should be used to enable changeable access control by encrypting each data block with a unique key. They did this by using cryptography. Cryptography was utilized in order to complete this task. In this approach, symmetric cryptography employing the shared secret key is applied, which enables the supply of mutual authentication.

When it comes to cloud computing, data privacy, and security are two of the most important concerns. Chen and Zhao (2012) carried out an in-depth analysis of these issues over the whole of the data life cycle, analyzed the effectiveness of various potential solutions, and outlined potential avenues for further research. The safety of storing data on the cloud and collaborating on that data is the primary topic of investigation in this study. The following is a synopsis of a few relevant research, with the primary attention being placed on the application of symmetric encryption, identity-based encryption, and attribute-based encryption in cloud storage systems.

However, because this method depends on the data owner delivering the paired keys to both the service provider and the end users, it takes a considerable amount of storage space. It is now possible to encrypt and decrypt user private information that is saved in the cloud thanks to a solution that was released by Ramesh et al. (2017) and is based on the secure e-stream cipher ChaCha20. This makes it possible for user information to be protected from prying eyes.

Li et al. (2009) presented a novel strategy for the authentication of cloud computing that was founded on the identity-based hierarchical architecture (IHA). This strategy was revolutionary because it took advantage of the benefits offered by cloud computing. Interdomain identity-based proxy re-encryption is a method that was developed by Tang et al. (2008) to securely transfer sensitive information between users who are located in different domains.

Wang et al. (2009) introduced a revolutionary IBPRE+ intending to make it easier and more secure for users of social cloud environments to share information. The method makes use of a delegator to generate re-encryption keys, which can be less taxing on the computer resources of the person who owns the data.

Tang et al. (2008) established the collusion attack against Tang approach, and they proposed a different method of data storage based on identities that is resistant to collusion attacks and can handle both local and remote inquiries. This method of data storage is based on identities. This type of data storage makes use of identities, and it is capable of responding to inquiries made both locally and remotely.

Ruj et al. (2012) presented a method for authenticated access control that is decentralized and intended for use with cloud storage. This technique does not necessitate the knowledge of user identities to carry out authentication, which means that the privacy of users is preserved. Later, they presented a new anonymous authentication system for cloud storage that was a decentralized access control mechanism. The data were encrypted utilizing an approach known as attribute-based encryption (ABE), and authentication was carried out utilizing an approach known as attribute- based signature (ABS), both of which are detailed in Maji et al. (2008).

Proposed Method

Each server in a single-server system must be registered by a mobile user in order for the latter to access the services. The mobile user has to keep several SCs and credentials after being registered on multiple SSS servers, which may be annoying for a mobile user.

Non-centralized design increases the risk of intruders, which has an impact on the whole routing process. In current cloud security measures, malicious nodes are removed from the network in order to prevent intrusions. As a result of these rogue nodes, the network as a whole suffers from severe packet loss, which exacerbates the problem of congestion.

Figure 1 provides an overview of our data storage platform that is hosted in the cloud at a high level. The semi-trusted third party (STTP), cloud storage servers, data owners, and requesters are the four different entities that make up the model. The STTP is responsible for the oversight of the users and servers that make up the cloud storage service and is responsible for supervising them. A user cipher text is saved and backed up on servers that are part of a cloud storage service. This ensures that the user data is secure as illustrated in Fig. 1.

The owner of the data stores encrypted copies of the data on servers that are located in other locations. This reduces the burden that is imposed on the local storage while simultaneously easing the process of accessing the data and enabling the data to be shared at any time and from any location. Those who send in requests do so intending to expose additional people to the material that is kept in the cloud.

A user management center, a key management center, and a data processing center are the three fundamental components that make up the STTP. The user management center is the most crucial of these three components. The User Management Center is the organization that is in charge of resolving any issues that may arise if a current user is deleted or a new user is registered.

The user list (UL) and the revocation list (RL) in the cloud storage system are regularly kept up to date by the system with the most recent list of allowed users and the public keys associated with their accounts. These lists are referred to as user lists and revocation lists, respectively. It is the responsibility of the key management hub to generate a partial private key for each unique user. The plaintext version of the cipher is stored on the servers that are used to store data in the cloud. These servers can provide the ciphertext to the data processing center when it is requested.

Only the STTP is given direct authorization to access the cloud storage servers in our cloud storage model, which keeps the servers secure and prevents unauthorized users from accessing their data. A cloud storage platform will often have its servers dispersed across a number of distinct physical locations.

Conclusions

In this paper, a reliable protocol that can be used for cloud-based authentication systems is developed. The proposed technique includes the following stages: initializing the system, generating and verifying signatures, registering, logging in and authenticating, and changing the password. Two of the most essential features of the proposed framework are the generation of a dynamic session key and the facilitation of mutual authentication between the gateway node, the distant user, and the sensor node. Both of these features are essential for the operation of the framework. According to the findings of our study, the proposed method is successful against a wide variety of different types of attacks, while simultaneously keeping the promises of safe mutual authentication, complete anonymity, and perfect forward secrecy. We provided evidence to show that the level of security provided by our proposed solution is superior to the level of security provided by the standard that is already in place.

Binary Classification of Medical Chest X-Ray Using Gaussian Naive Bayes in Machine Learning

S. Shanthi,65

E-mail: sshanthi4961@gmail.com, manimayur@gmail.com, dr.murugan.m@gmail.com

DOI: 10.1201/9781003430452-80

Abstract

Artificial Intelligence plays a major role in computer field as it handles large amount of data and prediction is faster and more accurate. Machine learning techniques and deep learning techniques are branches of artificial intelligence with deep learning as a subfamily of Machine learning. Machine learning techniques and deep learning help in the extraction of data to promote the biomedical field (Tiwari et al., 2018). Machine learning became popular and accomplished much better on unstructured data (Abound & Akpan, 2021). As the data increases enormously, the popularity of Machine learning grows. With rapid growth in medical data, classification of medical images plays a vital role in clinical care. The objective of classification is to find the target class (Perez-Careta et al., 2022). The target class should be accurate. Conventional method is time-consuming and need extra endeavor to find the target class.

Keywords: Naive Bayes, Gaussian Naive Bayes, Wiener Filter

Introduction

Machine learning learns patterns from the past to automate the model and predict the output. Machine learning become a widely used approach as it produces a more prominent result in complex tasks than human performance (Janiesch et al., 2021; Alzubaidi et al., 2021). The main goal of Machine learning is to build a model to perform various tasks like object classification, and detection. Handling large amount of complex data and amazing improvement in hardware engineering (ex: High Performance computing technology) increases the popularity of learning. Lung and Lung classification for disease prediction is an important topic for research in recent times The size of the medical image datasets also increases as it is used in hospitals, diagnostic centres etc. Yadav & Jadhav (2019) analysis x-ray for determining pneumonia, with that of the healthy person. This analysis is needed, as determining the affected person with pneumonia is expensive and need a radiologist proficient. To overcome this cumbersome task of classification, this research is about the Gaussian Naive Bayes Algorithm and the chest image processing analysis.

Related Works

Naive Bayes classifier is used and uses median filter to filter the noise in X-ray images (Bustomi et al., 2018). Classification of image classification is based on the Soft set. Soft set classifier is carried by mean values of the quantities of the classes and classification is carried out by labeling the unknown data (Lashari & Ibrahim, 2013). KNN classification and feature extraction is carried out for the medical classification. Classification on Small-class and imbalanced image data is performed using deep KNN (Zhuang et al., 2020). Ultrasound images are analyzed using various algorithms and show that the Support vector outperforms the other algorithms (Naziya & Jadhav, 2019). Image classification is executed by Bag of Features approach which focuses on vector representation. This is done by Support vector machine and by KNN and their accuracy are calculated. This representation is used find the class of the image (Loussaief & Abdelkrim, 2018). The aim is to find the infected and not infected tuberculosis patient by SVM classifier data. The performance result is 94.7% (Yahyaoui et al., 2017). Lung disease classification is accomplished using very less datasets of images (Krzhizhanovskaya et al., 2020). In Abu et al, (2019) tensor flow framework is used for the classification of various flower images. Using deep neural network, the images are classified and the accuracy obtained is 90%. Yu Zeng et al. carries out random forest and decision tree algorithm and show the noise is reduced. The paper aims on the various input features that is used in medical data. The accuracy obtained from this algorithm is 86% (Zeng & Cheng, 2021). Multivariate Bernoulli Naive Bayes is compared with Multinomial Naive Bayes to categorize of sentiment analysis for a less dataset. Singh et al, (2019)gives a comparison between these two algorithms and suggests that Bernoulli Naive Bayes algorithm gives a better result.

The Probability X happens after event Y has occurred already. is the probability of occurrence of both A and B. Bayes classifier states that

(2)
$$\text{P}\left\lbrack \frac{\text{V}}{\text{U}_{\text{i}}} \right\rbrack = \text{P}\left\lbrack \frac{\text{v}_{1}}{\text{U}_{\text{j}}} \right\rbrack \ast \text{P}\left\lbrack \frac{\text{v}_{2}}{\text{U}_{\text{j}}} \right\rbrack \ast .. \ast \cdot \text{P}\left\lbrack \frac{\text{V}_{n}}{\text{Uj}_{\text{j}}} \right\rbrack$$

$P\left\lbrack \frac{Vj}{Ui} \right\rbrack - >$ Posterior probability of the hypothesis is true.

$P\left\lbrack \frac{Ui}{Vj} \right\rbrack - >$ Likelihood probability of hypothesis is true

P [Vj] -> Class Prior probability of the hypothesis

P[Ui]-> Evidence probability is true. Naive Bayes classifier presume the independent features

(3)
$$\text{P}\left\lbrack \frac{\text{V}}{\text{U}_{\text{i}}} \right\rbrack = \text{P}\left\lbrack \frac{\text{V}_{1}}{\text{U}_{\text{j}}} \right\rbrack \ast \text{P}\left\lbrack \frac{\text{V}_{2}}{\text{U}_{\text{j}}} \right\rbrack \ast .. \ast \cdot \text{P}\left\lbrack \frac{\text{V}_{1}}{\text{U}_{\text{n}}} \right\rbrack$$

$P\left\lbrack \frac{V}{U_{1}} \right\rbrack - >$ The class Ui generating the instance V

$P\left\lbrack \frac{V1}{Uj} \right\rbrack - >$ The probability of class Uj generating the observed value for feature1,

$P\left\lbrack \frac{V2}{Uj} \right\rbrack - >$ The probability of class Uj generating the observed value for feature2,

$P\left\lbrack \frac{Vn}{Uj} \right\rbrack - >$ The probability of class Uj generating the observed value for feature n.

  1. Bernoulli Naive Bayes Classifier: Bernoulli Naive Bayes works well with discrete data and it is based on Bernoulli distribution (Ismail et al., 2016). When the predictor is binary then Bernoulli Naive Bayes classifier is used.

    The Bernoulli Naive Bayes decision rule is given by


    P(Xk ∣ Y) = P(k ∣ Y)Xk + (1 − P(k ∣ Y))(1 − Xk)

  2. Gaussian Naive Bayes

The best way to handle continuous data is the Gaussian Naive Bayes (Kamel et al., 2019). Naive Bayes is used when the data is discrete. Naive Bayes is a generative model and Gaussian Naive Bayes follows the Gaussian distribution (Normal Distribution). Gaussian distribution is widely used in statistical analysis and in machine learning. Gaussian distribution is a continuous probability distribution function (Shen & Fang, 2020).

The probability density function likelihood of the data is assumed to be

(5)
$$P\left\lbrack \frac{Xi}{Y = k} \right\rbrack = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2\pi\sigma\text{k}^{2}}}e^{({- \frac{xi - \mu\text{k}}{2\sigma\text{k}^{2}}})}$$

Where

  • Xi is the continuous variable
  • Y = k is class k of Y.
  • σ is the variance of the variable X
  • p is defined as mean of the variable Xi for Y

Gaussian Naive Bayes Algorithm:

Input: A set of Medical chest X-ray

Output: Classified data and finding the accuracy

  1. Step 1 Collecting the dataset
  2. Step 2 Collected data is pre-processed. The image may contain noise which should be removed before the classification
  3. Step 2.1 The noise is removed by the Wiener filter method
  4. Step 3 GNBM is created using python
  5. Step 4 Split the dataset into training and testing data. Training data is 70% and testing data is 30%
  6. Step 5 Testing the data and predicting the class. Examine the training data of the GNBA and predict the class.
  7. Step 6 Assess the performance metrics of the data and store the data

Implementation

Step 1: Medical data acquisition

Materials: Data is obtained from an Adapted version of Paul Mooney’s Chest X-Ray Images (Pneumonia) dataset.

Step 2: Processing: The first step in image classification is processing (Arya & Semwal, 2017) the image may contain noise that should be removed before the classification. Poisson noise, white noise, Gaussian noise, etc. are some of the noise that may be present in an image. To remove this noise, filters are used. Three types of filters are

  1. Wiener filter or linear filter
  2. Averaging filter or Mean filter
  3. Median filter

Step 2.1: i) Averaging filter: Averaging filter (Shetti & Patil, 2017) replaces each pixel element with the average of the pixel elements. This filter is simple and smoothes images by decreasing the intensity between two pixels. This is often used to reduce noise.

ii) Median Filter or Non-Linear Filter: It removes noise by preserving the edges. Each pixel element is replaced by the median of the intensity of the pixel element within the region.

Merits: Sharp details are retained. sensitivity to the outliers is less than the average filter. Effectively removes the outliers.

Demerits: Does not remove all kinds of noise

(iii) Wiener filter: It is a type 0 linear filter. The Wiener filter adopts to the image deviation. If the variance is small, wiener accomplish a very good smoothing and if the variance is large then it accomplishes it very less smoothing. It renders a better solution for determining computation difficulty in stationary signals. It provides a very good outcome in noise removal form the chest x-ray images. Comparing Median filters and Averaging filters, Wiener filters provides a very good result for filtering noise from chest X-ray.

In this paper, we use Wiener Filter (Fig. 3) to filter out noise

Step 3: Examining the data set of normal and pneumonia chest x-ray (Fig. 4)

Step 4: Total x-ray chest data is 387 and the total observations is 387 data. Training data set is 270 and testing data set is 117

Step 5: For predicting the class, import the Gaussian Naive Bayes. Fit the model by passing the training and testing data.

Step 6: Performance Metrics and Result:

The performance metrics are accuracy, Precision, and Recall. These metrics are calculated from the confusion matrix classification of the class. This shows how Gaussian Naive Bayes from sklearn predicts the class using the test data.

Accuracy: Accuracy value is given as total number of True positive values obtained plus the True Negative value obtained divided by total samples obtained.

(6)
$$\text{Accuracy} = \frac{\text{TPV} + \text{TNV}}{\text{TPV} + \text{FPV} + \text{TNV} + \text{FNV}}$$

The accuracy by using Gaussian Naive Bayes Algorithm is 96.90.

Precision: Precision is defined as the total positive values obtained divided by the total positive values obtained (True Positive + False Positive)

(7)
$$\text{Precision} = \frac{TPV}{TPV + FPV}$$

The precision shows well with 96.1 than the Naive Bayes Classifier and Bernoulli Naive Bayes.

Recall or sensitivity: Recall is positive prediction divided by the total samples in the prediction.

(8)
$$\text{Sensivity} = \frac{\text{True~Positive}}{\text{True~Positive} + \text{False~Negative}}$$

Table 1. Comparison of Algorithms with Performance Metrics
Performance Proposed Algorithm -Gaussian Naive Bayes Algorithm Naive Bayes Classifier Bernoulli Naive Bayes
Accuracy 96.90 85.1 94
Precision 96.1 77.62 92.6
Recall or Sensitivity 98.0 79.28 88.7

Conclusion

This idea is based on machine learning techniques for classifying medical health images. To classify the medical images, the proposed classification works efficiently. For the classification of Chest X-ray Gaussian Naive Bayes algorithm is used. Wiener filter method is applied to remove the noise and the GNBA model is implemented for Binary classification of Normal and Pneumonia chest data. The algorithm is simple and shows better performance metrics than the other algorithms.
